The one certainty is that Vincent Kompany will not be in the dugout. There is a version of this fixture that arrives every autumn as a formality, Bayern a dozen points clear and Dortmund playing for third. This is not that version. After seven matchdays the two clubs are identical on the only line that matters: played seven, won five, drawn two, lost none, seventeen points. They are the only unbeaten teams left in Germany. Saturday at the Allianz Arena is first against second in the literal sense. What separates them is style, and the gap there is enormous. Bayern have scored 25 goals, more than anyone in the division and five more than the next best. Dortmund have scored 12, a total that eight other clubs have bettered, and have conceded four. Four, in seven games. Nobody in Germany has conceded fewer, and only Bayern, on six, are anywhere near. So the match has an unusually clean shape to it. Bayern are a team that overwhelms; Dortmund are a team that refuses. One of those propositions is going to look foolish by Saturday evening. The absence that frames everything Bayern's week has not been about football. On Friday 23 October, Vincent Kompany collapsed while watching the club's second team train and was taken to hospital. He had been unwell for some time, carrying a viral infection that affected his legs, sitting through the 6-1 league win over RB Leipzig on 17 October and missing training and a press conference in the days before. He was discharged on Wednesday 28 October. Sporting director Max Eberl told ARD that the diagnosis was an irritation of the meninges, the membranes around the brain and spinal cord, and that it had caused the collapse. Eberl was careful to separate it from the job. "This is a condition that could strike any one of us," he said. "This has nothing to do with the pressure associated with the Bundesliga." Kompany will not be at the Klassiker. He is not on the bench and, by the club's account, is being kept away from football conversations entirely. Assistant Aaron Danks takes the team, as he did for the 3-1 win at Freiburg and the 6-1 cup win over Magdeburg. Danks has been pointedly undramatic about it. "No big changes, no big differences for us," he said on Friday. "We want the players to go out and show who they are." Kane, Guirassy and the two theories of attack Monday night in London, Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or. He beat Kylian Mbappe into second and Lamine Yamal into third, and he mentioned Kompany from the stage. Kompany had phoned him that morning to wish him luck. Kane has four league goals this season, fewer than you might expect from a Ballon d'Or winner, because Bayern's goals are spread everywhere: Michael Olise has six, Luis Diaz four, and the 3-1 at Freiburg included Serge Gnabry 's 100th Bundesliga goal and an Olise winner in stoppage time. Dortmund's attack is one man and a prayer. Serhou Guirassy has seven goals in all competitions, and Bundesliga's own preview has framed Saturday as Kane against Guirassy. The supporting evidence is thinner. Against Eintracht Frankfurt last Saturday, Dortmund took 18 shots, Guirassy missed two clear chances, and the game was settled on 80 minutes by Maximilian Beier off a Jobe Bellingham pass. Three days later, 2-0 up on Werder Bremen in the cup, they were pegged back to 2-2 by a Niclas Fullkrug brace and rescued by a Marcel Sabitzer free kick in stoppage time. That is the Dortmund pattern under Niko Kovac , whose contract was extended to June 2029 earlier this month, two years ahead of schedule. They do not score early and they do not concede. They win late. It is not thrilling and it has them level with Bayern. Bayern are the pinnacle not only in Germany but in Europe. There is no team in the world that dominates the opponent for 90 minutes. Niko Kovac, Borussia Dortmund head coach, speaking to dpa on 29 October Who is missing Bayern are without Manuel Neuer , whose foot injury is still painful enough that Danks ruled him out on Friday, leaving Jonas Urbig in goal. Jamal Musiala has not returned to full training since the September international break. Luis Diaz is out too. Joshua Kimmich has resumed individual training following the death of his father and may feature. "Life is different for him now and we don't need to hide that," Eberl said. Dortmund are missing Emre Can and Giannis Konstantelias , both with knee problems. Konstantinos Karetsas , injured at Union Berlin in mid October, trained partly with the squad on Thursday and will be assessed. Kovac said the side that played the last match is otherwise fit. The weight of recent history Dortmund have not beaten Bayern since March 2024. Club adviser Matthias Sammer was asked about Saturday and gave an answer that sounded less like a prediction than a confession: Bayern alone, he told Sky, will decide whether they win this game. It drew criticism in Germany as defeatism from a man who used to embody the opposite. There is a counter-argument, and it is sitting in the Bayern treatment room. A side missing its goalkeeper, its most creative attacker and its manager is a side playing on structure and habit. Dortmund's entire season has been built on being the team that is still standing at minute 85. If they are ever going to end the run, a week like this one is the week. Milan and Inter meet with the title race already strange The Derby della Madonnina lands on Saturday night with Inter joint top but short of bodies, Milan beaten at home for the first time, and Lazio refusing to go away. Serie A has produced the most unusual table in Europe. Inter and Lazio are tied on 25 points from nine games with identical goal differences of plus 15. Roma are third on 21, also plus 15, and have not lost. Como , under Cesc Fabregas, are fourth on 20. Napoli and Juventus are seventh and eighth on 14. The two leading scorers in the division play for Frosinone and Monza. Into that, Saturday at 12:45pm Pacific, comes the derby. AC Milan arrive off their first league defeat of the season, 4-2 at home to Bologna on Wednesday, in which Samuel Mbangula scored a hat-trick and Fikayo Tomori went off injured at the start of the second half. Milan conceded twice within two minutes of losing him. Tomori has a hamstring lesion and manager Ruben Amorim said on Friday he is out for at least a month. Inter's problem is sharper. Lautaro Martinez has a left hamstring injury and will not play again until after the November international break. John Stones , Benjamin Pavard , Curtis Jones and Luis Henrique are also out. "I am limited by injuries and some need to rest occasionally," Cristian Chivu said on Friday. "I have few of them." Chivu also offered the derby's standard disclaimer, and meant it more than most managers do: the table does not count, nothing counts, there are no favourites in derbies. Amorim's counter was that at Milan you always have to talk about the Scudetto as the objective. Both men are partly right, which is the point of a derby in the tenth round of a title race nobody can yet read. Transfer News Bayern say the Kane deal is all but done, and only the lawyers are left The Ballon d'Or winner's contract expires at the end of this season. Bayern's chief executive says the hard part was settled before the ceremony. The most consequential piece of contract business in European football is being conducted almost in public. Harry Kane 's Bayern deal runs out at the end of 2026-27. On Wednesday 28 October, after the 6-1 cup win over Magdeburg, chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen spoke to Kicker in terms that left very little room. "We had already discussed and negotiated all the important issues before the Ballon d'Or ceremony," Dreesen said. The remaining work is detail, which "simply takes a few days." And then the line that matters: "But we both know that we want to extend this arrangement for as long as possible." Dreesen described repeated conversations with Kane's father and brother. Certainty: personal terms agreed in substance, not signed and not announced. Nothing has been filed and Bayern have made no formal statement. Dreesen is the club's chief executive speaking on the record to Germany's most authoritative football title, which is about as strong as an unannounced deal gets, but it is not an announcement. The timing is not accidental. Kane won the Ballon d'Or in London on Monday 26 October, ahead of Mbappe and Lamine Yamal, and also took the Gerd Muller award. A player who has just been named the best in the world and whose contract expires in eight months is, in theory, the most available footballer alive. Bayern appear to have closed that window before it opened. Milan tie down Pulisic and open a January list A renewal to 2031 confirmed on Friday, and an owner saying out loud that the summer window left the squad short. AC Milan announced on Friday 30 October that Christian Pulisic has extended his contract to 30 June 2031. The club cited 44 goals in 141 appearances since July 2023 and framed the renewal as confirming a shared path. Tuttomercatoweb 's Simone Lorini had the financial terms in advance, reporting a salary of 6.5 million euros net per season, a figure that does not appear in the club statement. Certainty: OFFICIAL. Announced by the club and carried by the ANSA wire. The renewal landed the same day Gerry Cardinale , whose RedBird Capital owns the club, gave a long interview conceding that the summer had fallen short. "We have to keep improving the squad because in the summer I did not manage to do everything I wanted," he said, promising high-level reinforcements in January. The names being worked on, per Tuttomercatoweb and Gazzetta dello Sport , are mostly defenders, which is what you would expect from a club that just lost its best centre-back for a month. Goncalo Inacio of Sporting is described as the front-runner. Tiago Gabriel at Lecce is a longer-standing target. Kim Min-jae is said to be open to a Serie A return from Bayern. Further forward, Endrick is considered a possible loan from Real Madrid, with Roma also interested. Alex Scott of Bournemouth is on the list but a reported 100 million euro valuation makes January unrealistic. Certainty: concrete interest, no bids reported. Cardinale's quote is on the record; the target list is reporting, not confirmation. Milan also published their 2025-26 accounts on Thursday: revenue of 464.6 million euros, a net loss of around 24 million, sponsorship above 100 million, and average attendance over 72,000 despite a season with no European football. Chairman Paolo Scaroni called the figures evidence of "the resilience of our business model in a challenging season." Dortmund have a renewal queue, and Guirassy is not at the front of it Four key players are out of contract in 2028. Bild's BVB correspondent has laid out the order, and it says something about how the club values its only reliable scorer. Four of Borussia Dortmund 's most important players run out of contract in summer 2028: goalkeeper Gregor Kobel , full-back Julian Ryerson , centre-back Waldemar Anton and striker Serhou Guirassy . On Friday, Bild 's Dortmund correspondent Sebastian Wessling set out the club's priority order on the paper's "Dortmund Insider" podcast. Anton is first, with talks already under way. Kobel is second, and the club would ideally like him signed this calendar year. Ryerson follows. Guirassy is last, and talks are not expected to start before spring 2027. Wessling's phrasing was that Guirassy "is not quite at the front of the queue," which for a player with seven goals and two assists this season is a pointed piece of information. Certainty: advanced talks for Anton, stated intent for Kobel, deliberate deferral for Guirassy. Sky Germany first reported the Anton negotiations on 8 October. Manchester United have been linked with Anton, which is at the rumour tier and has no reported bid behind it. Elsewhere in Germany, Borussia Monchengladbach are negotiating an extension beyond 2028 for Wael Mohya , the 17-year-old who scored and assisted in last Friday's 3-2 win at Stuttgart, the club's first win of the season. Sky Germany reports the new terms would roughly double his salary to around 2 million euros a year. Head of sport Rouven Schroder was unrestrained: "The way he dribbles forward, the audacity with which he sets up the goal. Hats off." Certainty: advanced talks. Napoli need a midfielder, and Schira says they want a Monza forward Stanislav Lobotka's injury has reshaped Napoli's January, and their main attacking target is sitting in the relegation zone. Napoli lost Stanislav Lobotka to a joint and ligament injury in Wednesday's 4-1 win at Monza. Corriere dello Sport puts him out for roughly six weeks, back in December, missing Juventus on Sunday, Porto in the Champions League and Lazio. The paper expects Kevin De Bruyne to drop into the deep playmaking role alongside Gilmour and Anguissa. Tuttosport gives a slightly longer estimate of five to seven weeks. The knock-on is a January window that now needs a midfielder as well as a forward. Nicolo Schira reported on Friday that Napoli are "ready to pounce" for Gustavo Varela of Monza , calling him their main target for January. Varela has eight goals, joint top of Serie A alongside Frosinone's Antonio Raimondo. Schira set out two scenarios: sign him now and leave him at Monza until June, or bring him in immediately. The conditions are that Napoli move players out, find a loan for Lucca, and that Monza's league position does not harden into a relegation fight. Monza are 16th. Certainty: concrete interest, named reporter, no bid. A separate Portuguese report claims an offer is ready and that Benfica hold a sell-on percentage; that is single-sourced and should be treated as unconfirmed. Il Mattino reports Napoli plan three January signings, one per department, with the forward as cover for Hojlund. The specifics vary between outlets and are low confidence. The Rumour Mill Everything still simmering, with the certainty on each one labelled. The window does not open for two months, which is exactly when the groundwork gets done. Antonio Conte and the English question. The most interesting line of the week came from Nicolo Schira on Thursday. Conte, he reported, is in Sharm el-Sheikh fielding calls and appears inclined to wait until next season before taking a Serie A job. But, Schira wrote, "it is a different conversation for an English club (Manchester United), where it would take less time to rebuild." Conte himself said on Instagram that there are no negotiations at an advanced stage. With Michael Carrick's position at Old Trafford confirmed only as far as Saturday, that is a thread worth watching. Rumour, well sourced. Jacobo Ramon back to Real Madrid. Matteo Moretto , speaking on DAZN Espana on Thursday, said Real Madrid will execute the buyback clause on Jacobo Ramon , the academy-raised centre-back now at Como, for under 9 million euros. Timing and role are not settled. Ramon scored against Manchester United in the Champions League nine days ago. Concrete, stated club intent. Haaland and Spain. Moretto again, on Marca's programme this week: Erling Haaland "dreams of playing in LaLiga and is expected to end up in Spain sooner or later." No club named. His Manchester City contract runs to June 2034. Rumour and mood music, nothing more. Igor Paixao wants out of Marseille. Mohamed Toubache-Ter reports that the Brazilian winger wants a January move and that his representatives have reopened talks with Sunderland . He nearly left in the summer before Bruno Genesio insisted he stay and owner Frank McCourt pulled back. No bid or fee reported. Concrete interest, single-sourced. The same report has Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg wanting to leave with no suitor named, which is weaker still. Atletico's striker hunt. Atletico Madrid are reported to want another forward in January, with Victor Osimhen of Galatasaray the name attached and a figure around 70 million euros mooted. No originating reporter is cited and Galatasaray are described as reluctant. Separately, Lisandro Martinez of Manchester United is linked, his contract running to June 2027 and therefore open to foreign negotiation from January. Both rumour tier, aggregator-sourced. Treat accordingly. Kvaratskhelia's new deal. RMC Sport's Fabrice Hawkins reports Paris Saint-Germain are in talks over a new five-year contract for Khvicha Kvaratskhelia , who ruptured an anterior cruciate ligament in the 4-2 win over Barcelona on 20 October and faces surgery. PSG also want to extend 19-year-old Quentin Ndjantou and hand a first professional deal to 17-year-old David Boly . Advanced talks. A contradiction worth flagging. On 28 October Foot Mercato reported PSG's interest in Leverkusen's Ibrahim Maza was firming up. On 29 October RMC Sport reported PSG will not pursue him this winter, while remaining open to a January signing at a sensible price. Two reputable French outlets, one day apart, in direct opposition. Unresolved. Frankfurt's boardroom. Eintracht Frankfurt have been without a sporting director since Markus Krosche's departure on 18 October. Florian Plettenberg reports the shortlist is down to two: Joti Chatzialexiou of Nurnberg and Marcel Schafer , RB Leipzig's managing director for sport. Hessischer Rundfunk says Chatzialexiou leads. Nurnberg said as of Wednesday they had received no approach. Advanced talks, no formal approach confirmed. And one to discount. Around the Leagues Premier League A title race that has barely moved, a Manchester United collapse that keeps moving, and a weekend that could reshape both. Matchweek nine broke the pattern at the top. Aston Villa beat Manchester City 2-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, City's second defeat of the season and enough to drop them from first to second. Liverpool beat Brighton 2-0 at Anfield to move third on 18 points, their best run of the Andoni Iraola era, which is a sentence that would have read strangely in May. Brighton remain the league's most entertaining proposition: 23 goals scored, more than anyone, and a goal difference of plus 14 that is the best in the division despite sitting fourth. Below that, the table is compressed to the point of absurdity. Seven clubs sit between 11 and 12 points. Brentford have drawn six of nine. Leeds United have also drawn six of nine, including a goalless Sunday at Sunderland that did neither club much good. Tottenham won 2-0 at Chelsea , a result that says as much about Xabi Alonso's first months at Stamford Bridge as about Spurs: Chelsea have scored 17 and conceded 17 in nine games and are seventh. Old Trafford, nine games in The hard numbers first. Manchester United have taken seven points from nine Premier League games. One win, four draws, four defeats. They are 17th, above Crystal Palace only on goal difference, and below Nottingham Forest. The single league win was 5-2 against Ipswich on 30 August, two months ago. Sunday's 0-3 home defeat to Bournemouth came four days after a 4-1 loss at Como in the Champions League, after which Michael Carrick opened his press conference by apologising to the supporters and called the performance unacceptable. United are also out of the Carabao Cup, beaten 3-2 at home by Brighton in September, and have lost two of three in Europe. Wayne Rooney said this week that the club are "a million miles away." Gary Neville said he was surprised, and pleased, that Carrick is staying. Reports describe clear-the-air talks between Carrick and Bruno Fernandes , after the captain's post-Como comments about the pressing instructions drew a public correction from his manager. What the club has not done is say anything about Carrick beyond confirming he takes the team to Chelsea on Saturday. That is a specific and limited form of backing. The winner was Mbappe's 100th goal for Real Madrid, and it came from a Jude Bellingham turn and a Camavinga pass. It was Jose Mourinho 's first Clasico win since returning to the club in June. The Mbappe affair On Monday a clip filmed in April circulated in which Mbappe, asked about the funniest meme he had seen of himself, described it as putting his face on "some guy, I think he's a Chinese dictator." He did not name Mao Zedong. The reaction was immediate and severe. Dongpeng Beverage terminated his contract with immediate effect, saying it "firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments." Mengniu, China's largest dairy company, also cut ties. Xiaohongshu froze his account. Weibo barred new follows. State television halted broadcasts of LaLiga matches and of events involving Mbappe. Mbappe apologised on Tuesday in French, Mandarin and English: "My comment was ill-judged and I now understand that it hurt many people in China." LaLiga apologised the same day, president Javier Tebas meeting China's ambassador to Spain and saying "China is and will continue to be a strategic partner for LaLiga." Real Madrid issued their own apology on Wednesday. On Wednesday foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said Beijing takes the apology seriously. Roughly 45 percent of LaLiga's television income comes from abroad, which is the commercial context for how fast everyone moved. Bundesliga Beyond the Klassiker: a cup round that removed seven top-flight clubs, a 250 million euro investment in Bayern, and the slow reopening of the 50+1 question. The DFB-Pokal second round on 27 and 28 October was carnage for the top division. Stuttgart lost 1-0 at Paderborn. Schalke lost 2-0 at Dynamo Dresden. Hoffenheim went out on penalties at Holstein Kiel. Hamburg, Union Berlin, Werder Bremen and Elversberg fell too, seven top-flight clubs in all. 1. FC Koln hammered Union 5-0, with 20-year-old Said El Mala scoring twice and setting up another. The round-of-16 ties are on 1 and 2 December. The weekend before, Niclas Fullkrug scored twice from the spot in Werder's 3-2 win at Mainz and now has eight league goals in seven games, the division's leading scorer and a tally only Rudi Voller has matched for Bremen at this stage. Hoffenheim beat Bayer Leverkusen 3-0 to end a Leverkusen winning run that stretched across all competitions, the winning penalty coming after a VAR review and 35-year-old Andrej Kramaric scoring the club's 1,000th Bundesliga goal before being sent off for removing his shirt in celebration. Off the pitch, Bayern confirmed an investment from the Viessmann Generations Group reported at around 250 million euros, structured as a capital increase rather than a share sale. Viessmann will hold just under 6.7 percent; the members' association drops from 75 to its statutory floor of 70 percent, with Adidas, Audi and Allianz each diluted to just under 7.8. Separately, the Bundesliga executive committee set a timetable on the 50+1 ownership rule: a December membership vote to reaffirm it as a principle, then final proposals on uniform application in the first half of 2027. The federal competition authority closed its own examination in August without fundamental objection, but required consistent application. RB Leipzig remain the league's strangest team, perfect at home in the Bundesliga and the Champions League and beaten in every away game in both. Martin Demichelis is still in post, backed by a hierarchy whose managing director for sport is himself on Frankfurt's shortlist. Serie A A midweek round, a Lazio demolition, a two-match ban for Allegri, a manager under siege in Turin, and a new San Siro with a name. Serie A played a full midweek round from Tuesday to Thursday. The headline was Lazio 's 6-2 at Sassuolo: four goals inside the opening quarter of an hour, two Lazio penalties missed, a Sassuolo red card on 31 minutes, and a first Serie A goal for Romano Floriani Mussolini . Gennaro Gattuso 's response was characteristic: "We must not look at the table, otherwise we will get a headache." Juventus lost 2-0 at Genoa on Wednesday, beaten by Daniele De Rossi , who then embraced his mentor Luciano Spalletti at the whistle. Corriere dello Sport reports the club is backing Spalletti for now, with a direct meeting between chief executive and squad and a two-day training camp before Napoli on Sunday, while naming Stefano Pioli as the leading alternative. Juventus are eighth on 14 points with a goal difference of plus one. Sunday at 11:45am Pacific is being framed in Italy as decisive. The other Turin storm is Neapolitan. Massimiliano Allegri was sent off late in Napoli's 3-3 draw with Roma on 24 October and, walking to his press conference, was heard accusing Roma of having been handed the Champions League place last season at Milan's expense. Roma's Gian Piero Gasperini called the remark unfortunate and declined to add anything. The disciplinary judge handed Allegri a two-match ban and a 10,000 euro fine, citing protests to the fourth official, remarks in the dressing room and an aggressive attitude towards a Roma executive. Napoli announced an appeal and then dropped it. Allegri misses Sunday at Juventus. On Thursday, Inter and Milan unveiled the replacement for the San Siro: the Generali Stadium, around 71,500 seats, a continuous two-tier bowl with curva inclines of up to 37 degrees, designed by Foster and Partners with MANICA. Construction is scheduled from 2028 with a first match targeted for 2031-32, subject to approvals, at the centre of a 281,000 square metre regeneration. Naming rights run from day one. x: The Weekly Soccer Digest World football, reported in full Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Arsenal is covered in the companion Arsenal edition In this edition The Lead · Transfer News · The Rumour Mill · Around the Leagues · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch If you read nothing else Harry Kane won the 2026 Ballon d'Or in London on Monday, the first English winner of the award since Michael Owen in 2001. Real Madrid won 2-1 at Barcelona on Sunday through two Kylian Mbappe goals, ending Barcelona's nine-game winning start to La Liga. Manchester United are 16th and winless in eight, and were kept with Michael Carrick only because no successor has been agreed. The Lead Kane's Crown, and the Klassiker That Follows Harry Kane collected the Ballon d'Or at the Palladium Theatre on Monday night. On Saturday he walks into the Allianz Arena for a first-against-second Klassiker, with Bayern Munich 's head coach in hospital, their best creator in a brace and Borussia Dortmund carrying the meanest defence in Germany. The Lead · Munich The two facts sit oddly together. On Monday night in London, Harry Kane became the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d'Or , an award built on the 73 goals in 65 games he scored for club and country across 2025-26. On Wednesday morning in Munich, the official Bayern Munich line on his head coach was that a diagnosis is still pending. Somewhere between those two sentences is the strangest week this club has had in years, and at the end of it comes Borussia Dortmund . Start with the collapse, because everything else at Bayern is downstream of it. On Friday Vincent Kompany was watching the second team train when he went down. He was taken to hospital and kept there. Sporting director Max Eberl said his condition was stable and the headaches had stopped, but that doctors had not finished their work. Sport Bild reports heart attack and stroke ruled out, with the medical focus on a head problem. Assistant Aaron Danks took the team to Freiburg the next day and won 3-1. Kompany is not expected on the bench on Saturday. What Bayern did in the 48 hours after that is why they are still top. At Freiburg they played without Luis Diaz (a muscle tear from the Arsenal draw), Jamal Musiala , Manuel Neuer , Aleksandar Pavlovic , and captain Joshua Kimmich , who is away from the squad after the death of his father. Dayot Upamecano headed in a Michael Olise cross, Serge Gnabry scored his 100th Bundesliga goal in his first league start of the season, and Olise finished it in stoppage time. Bayern's own numbers put them at 2.99 expected goals to 1.05. Eberl was unusually candid afterwards. "I don't think we really understand what we've achieved this week," he said. "The win means three points, but it was a bigger win than just three points." Danks , asked about his absent manager's message to the squad, reported it verbatim: "Brilliant. Now get some rest." Bayern are 22 Bundesliga games unbeaten and lead the division for goals, shots, possession and distance covered. Not burning yourself out in those circumstances is a special skill. Lars Ricken , Borussia Dortmund sporting managing director, on the demands on a head coach, via Get German Football News The most generous words of the week came from the opposition boardroom. Borussia Dortmund 's sporting managing director Lars Ricken wished Kompany "all the best and a speedy recovery" and then talked about the job itself: the match every three days, the 200-plus press conferences a season that Niko Kovac gets through. Chief executive Carsten Cramer went further. "I thought the way FC Bayern handled the situation was exemplary," he said, before noting that a head coach has at least ten difficult conversations with non-starters before every match. It is not often that Klassiker week opens with the two clubs agreeing about anything. On the pitch this is the league's best attack against its best defence, and the gap in style is enormous. Dortmund have conceded four goals in seven games, kept five clean sheets, and allowed the lowest expected goals and only three clear-cut chances in the division. Kovac has them unbeaten away from home, and they arrive on the back of a 1-0 win over Eintracht Frankfurt and a DFB-Pokal night that showed both sides of them. That cup tie is the one piece of evidence that Dortmund can be got at. They led Werder Bremen 2-0 inside 17 minutes through Serhou Guirassy and Carney Chukwuemeka , then Niclas Fullkrug came off the bench and scored twice in about three minutes. Marcel Sabitzer rescued it with a free kick at 90+3, and only because Kovac overruled his own defenders from the touchline. "I then shouted from the sideline, 'Sabi, please shoot!'" he told ZDF. "Because I know what kind of shot he has." Which brings it back to Kane , and a small statistical joke. The man who just won the Ballon d'Or has four Bundesliga goals this season and sits behind Fullkrug , Olise , Patrik Schick and others in his own league's scoring chart. Against Dortmund , though, his record is 10 goals in 11 games, and Dortmund have won three of the last 23 meetings in all competitions and only once at the Allianz Arena in the Bundesliga since 2013-14. NBC Sports , which has the game in the United States, still went for 1-1, on the grounds that neither side has kept a Bundesliga clean sheet in four matches. The stakes are simpler than the Bundesliga usually allows. Both clubs are on 17 points from seven games, with Bayern ahead only on goal difference. The winner goes clear; a draw leaves them locked together and leaves the rest of Germany where it has been for most of this decade. Fernando Carro of Bayer Leverkusen made that point this week in response to the news that the Viessmann Generations Group had bought about 6.7 per cent of FC Bayern Munchen AG for 250 million euros. "No, the next titles are not cemented," Carro said, which is the kind of denial that tells you what everyone is thinking. A Stay of Execution at Old Trafford Manchester United are 16th, winless in eight and were beaten 3-0 at home by Bournemouth with their captain dropped. Michael Carrick kept his job on Monday for one reason: the club has not settled on who replaces him. The sequence is now familiar enough to be a genre. On Wednesday Manchester United lost 4-1 at Como in the Champions League, in a 10,000-seat stadium, to a club playing its first European campaign at this level. On Thursday their captain gave an interview to Sky Sport Italia. On Sunday they lost 3-0 at home to Bournemouth , with that captain sitting on the bench for 90 minutes. On Monday the executives met and decided to keep the manager anyway. Bruno Fernandes said this, among other things, to Sky Sport Italia's Pierluigi Bagnulo : "At this club, we focus too much on what was achieved in the past, but we are no longer the same." And, on the run itself: "Unfortunately, it's one of those moments where it seems like we can't get out of it." Gary Neville on Sky Sports called it "a direct attack on the manager." Carrick left him out against Bournemouth and gave no public reason. What followed was one of the bleaker afternoons Old Trafford has staged. Rayan scored at the far post from a Justin Kluivert free kick on 38 minutes, Marcus Tavernier added a second on 43 after a Leny Yoro slip, and Evanilson beat Senne Lammens to the ball on 71. The Stretford End turned its anger on the Glazer family, Sir Jim Ratcliffe and director of football Jason Wilcox , then sang Carrick 's name as he walked off. Marco Rose , whose Bournemouth side have won four in a row, said simply: "We were just Bournemouth today." Opta records seven points from eight games as United's worst start to a league season since 1986-87. They have also suffered seven home defeats by three goals or more in all competitions since 2023-24, more than any other Premier League club. The decision not to sack him was a decision about the replacement rather than the incumbent. Chief executive Omar Berrada and Wilcox met at Carrington on Monday and gave Carrick at least one more game. Fabrizio Romano , speaking on Wednesday, put the order of preference as Eddie Howe first, then Julian Nagelsmann , then Antonio Conte , with Unai Emery admired but, as Romano framed it, very attractive and very difficult to get while he is under contract at Aston Villa . United have spoken to representatives, Romano said, but have not yet said "okay, let's go for this coach." The Athletic's reading is that the November international break is the realistic decision point, which gives Carrick Chelsea on Saturday, Roma on Tuesday and Aston Villa after that. Ratcliffe is reported to be flying in for Stamford Bridge, a ground at which he has never seen his club win. The Carrick File Position 16th, seven points from eight games, one point above the relegation zone. Contract A two-year deal signed in May 2026 after a successful spell as interim. No compensation figure has been published; do not trust one that is. Next three Chelsea away, Saturday October 31, 5:30am Pacific. Roma at home, Tuesday November 3, 12:00pm Pacific. Aston Villa away. What follows is the paper trail as it stood on Wednesday, with the stage of each deal stated plainly and the reporter or outlet named. Chelsea Move First, and Alone, on Alex Scott The most advanced January deal in Europe is also the least priced. Bournemouth 's owner has admitted on the record that his midfielder has turned down the chance to become the club's highest earner. Bill Foley , who owns Bournemouth , went on talkSPORT last week and said the quiet part out loud: the club "haven't given up" on a new contract for Alex Scott , that Scott has rejected several offers including one that would have made him the best-paid player at the club, and that talks will continue through the year. Foley also mentioned Manchester City as the kind of club players are drawn towards. For an owner, that is close to a concession. On the Chelsea side, the furthest-reaching claim comes from the Chelsea journalist Simon Phillips , who said on his YouTube channel on October 19 that Scott has verbally agreed personal terms that fit Chelsea 's wage structure and include a Champions League qualification bonus, and that Chelsea want to agree a base fee of 90 million pounds. Phillips added his own caveat: "it's not done until it's done." Football365, reporting it, labelled it honestly as coming from a journalist rather than a club. Nothing has been agreed between the two clubs. The asking price is the part nobody agrees on. FootballTransfers put it at "over 100 million euros" on October 22; SempreMilan put it at 140 million euros on October 27, while reporting that AC Milan 's interest is fading because, in its words, Chelsea are accelerating. Those two figures are five days apart and should not be averaged. ESPN frames Chelsea's motive as replacing Enzo Fernandez , and Liverpool are expected to compete, with Andoni Iraola reportedly keen to work with Scott again. Monaco's January Is a Compliance Sale Monaco 's chief executive has said publicly that Folarin Balogun is going in January, and explained why: the money is what lets the club keep Lamine Camara and Aleksandr Golovin until the summer. Most January stories are built from anonymous sourcing. This one comes from Monaco 's own chief executive. Thiago Scuro has confirmed on the record that Folarin Balogun is set to leave in the winter window, and tied it directly to French football's financial rules: selling the striker is what allows Monaco to keep Lamine Camara and Aleksandr Golovin to the end of the season. He also admitted there is no guarantee a buyer appears. Juventus are the named interest, reported by beIN Sports on October 27, and ESPN's round-up has Saudi Pro League clubs circling. Balogun's summer move to Everton collapsed after a failed medical, and when Everton came back late on deadline day the player declined. The second-order consequence is the interesting one, and nobody is writing it. Camara already had a move agreed once: the Evening Standard reported a fee of 47 million pounds settled with Chelsea and a six-year contract ready, before Monaco pulled out on deadline day. Monaco now want 70 million euros. But if no Balogun buyer materialises by late January, Monaco's own stated logic says the compliance money has to come from somewhere, and Camara is the only asset big enough to provide it. Milan's Window Begins in an Office, Not a Dressing Room AC Milan want Markus Krosche to run their recruitment. A buyout clause worth between five and seven million euros is in the way, and Gerry Cardinale wants the matter closed before the derby. Markus Krosche has just left Eintracht Frankfurt , where he built a reputation for buying cheaply and selling high. He is Gerry Cardinale 's preferred candidate to be AC Milan 's head of football. According to Calciomercato's Daniele Longo , writing on October 27, Krosche and Cardinale agree on the project and on his remit, money is not the obstacle, and the thing holding it up is the buyout clause in his Frankfurt contract, which runs to 2028 and which Longo puts at five to seven million euros. Milan do not want to pay it, and Krosche is talking to his former employer about a solution. Matteo Moretto reported as far back as June that Krosche had already reached an agreement with Milan; against that, SempreMilan carried a Sky Germany line that there are no advanced negotiations. The contracts, meanwhile, are nearly done. Corriere dello Sport reported on Wednesday that Christian Pulisic has a verbal agreement on an extension to 2031 worth around five million euros a year, with only the signature missing. Adrien Rabiot 's renewal, per Gazzetta dello Sport, is roughly two years plus an option, and Cardinale wants it signed by Christmas. On the pitch, Longo reports Milan's January priority is defensive cover rather than a striker, with Goncalo Inacio , Kim Min-jae , Thiago Gabriel and Daniele Ghilardi named. Milan also want Endrick , where they are not alone. Real Madrid Own Como's Future, and Como Agreed to It Two buy-back clauses, both exercisable in 2027, sit over the two players who have made Como the surprise of Serie A. One of them is priced at nine million euros. Nico Paz scored twice as Como beat Manchester United 4-1 last Wednesday and then headed in the 87th-minute winner at Torino on Tuesday. He belongs, commercially, to a structure Real Madrid designed. In June, Madrid activated a nine million euro buy-back on him and immediately sold him back to Como for 60 million, keeping a second buy-back worth 80 million euros exercisable in 2027. Madrid Universal, citing the Spanish journalist Ramon Alvarez , reported on October 24 that Madrid are considering activating it and want to exercise it. Como are not selling: TEAMtalk has them asking as much as 100 million euros if anyone approaches. The less-noticed clause is the bigger bargain. TuttoMercatoWeb reported on Wednesday that Jacobo Ramon , the 21-year-old centre back Como bought from Madrid for 2.5 million euros in 2025 and who headed in their equaliser at Torino, is covered by a buy-back of nine million euros, exercisable in three separate windows, the next of which falls in 2027, plus a 50 per cent share of any future resale. Ramon's current valuation is put at 45 to 50 million euros. Chelsea and Manchester United are among the clubs named as interested, as is Arsenal . Put plainly: the club that dragged itself into the Champions League and up to fourth in Serie A may lose both of the players who got it there, at prices it does not set. PSG Are Working a List, Not a Target Khvicha Kvaratskhelia has a torn cruciate ligament and is out for months. Paris Saint-Germain have approached two different left-sided forwards and bid for neither. The injury is the whole story. Nicolas Jackson scored both for Aston Villa , the first on six minutes after a loose touch by Marc Guehi , the second on 60 with a first-time finish that slid under Gianluigi Donnarumma . On September 29 an independent commission found Manchester City guilty of all charges relating to serious breaches of the league's financial rules across nine seasons from 2009-10 to 2017-18, and guilty of three of four alleged breaches of the duty to cooperate. Chief executive Richard Masters called it the most significant case in Premier League history. Sanctions are to be decided separately at a private hearing and no penalty has been announced; we could not confirm this week whether City have appealed, and will not speculate on a points deduction. Bukayo Saka tore a quad at Bayern Munich and will be out for weeks, with a rescan due around the start of November. 2. Arsenal beat Everton 2-0 while Manchester City lost at Aston Villa , leaving the two level on 21 points. 3. Sunday brings Liverpool away, a side on four straight wins under Andoni Iraola and unbeaten by Arsenal since 2024. The Lead Anfield, Without Him Arsenal arrive on Merseyside on Sunday level on points with Manchester City and shorn of the player who has started almost every important afternoon of the Arteta era. What follows is a test of whether the champions are a system or a supporting cast. T here were about ten minutes on the clock at the Allianz Arena last Wednesday when Bukayo Saka played a simple pass, reached for the back of his upper leg and stopped running. He did not go down theatrically. He did not wave at the bench. He simply walked, slowly, towards the touchline with the expression of a man who already knew. Eberechi Eze came on. Twenty-five minutes later Eze put Arsenal in front in Munich, and by the end Declan Rice had rescued a 2-2 from a game Bayern Munich had begun to control. The night was a credit to the squad. It was also the moment this season changed shape. Mikel Arteta was immediately blunt. "It doesn't look good at all but we have to wait and see," he said in Germany, and by Friday he had hardened it: "It will be weeks." A second scan was ordered because of fluid in the area, and the club expects to rescan again a week to ten days from now before fixing a return date. Several national outlets have put the window at six to eight weeks, which would take the vice-captain past the Champions League league phase and into the back half of December. That figure is not Arteta's, and the Digest treats it as unconfirmed; what is confirmed is that Saka will not play at Anfield, and that Arsenal are now asking a reshaped front line to go to the venue where their season most often curdles. Key facts: Liverpool v Arsenal WHEN Sunday, November 1, 8:30am Pacific. Anfield. Kick-off 4:30pm in the United Kingdom. FORM Liverpool 4th, 15 points, four straight wins in all competitions. Arsenal 2nd, 21 points, one defeat in thirteen. THE RUN Arsenal have not beaten Liverpool since February 2024. The last four meetings: three draws and a 1-0 defeat at Anfield in August 2025. MISSING Saka (quad) and Saliba (back) for Arsenal. Szoboszlai and Wirtz are doubts for Liverpool, with Frimpong and Ekitike out. The Iraola problem Begin with the tactical shape of it, because this is not the Liverpool anyone scouted a year ago. Andoni Iraola replaced Arne Slot on a two-year contract in June and has spent four months dismantling the idea that Anfield must be a possession fortress. Against Brighton on Sunday his side won 2-0 with 35.6 per cent of the ball, which Opta logged as Liverpool's second-lowest possession share in a Premier League home win since 2003-04. Brighton had 64 per cent and one shot on target. That is the Iraola signature transplanted from Bournemouth: a high, aggressive, man-oriented press, an invitation to play out, and then four players arriving in the box within six seconds of the turnover. Which sets up the key battle, and it is not the one the television build-up will choose. Liverpool's press is designed to force the ball into the full-back channels and then trap it there. Arsenal's build-up this season has leaned harder than ever on Myles Lewis-Skelly stepping inside from left-back and on Ben White holding width on the right, because William Saliba has not played a minute all season and Jurriën Timber has been in and out. With Riccardo Calafiori only just cleared and Piero Hincapié freshly back from an ankle problem, the back four that walks out at Anfield may be the fourth or fifth distinct combination Arteta has used in thirteen games. Against a side that hunts exactly those players, composure in the first fifteen minutes will decide more than any substitution. "It will be weeks." Mikel Arteta on Bukayo Saka, October 23 Who plays wide, and who scores The selection questions multiply from there. Noni Madueke has taken the right wing and done it well, scoring the only goal at Nottingham Forest and starting on the left in Munich before drifting back to his natural side. He is not Saka and Arteta has sensibly stopped asking him to be: where Saka manufactured chances by holding the touchline and inverting late, Madueke is at his best attacking a defender who is already moving. That suits a transition game, which is precisely what Sunday will be. Eze , meanwhile, has two goals in his last three appearances and looks liberated by a role that lets him begin wide and finish central. The uncomfortable question is the centre forward. Viktor Gyökeres has not scored for Arsenal this season. Not in the Premier League, not in Europe, not in the Carabao Cup. He assisted Ezri Konsa 's opener against Everton and played the one-two that set up Rice in Munich, and Arteta's defence of him has been consistent rather than grudging: "He was unlucky two or three moments. He's in front of goal, he's won the position to both centre-backs," the manager said on Monday, adding that the ball simply does not arrive. The data broadly agrees that Arsenal's open-play threat is up on last season. It does not change the fact that a title race in which your striker has nothing is a title race fought with a hand behind your back, and that Kai Havertz , three goals already, is the man Arteta has turned to when the game needs a goal rather than a structure. Title race tracker, after eight matches 1. Manchester City 21 pts (+11) 2. Arsenal 21 pts (+8) 3. Brighton & Hove Albion 16 pts 4. Liverpool 15 pts 5. Chelsea 13 pts City lost 2-1 at Aston Villa on Saturday while Arsenal were beating Everton. Arsenal have conceded five goals in eight league games and kept five clean sheets. What is actually at stake The stakes are plainer than usual, because the table has closed up in Arsenal's favour at exactly the moment their squad has thinned. Manchester City went to Villa Park on Saturday and lost 2-1; Arsenal beat Everton and drew level on 21 points, second only on goal difference. In other words the champions have been handed the initiative in the week they lost their most reliable attacker. Win at Anfield and they go top with the hardest away day of the autumn behind them. Lose and the narrative writes itself: a title defence that survives on set-piece margins and a goalkeeper, with no striker and no Saka. Which is unfair, but not entirely. The record at least is suggestive. Arsenal have not beaten Liverpool in any competition since February 2024, a run of three draws and one defeat that spans the whole of their rise from nearly-men to champions. They drew 0-0 at the Emirates last January and lost 1-0 at Anfield the previous August, both games in which they controlled possession and found no way through. Iraola's version of Liverpool will offer them far more of the ball and far less space. On the evidence of Munich, where Arsenal were second best for forty minutes and still left with a point, that may suit them better than anyone expects. Before any of that there is tonight: League Two Fleetwood Town , in the last sixteen of the Carabao Cup for the first time in their history, with no VAR and penalties straight after ninety minutes. Arteta has made nine changes and handed debuts to Illan Meslier and the 18-year-old Ceadach O'Neill . "We know the risk," he said. "Show them the Arsenal shirt and what we represent and that's it." It is the right instinct. It is also, this week, the second story. The Set-Piece Machine Went Quiet for 153 Days Arsenal scored nineteen Premier League goals from corners last season, a competition record. Before Ezri Konsa's header on Saturday they had scored none at all this season. The numbers say this is mostly not a conspiracy. Konsa 's seventh-minute finish from Martin Ødegaard 's corner against Everton ended a run of thirteen competitive games and 153 days without a goal from a corner or free kick. The previous one came from Madueke 's delivery against Crystal Palace on the final day of last season, in May. For a team whose set plays accounted for 26.8 per cent of their goals in a title-winning campaign, the highest share any Premier League champion has recorded, that is a genuine structural absence rather than a quirk. The Opta Analyst breakdown published on Saturday is worth reading in full, because it argues against the simplest explanations. Arsenal are still whipping in almost as many crosses from corners (84.9 per cent this season against 86.6 per cent last) and every single crossed corner has been an inswinger. They are actually winning first contact far more often: 42.9 per cent, second highest in the league, against 28.3 per cent last season. What has fallen is the quality of what follows. Shots from corners are down from 2.8 a game to 2.1, expected goals from corners down from 0.36 a game to 0.22, and the conversion rate from a league-best 8.8 per cent of corners to nothing at all. Arsenal are 1.55 goals below their corner expected goals, the second-largest shortfall in the division behind Liverpool. The corner, season by season Per Premier League game, 2025-26 against 2026-27. Each pair is drawn to its own scale by the Digest, from the Opta Analyst figures cited below. Shots from corners, 2025-26 2.8 per game Shots from corners, 2026-27 2.1 per game Expected goals from corners, 2025-26 0.36 per game Expected goals from corners, 2026-27 0.22 per game Goals from corners, 2025-26 (19 in all) 0.50 per game Goals from corners, 2026-27 (none in the league) 0.00 per game Three explanations have real weight. The first is personnel: Saliba has missed the entire season and Timber , one of last year's most dangerous near-post runners, has been intermittent. Havertz now leads Arsenal for first contacts from attacking corners with four; Gabriel , the totem of the whole operation, has one. The second explanation is placement. Arsenal have cut central six-yard-box deliveries by nearly eight percentage points and added almost exactly that volume to the near post, chasing flick-on routines that die on the first defender when the delivery is a fraction flat. The third explanation is simply the league: corners have produced 9.8 per cent of Premier League goals this season against 18.0 per cent last, and referees are awarding defending teams free kicks from four per cent of corners, the highest rate in seven seasons. Grappling is being policed. Nicolas Jover 's choreography depended on it being tolerated. The consoling counterpoint is that Arsenal have not needed it. Open-play expected goals are up roughly seventeen per cent, from 1.06 a game to 1.24, and the team is second in the table having conceded five league goals. A side that has swapped a dead-ball edge for a live-ball one has traded sideways, not down. But dead-ball goals are the ones you can still manufacture at Anfield when a press has pinned you in your own half for an hour, and that is the context in which Konsa's header mattered more than its timing suggested. Transfer News Brugge Draw a Line in the Sand Over Tresoldi Arsenal's interest in the Italian striker is real and reported by Sky. The selling club's answer, delivered through the Belgian press this week, was about as flat a no as a board can give. The most substantial live thread of Arsenal's autumn runs through Belgium. Nicolò Tresoldi , 22, has twelve goals in fourteen games for Club Brugge this season, four of them in three Champions League matches including one against Aston Villa , and sixteen in twenty-seven for the Germany under-21s. Sky Sports Germany reported this week that Arsenal are seriously interested and had him on their radar over the summer, while judging a January move unlikely and a summer approach the likelier route. The Belgian outlet Nieuwsblad went further, reporting that Arsenal are weighing a January bid with Barcelona also interested. Status: concrete interest, no bid, two independent reports. Brugge's response was unusually direct. A board member told Nieuwsblad that "there is no price for Nicolò, and there never will be," adding that any January offer would be "completely irrelevant" to them. The club rejected €35m from AS Roma in the summer, Tresoldi is contracted to 2029, and the stated position is that they expect to sell him eventually but want a marquee exit rather than a mid-season one. Read that as a price being set by refusing to set one. The strategic logic is obvious, and it is also why the Digest urges patience with it. Arsenal's centre forward has not scored this season. Havertz is 27 and has never been a volume striker. On the Here We Go podcast in September Fabrizio Romano described Arsenal's striker search as neither "imminent or urgent," said the club were "very happy with the strikers they have," and pointed to summer 2027 rather than January, with Eli Junior Kroupi of Bournemouth named as a player they may revisit. Romano also flagged right-back as the position to watch. Nothing reported since has contradicted that framing. A Tresoldi deal in January would be a reaction to Saka's injury as much as to Gyökeres's drought, and Arsenal's recruitment under Andrea Berta has not been a reactive operation. Calafiori, and the Price of Being Indispensable Chelsea have not gone away. Real Madrid have been mentioned. The eye-catching valuation attached to all of it comes from an aggregator, not a tier-one source. Riccardo Calafiori scored twenty-three seconds into the Community Shield and equalised against Leeds United on October 10, and has become the kind of left-sided defender who starts conversations. Chelsea retain interest after a bid Arsenal rejected, Real Madrid have been linked, and the figure circulating is a €100m asking price that would be a world record for a defender. That number originates with CaughtOffside and has not been stood up by a tier-one reporter, so treat it as mood music rather than a valuation. Status: rumour, single-sourced on the fee. What is harder to dismiss is the squad arithmetic. With Saliba absent all season and Timber and Hincapié both carrying knocks, Calafiori is simultaneously Arsenal's most valuable asset in that part of the pitch and their least dispensable one. Any serious January bid would land in the middle of an injury crisis. It is not a coincidence that reporting on an Arsenal interest in Xavi Espart , the 19-year-old Barcelona full-back, has been framed as insurance against losing him. Arteta singled out the cameo as a turning point. Scouting the Next Opponent Liverpool, Rebuilt From the Press Up Andoni Iraola has spent four months turning Anfield into a counterattacking ground. Arsenal visit a side that no longer wants the ball and is suddenly very good at not having it. Liverpool sacked Arne Slot and appointed Andoni Iraola on a two-year contract on June 4, then spent more than £200m rebuilding around him: Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain for a reported £106m, Jérémy Jacquet from Rennes for £55m, Víctor Muñoz from Osasuna for £34.5m and Ronald Araújo on loan from Barcelona with a purchase option. On the other side of the ledger, Mohamed Salah , Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konaté all left on free transfers and Curtis Jones went to Inter Milan . It is a different club, and for six weeks it looked like a confused one. It is not confused now. After a 0-3 home humiliation by Manchester City on October 11, Liverpool have won four in a row in all competitions, including 2-1 at Brentford and 2-0 at home to Brighton . They sit fourth on fifteen points from eight, one behind Brighton, and third in the Champions League league phase on nine points. Alexander Isak has six league goals, three in his last three league games, and Barcola has assisted him in each of the past two. Cody Gakpo has been impressive from the left. Florian Wirtz manufactured the opener against Brighton with the shot Pascal Groß turned into his own net. The three Arsenal must stop are therefore clear. Isak is the finisher and the first press trigger, dropping into the left channel to drag a centre-back out. Barcola is the width and the cut-back, switched to the right against Brighton and immediately decisive from there, which puts him directly into whichever of Lewis-Skelly or Calafiori plays left-back. Wirtz is the connector, and his availability is genuinely unclear: he twisted an ankle on the hour against Brighton, with Iraola saying it "doesn't look very big" while conceding the schedule forces caution. Dominik Szoboszlai is the other doubt, having lasted 32 minutes at Brentford and missed Brighton with a hamstring problem; Iraola says he is "close." Jérémie Frimpong , Hugo Ekitike and Víctor Muñoz are all out, with Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni and Vitezslav Jaros also absent with knee problems. Where they are vulnerable Where are they vulnerable? In exactly the place their new identity creates. A side that concedes 64 per cent of the ball at home and generates its chances from transition has to defend long spells in a mid-block, and Brighton proved the block can be pulled around: they simply could not finish, managing one shot on target from all that possession. Liverpool have also drawn three of eight and conceded in each of their first four league games of the season, including two-goal leads surrendered against Newcastle United and Nottingham Forest . If Arsenal can survive the opening twenty minutes of the press, a patient 2-0-style afternoon is available. The dead ball is the other lever, and the reason the Konsa goal mattered. Both managers will rotate. Neither can rotate freely. The Squad A Depth Chart Being Tested to Its Design Limits Arsenal spent £200m in the summer to be able to absorb exactly this. The absorption is working. It is also not free. The single most striking fact about Arsenal's season is one that almost never gets said out loud: William Saliba has not played a minute of it. The back problem he aggravated at the World Cup has been managed without surgery, he is understood to be back working on grass, and the current target is December with another scan to come. Arsenal are second in the Premier League with five goals conceded in eight games and a first-choice centre-back who has not kicked a ball. That is the clearest possible vindication of the Ezri Konsa signing, and of Cristhian Mosquera , about whom Arteta was pointed this week: "We have won some big games playing with him and we need him." The rest of the ward is less reassuring. Saka is out for weeks with the quad. Christos Tzolis , the £34m summer arrival, tore a hamstring on international duty with Greece and has barely been seen. Calafiori missed the Everton start with a small issue and came off the bench. Hincapié has returned early from an ankle injury. Gabriel hurt himself clearing a cross on 56 minutes on Saturday, carried on and scored twelve minutes later. Rice went off on 80 with what the club has not called an injury. The reporting from now.arsenal on Monday was that both Calafiori and Tzolis should be available at Anfield, which is the only genuinely good news in the paragraph. Rotation as policy, not panic Arteta's response has been to rotate hard and early rather than wait to be forced. Nine changes tonight at Fleetwood. A triple substitution on 68 against Everton with the game won. Zubimendi , barely a starter this season, given the holding role in the cup. Asked on Monday whether fringe players could earn promotion, the manager was careful: "Let's see tomorrow where everybody is because individually as well we have put so much demand in so many players." The phrase to notice is "so much demand." Arsenal have played thirteen competitive matches in ten weeks and have a Champions League trip to Prague three days after Anfield. Tactically, two shifts stand out. The first is the set-piece decline covered above, offset by an open-play threat up roughly seventeen per cent on last season. The second is the reconfigured front line. With Gabriel Martinelli sold to Al-Hilal for a club-record £60m and Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Jesus also gone, Arsenal's left side is now Eze by default and Madueke by necessity, with Max Dowman as the emergency teenager. That worked in Munich. Whether it works against a man-marking press at Anfield is Sunday's actual question. The manager's own yellow cards One subplot to watch: Arteta himself is a yellow card from a touchline ban. Referee Tony Harrington booked him in the second half against Everton for leaving his technical area, his second caution of the season, and one more brings a one-match suspension from the touchline. His reaction was equal parts joke and grievance. "I do have to be careful, yeah. I'm going to put sensors there!" he said, before claiming that rival managers leave their areas "36 times in 10 minutes, no yellows" and that he is building a case: "So I am clipping all of that so I have a massive storage of images." A manager compiling video evidence against his peers is good copy. A manager banned from the touchline for a title run-in is not. Availability, as of Tuesday Bukayo Saka , quad. Out. Hurt at Bayern on October 21. Arteta: "It will be weeks." Rescan due in a week to ten days. Six to eight weeks has been reported nationally and is not confirmed by the club. William Saliba , back. Out. Aggravated at the World Cup, managed without surgery, yet to play this season. December is the working target, with another scan planned. Christos Tzolis , hamstring. Picked up with Greece. Expected back in contention for Liverpool. Riccardo Calafiori , minor issue. Came off the bench against Everton and is expected to be available at Anfield. Piero Hincapié , ankle. Returned early and starts tonight. Declan Rice and Gabriel both took knocks on Saturday without either being confirmed as an injury. Hale End Two Debuts Tonight, and an Under-21 Side Going Nowhere The academy's best are being promoted faster than ever. The team they leave behind has not won a league game all season. Start with the good. Ceadach O'Neill makes his Arsenal debut at Fleetwood tonight, as does the summer free signing Illan Meslier in goal. Marli Salmon , 17, starts in central defence alongside Mosquera , and Max Dowman starts in attack. On the bench sit three more academy names in Harriman-Annous , Washington and Hashi . For a club in a title race and a Champions League league phase, that is a remarkable amount of trust to place in a League Two away tie with no VAR and penalties straight after ninety minutes. Dowman remains the headline act and the reason the academy is a first-team story rather than a footnote. He is 16 until December 31, when a pre-contract agreed in January converts into professional terms. He already holds the records for the youngest Premier League goalscorer (16 years 73 days, against Everton in March), the youngest Premier League title winner, the youngest starter in Premier League history and the youngest player ever to appear in the Champions League, at 15 years 308 days. He scored twice in the Carabao Cup win at Ipswich Town in September and came off the bench against Everton on Saturday. Whether Saka's absence accelerates him into a league starting role is the most interesting selection question Arteta faces before Christmas. The league table nobody mentions Below that, it has been a grim autumn. The under-21s lost 4-1 at Leicester City on Saturday, O'Neill scoring the consolation and Salmon playing the first half before being withdrawn with tonight in mind.
