x: World football, every Wednesday · Arsenal covered separately The Weekly Soccer Digest Wednesday Edition · October 21, 2026 · Vol. 1 In this edition The Lead · Como's Night · Transfer News · The Rumour Mill · Around the Leagues · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead Mourinho Walks Back Into the Camp Nou Thirteen years after he left Spain, Jose Mourinho returns to Barcelona as Real Madrid's manager, six points adrift of a side that had won eleven straight until Tuesday, and without the two wingers who were supposed to win him the game. T here is no gentle way to walk into the Spotify Camp Nou, and Jose Mourinho has never looked for one. On Sunday evening, at 1 p.m. Pacific, he takes Real Madrid back to the ground where he spent three seasons in open warfare with the institution he is about to visit, and he does it as the underdog. Barcelona have won nine from nine in La Liga. They have 27 points. Real Madrid have 21, and are third, behind Atletico Madrid as well. A Barcelona win on Sunday makes the gap nine points before Halloween. What makes the fixture genuinely hard to call is that both sides arrive bruised in different places. Barcelona's winning run, eleven matches across all competitions, ended on Tuesday night at the Parc des Princes, where Paris Saint-Germain beat them 4-2 in the best game of the Champions League season so far. It was not a collapse. It was something more worrying for Hansi Flick : two individual errors, one from Lamine Yamal inside his own half for Desire Doue 's opener, one from Warren Zaire-Emery 's opponent under a high ball, and a midfield that could not hold the ball when Vitinha decided to take the game. Barcelona equalised twice, through Xavi Espart and then Yamal himself, and still lost by two. Real Madrid, meanwhile, will play the biggest match of their season so far without Vinicius Junior , who is suspended, and without Rodrygo , who has a cruciate ligament injury. That is a Clasico without either of the wingers who have carried Madrid's transitions for the better part of five years. Kylian Mbappe has nine La Liga goals and will almost certainly start centrally. Beyond him, Mourinho is short of the specific thing his teams have always been built to do, which is run at a high line with pace in the wide areas. Ferland Mendy is back in training. Raul Asencio is not available. Madrid at least arrive in form: they beat RB Leipzig 4-1 at the Bernabeu on Wednesday night, Mbappe and Arda Guler among the scorers, a third straight Champions League win. El Clasico: Key Facts Kickoff Sunday October 25, 1:00 p.m. Pacific (9:00 p.m. in Barcelona) Venue Spotify Camp Nou, La Liga matchday 10 Managers Hansi Flick (Barcelona), Jose Mourinho (Real Madrid) League Barcelona 1st, 27 pts from 9. Real Madrid 3rd, 21 pts from 9 Barcelona out Olmo, Christensen, Eric Garcia, Kounde, Bardghji, de Jong Real Madrid out Vinicius Junior (suspended), Rodrygo, Asencio. Mendy back in training Head to head Barcelona 29 wins, Real Madrid 21, 10 draws Which leaves the tactical question of the week: does Mourinho try to win this game, or does he try to stop Barcelona winning it? His record at the Camp Nou in his first spell suggests he is perfectly willing to do the latter and absorb the criticism, and there is a reasonable argument that 21 points from nine games is not a platform from which to gamble. Barcelona's shape under Flick is still the most aggressive in Europe's top five leagues, a high line that invites exactly the ball in behind that Mbappe has spent his career running onto. PSG hurt Barcelona by playing through them rather than over them. Madrid, without Vinicius and Rodrygo , may not have that option. Barcelona's own absentee list is longer. Dani Olmo came off injured in Paris. Andreas Christensen and Eric Garcia have thigh problems, Jules Kounde a sprained ankle. Roony Bardghji ruptured a cruciate ligament in training in August and Frenkie de Jong has been out since tearing the medial collateral ligament in his right knee at the World Cup. The absence that matters most tactically is at centre back: with Christensen out, Ronald Araujo on loan at Liverpool and Kounde injured, Gerard Martin is Flick 's only natural left-sided option. Catalan reporting this month names a left-footed centre back as Barcelona's clearest squad need, and the club cannot address it in January without selling first. More on that below. The two squads were rebuilt around each other over the summer, which gives Sunday an extra edge. Barcelona spent roughly 174 million euros on seven players, headlined by Anthony Gordon from Newcastle United for 70 million plus up to 10 million in variables and Rodri from Manchester City for 60 million plus up to 15 million, with Karim Adeyemi arriving from Borussia Dortmund and Joao Cancelo back on a free. Robert Lewandowski left at the end of his contract. Ferran Torres was sold to PSG for 48.5 million euros, which is why he was on the pitch in Paris on Tuesday in the other shirt, and why he hit the post against the club that made him. "I don't care about [the favourites tag] because I don't see PSG as the favourite. This match isn't decisive. The decisive month will be in April." Luis Enrique, after PSG 4-2 Barcelona The individual duel to watch is Raphinha against whichever full back Mourinho trusts. Raphinha leads the Pichichi race with twelve goals, three clear of Mbappe , and is the one Barcelona attacker whose form has not wobbled. Yamal has eight in La Liga and nine goals with ten assists across eleven appearances in all competitions, and Joan Laporta chose the week of the PSG tie to tell L'Equipe that he is going nowhere. "He's a Barca fan and came through La Masia," Laporta said, in beIN Sports' English rendering of the French interview. "All of that helps when it comes to renewing a contract. We're not worried." The Pichichi Race La Liga top scorers after matchday 9. Raphinha Barcelona 12 Kylian Mbappe Real Madrid 9 Lamine Yamal Barcelona 8 Sergio Camello Rayo Vallecano 7 Ante Budimir Osasuna 7 The head-to-head record in the fixture's modern run reads 29 wins to Barcelona, 21 to Real Madrid, ten draws. None of that will matter much by Sunday evening. What will matter is whether Mourinho , who built his reputation on exactly this kind of night, can produce one more of them with half his attack missing, and whether a Barcelona side that has not lost a league game all season can absorb the first real test of its nerve. The tie is at 1 p.m. Pacific, 9 p.m. in Barcelona. Spain's clocks go back that morning, so the local time reads the same as it did in September while the Pacific conversion shifts. Como's Night Como 4, Manchester United 1 A club playing its first Champions League campaign took Manchester United apart on the shore of Lake Como, and the questions about Michael Carrick are now the loudest in English football. Nico Paz scored inside two minutes. By the time Anastasios Douvikas made it two early in the second half, Manchester United had managed no shots on target at all in the first half, had committed nine fouls to Como 's two, and had seen 62 per cent of the ball go the other way. Michael Carrick made two substitutions at the interval, sending on Amad Diallo and Carlos Baleba for Matheus Cunha and Andrey Santos . It did not help. Como finished 4-1 winners, with Paz scoring twice and assisting another, and Douvikas and Ramon also on the scoresheet, according to Corriere dello Sport . It was Como's first home match in the competition. Como are fifth in Serie A on 14 points, have won four of seven, and beat Fiorentina 3-1 away on Sunday. Cesc Fabregas , whose contract runs to June 2028, has built something that now has to be taken seriously rather than enjoyed as a curiosity. His line after the match, to Gianluca Di Marzio , was about the next one rather than this one: "Crediamo tanto in Baturina. Vogliamo diventare una realta solida." We believe a great deal in Baturina. We want to become a solid reality. United's position is harder to describe charitably. They are 13th in the Premier League on seven points from seven games, with one win, and drew 1-1 at Leeds United on Sunday. They have now lost to Atletico Madrid and Como in successive Champions League matchdays after opening with a 4-0 win over Sabah . Carrick used his press conference last weekend to talk about January, telling Sky Sports : "When the next transfer window comes, you want to plan and you want to make the best of it. Whatever that looks like at this stage, we don't quite know. But without doubt, there's opportunity because the transfer window is open." Sky reported centre back and left back as the priorities. With Luke Shaw injured, United currently have no senior left back. The commercial irony is sharp. In late September the club reported record revenue of 677 million pounds achieved without European football. It now has European football and a 4-1 defeat to a club that was in Serie B three years ago. Across the rest of matchday 3 on Wednesday night, nine matches produced 34 goals and exactly one draw. Real Madrid beat RB Leipzig 4-1, Aston Villa made it three wins from three by seeing off Viking 3-1, Club Brugge beat Lens 3-0 and Inter Milan edged Shakhtar Donetsk 1-0 with ten men after Alessandro Bastoni was sent off. Real Betis beat Feyenoord 1-0 through an Isco penalty, Galatasaray came from 2-1 down to win 4-2 at Lille with Victor Osimhen scoring, and Bayern Munich were held 2-2 at home by Arsenal. The shock was in Lisbon, where LASK , pointless after two matchdays, won 3-2 at Sporting CP . Transfer News Europe's summer window closed on September 1, so nothing below is a completed transfer. What is moving instead is the thing that always moves in late October: the January pre-contract clock, which starts on New Year's Day and turns every player whose deal expires in June 2027 into either an asset to be sold now or a free agent to be lost later. Certainty tiers are stated for every item. The January 1 Clock Is Already Driving the Market Every contract expiring in June 2027 becomes a pre-contract target on New Year's Day. That single date explains most of this week's reporting. Under FIFA rules a player inside the final six months of a contract can agree a pre-contract with a club in another country. From January 1 that applies to the whole June 2027 cohort, and clubs with sellable players and no signatures are suddenly motivated. The cleanest illustration is at Bournemouth , where Rob Dorsett and Mark McAdam of Sky Sports News reported on October 16 that the club will consider offers in excess of 80 million pounds plus add-ons in January for Alex Scott , who has refused a new contract reported to be the best the club has ever offered. Status: concrete interest with a club valuation set, no bid on the table. Fabrizio Romano corroborated it four days later, saying Chelsea are "definitely there" and have had several contacts with Scott's representatives after a rejected summer bid, and that Liverpool made calls in late June and early July without ever bidding. Scott is 23, an England international, currently injured, and has a little over 18 months left. Marco Rose was blunt when asked: "I told you that Alex Scott was going to stay in the summer. He's a player of our club and now he's injured. If he is back, he's playing for Bournemouth." The same mechanism is producing stories everywhere. Jean-Philippe Mateta is out of contract in June 2027 at Crystal Palace and, per talkSPORT material carried in Sky's Paper Talk on October 20, is showing no inclination to extend, with Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur both linked. Graeme Bailey of TEAMtalk reported in late September that United's director of football Jason Wilcox rates his Premier League goals record. Status: concrete interest plus reported player willingness, no talks between clubs. Mateta has made two appearances this season with a hamstring problem, which is the obvious complication. In Spain the same clock is ticking loudest at Sevilla . Javier Merino of JaviSFC reported on October 21 that centre back Andres Castrin , out of contract on June 30 2027, agreed terms in early October on a three-year extension with a significant rise and a 50 million euro release clause, and that the club is still waiting for a formal response from his agency. From January 1 he can sign elsewhere for nothing. Bayer Leverkusen are following closely; Valencia , Real Sociedad , Leeds United and Espanyol are named as interested. This is a Sevilla-specialist outlet rather than a national one, so treat the detail as single-sourced, though the structural facts are not in dispute. Garcia Plaza said in late September: "Ojala renueve, ojala." Liverpool Have Three Midfielders on One List Alex Scott, Lamine Camara and Adam Wharton are all live Liverpool links inside ten days. Romano says the intent is explicit. The most useful kind of transfer signal is not a single report but a cluster, and Liverpool have produced one. Fabrizio Romano said on October 20 that "Liverpool are planning to do something important in midfield in 2027," and inside the same ten-day window three separate midfielders have been reported as targets. Lamine Camara is the one with the most history. Romano reported, in material written up by James Marshment at TEAMtalk , that Chelsea had agreed a 47 million pound fee for the 22-year-old Senegal international with Monaco on deadline day before the deal collapsed, that Chelsea were "furious" and are "no longer in talks," and that Liverpool are now frontrunners at a price closer to 59 million pounds. Status: concrete interest and long-term tracking, no bid. Single-origin to Romano, carried by two outlets. There is a separate Liverpool thread worth tracking. Romano said on October 21 that there are "active conversations ongoing between Rio Ngumoha and Liverpool over a new, long-term contract," that the club "absolutely want to keep Rio," and then hedged carefully: "Let's see what's gonna happen in the future, but his contract talks are taking place." Rio Ngumoha is 18 and under contract to 2028. Status: active talks, no agreement. Separately, The Telegraph reported on October 21 that Liverpool have not yet opened renewal talks with Alexis Mac Allister , whose deal runs to 2028, and that Chelsea are watching. Single-sourced. Kane Agrees Terms to 2029, and Dortmund Tie Down Kovac Bayern got the shorter deal they wanted. Dortmund extended their manager a week before the doubts came back. Michael Bridge of Sky Sports News reported on October 16 that Harry Kane has agreed a new Bayern Munich contract in principle through the summer of 2029. Sky Sport Germany and Bild had the same line the previous day. Kane reportedly wanted 2030, so Bayern got their preferred term. The Times put the terms at roughly 474,000 euros a week, just under 25 million a year, which is his existing salary unchanged. Status: personal terms agreed, not signed and not announced. Bridge: "There are just a few things to iron out before confirmation." President Herbert Hainer called the talks "hervorragend." No release clause has been reported. At Borussia Dortmund , the extension is done and official. Niko Kovac signed to 2029 on October 13, along with assistants Robert Kovac and Filip Tapalovic , per the club and Get German Football News . Lars Ricken , managing director for sport, said: "With Niko Kovac, we've been on a very good path since he took office a little over a year and a half ago." Kovac inherited an 11th-placed team in February 2025 and finished second on 73 points last season. Barcelona Have About One Million Euros of Room A detailed look at the club's fair-play position concludes that any January signing must be preceded by a sale. The renewals are eating the margin. Artur Lopez published the single hardest number in this week's European reporting. Writing for Cronica Global on October 11, he set out Barcelona 's position under La Liga's salary rules: the club's limit has risen from 432 million euros to 582 million, and its sporting costs have risen 115 million to 581 million. That is a margin of roughly one million euros. His conclusion is unambiguous: "Todo fichaje en enero de 2027 tendra que pasar primero por ventas." Every January signing will have to come after a sale. At Real Madrid the renewal board is busier and the money less constrained. Jose Felix Diaz of Diario AS reported on October 16 that Jude Bellingham has agreed an extension to June 2031, two years beyond his current deal, with a rise and no figure published. Status: agreement reached, official announcement still expected, and effectively single-sourced to AS. Thibaut Courtois has verbally agreed a one-year extension to 2028, per both Romano and MARCA on October 13, unsigned. Arda Guler 's extension to 2031 is reported closed and awaiting announcement. Antonio Rudiger , out of contract in 2027, has no deal and no talks, which makes him Madrid's only senior expiry inside twelve months. Eduardo Camavinga , to 2029, has no extension conversations at all. Vinicius Junior 's file is closed: he signed to June 2032 in the summer, and his terms set the ceiling every other negotiation at the club is measured against. Nico Paz, Chelsea, and Real Madrid's 80 Million Euro Button Como own him outright. Madrid can buy him back next summer for a fixed price. Chelsea have been watching, and Como's number starts with a one. The most interesting contractual object in European football right now sits on the shore of Lake Como. Marco Conterio of TUTTOmercatoWEB reported on October 21 that Chelsea staff have watched Nico Paz in recent Serie A and Champions League matches and are not deterred by the price. Como own 100 per cent of his registration after paying around 60 million euros in June 2026. Real Madrid hold an exclusive buy-back at 80 million euros, exercisable in the summer of 2027, and take a percentage of any onward sale if they decline it. Guido Lorenzelli of CalcioComo added the same day that Como would only entertain 100 to 120 million euros, and attributed the Chelsea line to unnamed market whispers. On the Spanish side, Diego Vargas at Defensa Central reported the identical 60 and 80 million structure and said Madrid have not decided. Status: concrete interest at scouting level, no bid. The sequencing is the story: if Madrid press the button at 80 million, they buy a 22-year-old playmaker for less than Como could get on the open market, and Como's upside evaporates. The Rumour Mill The Rumour Mill The sagas still simmering, with the certainty of each stated plainly. Where something is single-sourced or rests on an aggregator, it says so. Lewis Hall, Newcastle to Manchester United Rumour, plus reported player willingness. No bid, no talks. The i Paper reported on October 20 that Hall was interested in Old Trafford a few months ago and has not changed his stance; Dean Jones at FlashScore reported on October 14 that Newcastle could value him above 100 million euros and that the finances are the major obstacle. Hall signed a new Newcastle deal in September running to 2031, which is the club's shield. Framed for 2027 rather than January. Two independent reporters. Lisandro Martinez, Manchester United Club planning, and the sources conflict. MailSport reported on October 21 that United will trigger their 12-month option to 2028 and then transfer-list him. Romano said on October 5 that United "have a clause to extend the contract till 2028, so they feel calm, they feel in control," that they still believe in him as a leader, and that he "is not in advanced negotiations with any other side." The Mail line is single-sourced and contradicts Romano. Treat with caution. Emiliano Buendia, new Aston Villa deal Advanced talks, offer on the table. Graeme Bailey at TEAMtalk and The Athletic both reported on October 20 that Aston Villa have offered Buendia, whose deal expires this season, a two-and-a-half-year extension to summer 2029, and that talks with Victor Lindelof and George Hemmings are also progressing. Two independent outlets on the same day, the best-sourced contract story of the week. A renewal ends Leeds United , Galatasaray and Fenerbahce interest. Markus Krosche, Eintracht Frankfurt to AC Milan Departure done, appointment in advanced talks. Kicker broke it on October 18: Krosche asked Eintracht Frankfurt to release him from his sporting-director duties, saying he needed a change, and the club agreed. x: The Weekly Arsenal Digest One club, every front, every Tuesday No. 10 · Season 2026/27 Tuesday, October 20, 2026 Read this edition on the web In this edition The Lead · Transfer News · The Squad · Hale End · Arsenal Women · Gunners Abroad · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead Back to Munich, Carrying a Different Kind of Problem Arsenal arrive at the Allianz Arena as champions of England, unbeaten in Europe and yet to concede a Champions League goal. They have also scored eleven times in seven league games. Wednesday night asks the question this season keeps asking: can a team this good at not losing find a way to actually win something bigger? T here is a version of this week that writes itself. Arsenal go to Bayern Munich on Wednesday with fourteen consecutive Champions League league-phase wins behind them, two clean sheets from two this season, a Premier League title in the cabinet for the first time since 2004 and a manager who has just signed on until 2030. They are second in the table, three points behind Manchester City , and they have lost once all season. By any ordinary accounting, this is a club in rude health walking into the most glamorous fixture on its calendar. Then you look at Sunday afternoon. Arsenal went to the City Ground, held seventy-four per cent of the ball, played 629 passes at ninety per cent accuracy, and registered precisely one shot on target. It went in, because Noni Madueke drove inside from the left on eighty minutes and the ball glanced off Jair Cunha and past Matz Sels . Without that deflection this is a goalless afternoon against a side that had not scored at home in the league all season, and the conversation this morning is very different. That is the real story of Arsenal 's autumn, and it is the thing Mikel Arteta will be turning over on the flight to Bavaria. His team have won 1-0 thirteen times in the last 366 days. They have conceded five goals in seven league matches. They have also scored eleven, which is fewer than Brentford , fewer than Chelsea , and barely half of Brighton 's twenty-three. A title defence built on a back four and a goalkeeper is a legitimate way to win a league. It is a far harder way to win in Munich. Key facts: Bayern Munich v Arsenal The tie Champions League league phase, matchday three, Allianz Arena, Wednesday Kick-off 12:00pm Pacific (8:00pm in London, 9:00pm in Munich) Bayern at home Unbeaten in a Champions League group or league-phase match at the Allianz since December 2013 Harry Kane 15 goals in 22 appearances against Arsenal Last meeting Arsenal 3-1 Bayern, Emirates Stadium, November 26, 2025 Out Arsenal: Saliba, Hincapie, Tzolis. Bayern: Musiala, Olise (suspended), with Kompany and Neuer both doubtful The shape of the night The tactical shape of the evening is unusually legible, because both teams are missing the player who would normally bend it. Bayern are without Jamal Musiala , who has a thigh problem, and without Michael Olise , suspended after his red card against Viking on matchday two. Vincent Kompany is recovering from a viral infection, missed training and did not take Tuesday's press conference, which assistant Aaron Danks fronted instead. Manuel Neuer has fluid on his foot. For a club that beat RB Leipzig 6-1 on Saturday, this is still a formidable team, but it is a reshuffled one, and Serge Gnabry is the likeliest man to take Olise's place against the club where he began. Arsenal 's own absence is the one that matters most. William Saliba is still out with the back problem that has cost him most of the autumn, and is only now back in individual training with a return targeted for next month. In his place Ezri Konsa , the £55m arrival from Aston Villa , has formed a partnership with Gabriel Magalhaes that has produced five clean sheets in nine appearances. Arteta was unambiguous about them after Sunday, saying the win "was not possible without them." Konsa also happens to have a good personal record against Kane, who had a thin evening at the Emirates last November. "We reached a mountain, but not the highest one or the one that I certainly visualise." Mikel Arteta, on winning the Premier League That quote, given to HBO Max's Inside the Game , is the key to why this fixture carries more freight than a matchday-three away trip ought to. Last season Arsenal were on for a quadruple and finished with one trophy. They lost the EFL Cup final to Manchester City , went out of the FA Cup to Southampton in the quarter-finals, and lost the Champions League final to Paris Saint-Germain 4-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw. The league title ended a twenty-two-year wait and it genuinely changed the club. It also left the one trophy Arteta talks about in those terms still unwon, and the shortest route to it runs through nights exactly like Wednesday. Arteta's choices The selection questions are real. Jurrien Timber is expected at right-back, sharing the load with Ben White . Martin Zubimendi is back from a minor hamstring issue but has played so little this season that a start would be a surprise, which leaves Declan Rice as the fixed point and a genuine choice between Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes alongside him. The midfield triangle against Joshua Kimmich and Aleksandar Pavlovic is where Danks expects the match to be settled, and he is probably right. Up front, the arithmetic is awkward. Kai Havertz has three goals in nine appearances and has been below his level since the international break, but Arteta picks him for big games and went out of his way last week to argue that Havertz can become a twenty-five-goal striker. Viktor Gyokeres has started both Champions League matches and has not scored for the club this season. Bukayo Saka has four goals in all competitions and was quiet at Forest. The one man in form is Madueke, who scored the winner from the bench on Sunday after being hauled on for Eberechi Eze at half-time, and who is the obvious candidate to start on the left. Arteta's framing of the whole thing has been notably unhedged. He said he wants Bayern at full strength, expects "96 minutes of man-to-man," and intends to "confront that and go for it." He will not get Bayern at full strength, and he arrives without his best defender. A draw in Munich would keep Arsenal comfortably inside the top eight and would be a perfectly good night's work. A win would be the first proper statement of the defence of a title and of a continental ambition that last May came down to a shootout. Either way, the number that will tell us most is not the scoreline. It is the shot count. One on target at the City Ground was enough on Sunday. It will not be enough on Wednesday. The Vacancy on the Left Gabriel Martinelli is in Saudi Arabia, Christos Tzolis is injured, Eberechi Eze keeps drifting inside and Noni Madueke has just won a match from the bench. Arsenal's left wing has become the most open job at the club. When Gabriel Martinelli left for Al Hilal for £60m in early September, Arsenal accepted a reality that had been building for a while: the left flank was no longer a settled position. The summer replacement was Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge at £34m, who is a useful footballer rather than a transformative one, and who is currently out with a hamstring problem until roughly the start of November. Into the gap stepped Eberechi Eze , the £69m signing from Crystal Palace , who scored against Lille by drifting inside from the touchline, which is both his great strength and the reason he keeps being described as a stopgap out wide. At Forest he was anonymous and came off at half-time. Arteta did not name him in his post-match remarks. He did not need to. The man who has taken the chance is Madueke , and the story of how is worth knowing. Not called up by England over the October break, he stayed at the training ground and worked with Arteta, who afterwards said he had created more chances and taken more touches in the opposition box than anyone there. He started against Leeds United , crossed for Riccardo Calafiori 's equaliser in the 2-1 win, and then won the Forest game off the bench. Arteta's verdict was blunt: Madueke "gave me no option," and had been the best player in training for ten days. It is a left-footer on the left, which is unusual for this manager, and the wider question remains open. Arteta has floated Max Dowman there. Myles Lewis-Skelly can cover it. None of that is the same as an elite option, which is precisely why the January conversation below exists. Transfer News The January Attacker, and the Line Arsenal Cannot Cross David Ornstein's assessment is the one to trust: Arsenal know they are short in attack, they wanted to fix it in the summer and did not, and the constraint is financial rather than philosophical. Nothing has moved publicly on this thread in the last seven days, which is itself worth reporting, because the volume of speculation around it has gone up considerably while the sourcing has stayed exactly where it was. The best account remains David Ornstein 's reader Q&A for The Athletic in mid-September, and it is unusually candid. Arsenal lost Leandro Trossard , Gabriel Jesus and Martinelli in one window, loaned out Ethan Nwaneri , and did not "go beyond the signing of Christos Tzolis," who was in effect the Trossard replacement. Jesus was not replaced at all. On whether they will act in January, Ornstein's words were: "I could see something happening because they wanted to, and I thought they needed to, in the summer and they didn't." He paired that with a warning. The Lead The champions of Europe walk into the one place nobody is losing Paris Saint-Germain have won the last two Champions Leagues. There is also the matter that will not be in the team sheet. This is City’s first European night since an independent commission found the club guilty of almost all of the financial charges brought against it by the Premier League , covering nine seasons to 2017/18, including what the league’s own statement called “sham” sponsorship arrangements used to inflate revenue by more than 900m pounds. City lodged an appeal on 1 October, to be heard within twelve weeks. Sanctions have not yet been set. Maresca was asked about it in the international break and said simply: “I completely trust the club.” Asked whether past titles were tainted, he answered: “Absolutely not.” And the last wrinkle is the sweetest. Pep Guardiola , who resigned in the summer after nine completed seasons, is expected in the stands. Maresca was asked whether that was awkward and declined the invitation: “He can come at any time he wants.” Nine years of City’s European identity were built by the man in the seat; the new one is unbeaten and has a European Cup holder to measure himself against. Kick-off was noon Pacific on the day this was written, which is to say that the edition and the football match were meant to reach the world at the same moment. Matchday three gives the loser no rest either: PSG host Barcelona next Tuesday, and City go again on the same night. Mourinho goes back to Rome with his own October on the line Four months into the Real Madrid job, Jose Mourinho returns to the club he managed for two and a half years, without Vinicius Junior and with four defenders in the treatment room. The symmetry was always going to be too good to leave alone. Jose Mourinho was appointed Real Madrid manager in June on a three-year deal to 2029, his second spell at the club and his first since 2013. His first October in charge has handed him a trip to the Roma he managed from 2021 to 2024, and with whom he won the inaugural Conference League in 2022. He is still sung about in that stadium. He is also, four months in, being written about in Madrid in the way Madrid managers get written about. The numbers behind the noise are not catastrophic and not comfortable. Madrid are fourth in La Liga on 18 points from eight, six wins and two defeats, beaten by Atletico Madrid and by Real Betis . Infobae noted this week that the tally is three points worse than Xabi Alonso ’s side managed at the same stage, and framed a five-game October in fifteen days as the stretch that could shape Mourinho’s future. Saturday’s 1-0 over Villarreal was won by Diomande , the 140m euro summer signing, with his first Madrid goal, assisted by Fede Valverde . Kylian Mbappe hit a post, was twice denied, and was whistled by some of his own supporters. The afternoon’s lasting damage was not the performance. Vinicius Junior , a substitute, had a goal disallowed and was then sent off after a VAR review showed him pulling the hair of Villarreal ’s Nathan Saliba . On Wednesday the Spanish federation’s disciplinary committee handed down four matches: two for violent conduct away from the ball and two for protesting to the referee. Madrid’s claim of a “manifest material error” was rejected. He misses Sevilla on Sunday and, more to the point, he misses the Clasico at Barcelona on 25 October. His own public response was short: “The joy continues. My apologies to my team and the fans.” Mourinho skipped his post-match press conference entirely after Villarreal, giving no reason, having himself been booked for protesting. That followed a September in which he produced a printed sheet of disputed refereeing decisions after the derby defeat to Atletico, prompting league president Javier Tebas to reject any suggestion of a conspiracy and Madrid to reply that Tebas is “not the owner of the competition”. Four defenders were unavailable for the flight to Rome: Ferland Mendy , Eder Militao , Rodrygo and Raul Asencio , whose prognosis the club lists as pending. Roma, by contrast, have rarely looked more organised. Gian Piero Gasperini ’s side are third in Serie A on 14 points with the best goal difference in the division and the best defence in it, three goals conceded in six games. They drew 1-1 at Fenerbahce on matchday one and held Como to the league’s first goalless draw on Sunday, a night that cost them Donyell Malen to the first red card of his career. Malen leads Serie A’s scoring charts with six and serves his domestic ban against Genoa on Saturday, which means he was free to play against Madrid. Mourinho, of all people, will have noted that. Carvajal’s long wait ends in the unlikeliest place A Champions League winner with Real Madrid, out of contract since June, has agreed terms with a club 14th in La Liga. The only remaining obstacle is a spreadsheet. Dani Carvajal is 34 and has been a free agent since 30 June, when a Real Madrid contract that spanned six European Cups expired without renewal. This week it became clear where he is going, and it is not where anyone would have guessed: Getafe , fourteenth in La Liga on eight points, managed by Jose Bordalas , playing in a 17,000-seat stadium on the southern edge of Madrid. The paper trail is unusually clean. Getafe ’s interest was first reported by ABC. Marca reported on 6 October that an agreement had been reached, subject to La Liga approving the club’s squad-cost position. Getafe’s president Angel Torres confirmed as much on DAZN, saying Carvajal had passed a medical and that the move is a free transfer: “If I can reach an agreement with La Liga, he will most likely join us.” By 8 October the deal was still being described as at risk on exactly that point. Fabrizio Romano now reports the salary has been cleared and that only the official announcement remains. Where it stands Agreement reached, announcement pending. Reported by Fabrizio Romano, after Marca on 6 October and confirmation on camera from Getafe ’s own president. The lesson is less about Carvajal than about the mechanism. Getafe are operating under a La Liga squad-cost limit that is a rounding error next to the clubs Carvajal spent his career beating. Real Madrid’s 2026/27 limit was set at 832.78m euros, Barcelona’s at 582.76m, Atletico’s at 361.27m and Sevilla ’s at 20.16m, the lowest in the division. In that world, a free transfer is not a bargain. It is a negotiation with a regulator. Madrid quietly solve their biggest 2027 problem Thibaut Courtois was on every list of players whose contracts expire next June. He will not be on the next one. Thibaut Courtois has agreed a new Real Madrid contract to June 2028, according to Fabrizio Romano , who describes it as done with only the club’s statement outstanding. AS had reported on 13 September that the two sides were close to an extension on those exact terms. Madrid have not yet announced it. Where it stands Agreed, announcement pending. Romano, with AS reporting the same terms a month ago. It matters more than a goalkeeper renewal usually does, because Madrid’s summer 2027 exposure is real. Antonio Rudiger and Brahim Diaz are also into the final year of their deals, and the club has already spent heavily at the other end of the pitch, including the 140m euros on Diomande . The one piece of long-term certainty they did buy themselves came in August, when Vinicius Junior signed through to June 2032, a deal that looks rather different in a week when he has been banned for four matches. Kane leaves the door open, and takes a step back from England Bayern’s captain says there have been no talks about a new contract. He also says the idea of going home has faded. Harry Kane ’s Bayern Munich contract runs to 2027, with a release clause reported at around 67m euros. Speaking to Reuters this month, he said he is open to extending beyond it, that no talks have taken place yet, and, most notably, that his desire to return to the Premier League has “decreased”. Where it stands No negotiation under way. The player is publicly receptive, and the release clause is reported rather than confirmed by the club. The timing is interesting because Kane’s own form is not the issue and Bayern’s is. He became the fastest player to 100 Bundesliga goals, reaching the mark in 98 appearances in September’s 7-0 against Union Berlin . He has now scored in nine consecutive Champions League matches, including both of Bayern’s goals from open play and the penalty in Tuesday’s extraordinary 3-3 at Viking in Stavanger. He also provided both assists in the 2-2 at Augsburg on Saturday without scoring, after which he told DAZN it “feels more like a defeat”. Bayern are third, eleven points from five, and have not won in four weeks. A club that has historically let contracts run until the player’s leverage has evaporated is dealing with a 33-year-old centre-forward who is the only reason several of those results were not worse. Expect this one to be settled quietly and in Bayern’s favour, and expect the Premier League clubs who have been waiting for the clause to become usable to read the word “decreased” several more times. Manchester United keep answering a different question The club insists Michael Carrick is safe. Everyone briefing about January is briefing about a left-back. Neither of those is the problem. Six points from six league games is Manchester United ’s worst start since 1986/87. On Tuesday they lost 2-0 at Atletico Madrid , conceding inside a minute to Pablo Barrios and finishing with ten men after Leny Yoro was dismissed. Fabrizio Romano reported on 13 October that the club is “still giving time and confidence” to Michael Carrick , that the players remain with him, and that the results are “not acceptable”. A day later he added that no last-minute change is expected and that United have not contacted any other manager. Where it stands Carrick is backed, for now. Two tier-one reporters arrive at the same answer from opposite directions, and no successor has been approached. David Ornstein landed in the same place from the other direction: he knows of no desire to remove Carrick, but said the manager “needs to improve things” and pointed the rest of the blame at recruitment, executives and owners. He singled out Sunday’s trip to Leeds United as “massive”. Nicolo Schira has gone further, naming Leeds, Como and Bournemouth as the decisive run. Reports linking Eddie Howe and Fabian Hurzeler to the job trace back to unnamed accounts and should be treated as speculation. Antonio Conte is a different case: Romano says he would be open to a mid-season move to a historical club and would not want the Middle East, while explicitly refuting a claim that he was reaching an agreement with INEOS. On the squad, Romano says January is “too early to say” and depends on conditions he did not specify, but that a left-back would not be “crazy money”. The name that keeps recurring is Adrien Truffert of Bournemouth , whom Ornstein valued at around 60m pounds last month while suggesting a deal was more likely in the summer of 2027. Bournemouth are expected to reject January offers. United wanted Newcastle United ’s Lewis Hall in August; Hall has since signed a new contract there. Milan and Inter spend the autumn protecting what they have Two clubs with no money to spend in January are doing the next best thing, which is making sure nobody can take anything for free in June. Inter have opened renewal talks with Federico Dimarco aimed at a contract to 2030, Gazzetta dello Sport reported on 12 October. The club holds a unilateral option to 2028, so there is no cliff edge, and no agreement has been reached. At Milan , Gazzetta reported in late September that Adrien Rabiot is close to a renewal through 2030 with an option year. Nothing is official on either. Where it stands Talks opened at Inter , reported progress at Milan . Neither club has announced anything, and both reports originate with Gazzetta dello Sport. Milan’s more pressing problem is structural. Matteo Gabbia tore a left hamstring with partial tendon involvement at Sassuolo on Sunday and is out for months, with a specialist deciding between surgery and conservative treatment. A club that drew 1-1 that afternoon and sits fifth now has a January window in which a centre-back is close to compulsory. Links to specific names have circulated without attribution and are not worth printing yet. Juventus , meanwhile, are reported by Tuttosport to be considering a striker in January to support Randal Kolo Muani , whose 81st-minute header at Cagliari rescued a point and was his first Serie A goal of the season. They have the balance sheet to think about it: the board approved accounts carrying a forecast 66m euro loss on 29 September and proposed a delegation for a capital increase of up to 250m euros, with Exor confirming an advance. k: Arsenal followed Mikel Arteta's new contract to 2030 with a comeback win over Leeds and a 3-0 Champions League rout of Lille, in a week that ended with the death of Ken Friar.
x: The Weekly Arsenal Digest Everything Arsenal, every Tuesday No. 9 · Season 2026-27 Tuesday 13 October 2026 Catch-up edition, published October 26, 2026. In this edition The Lead · Transfer News · The Squad · Hale End · Arsenal Women · Off the Pitch · Gunners Abroad · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch Collapse all sections The Lead A new contract, two wins in four days, and the answer last month's defeat demanded Arsenal came back from the international break needing to prove the 3-0 defeat at Brighton was a blip. They signed their manager to 2030, came from behind to beat unbeaten Leeds United and then took Lille apart in seven second-half minutes. T he week began with paperwork. On Wednesday 7 October Arsenal confirmed that Mikel Arteta had signed a new contract, reported as a four-year deal running to 2030. His previous agreement was due to expire at the end of this season. It was the least surprising announcement of the autumn, and it was treated that way. Arteta , 44, is the longest-serving manager in the Premier League now that Pep Guardiola has left Manchester City . He arrived in December 2019, won the club's first league title in 22 years last season and took them to a Champions League final they lost to Paris Saint-Germain on penalties. “It's a privilege to commit my future to the club,” Arteta said in the club's announcement. “This club is unique, its character and the way it makes you feel.” He added that this is only the beginning of what we can achieve together . The co-chairs, Stan Kroenke and Josh Kroenke , said: It has been an incredible journey so far and we are excited for what lies ahead. Two days later, in his press conference before the Leeds game, Arteta spoke more personally. He told reporters the thing he would remember was the moment of signing: looking around the room and seeing excitement in their eyes . He named Stan and Josh Kroenke , chief executive Richard Garlick , James King and sporting director Andrea Berta . Then he closed the subject: Now I have to earn the right every single day to continue at this level, and make the most of it. He did not have to wait long to start earning it. Saturday: a crowd that told them to wake up For fifty-five minutes on Saturday, the Brighton hangover looked real. Leeds United , unbeaten and with only three league goals conceded all season, came to the Emirates for the 12:30 kick-off and did exactly what Daniel Farke 's side had done to everyone else. They sat in shape, defended the box and waited. Arsenal had one meaningful chance in the first half, a Kai Havertz header straight at James Trafford . Gabriel Gudmundsson should have put the visitors ahead just before the break and was denied by a strong save from David Raya . According to the PA Media report, one supporter shouted Wake up as the players went down the tunnel at half-time. Ten minutes after the restart, Leeds scored. Gudmundsson drove a low cross into the six-yard box, Raya could not deal with it and James Justin blasted in from close range. It was the 55th minute. The equaliser came seven minutes later and changed the afternoon. Noni Madueke , starting on the left in place of the injured Christos Tzolis , crossed to the far post. Ben White nodded the ball back across goal and Riccardo Calafiori ran in to finish from close range. It was his first goal at the Emirates. A minute later Arteta sent on three players at once: Bruno Guimaraes for Myles Lewis-Skelly , Jurrien Timber for White and Viktor Gyokeres for Havertz . It took Guimaraes seven minutes to decide the match. A quickly taken free kick was flicked between several players, Declan Rice laid it into his path and the seventy-five million pound midfielder drove it into the bottom corner from just outside the box on 70 minutes. It was his first goal at the Emirates and his second for the club. This is the level for Arsenal , every week, every game, every minute, every action that you have to be at. Mikel Arteta , after Leeds Raya also turned an Ao Tanaka drive over the bar, and Arsenal saw it out. Arteta told TNT Sports the team had come in with something to prove. We weren’t pleased about what we did against Brighton , and today was an opportunity to prove that right , he said, and of the winner: The timing, I think, the connection and the execution of it, it was a beauty. The losing manager was gracious. Arsenal is the most consistent team in Europe, one of the best in the world , Farke said, before adding that he was heartbroken and gutted for players who had deserved to travel home with points. Justin , the scorer, put it more simply: Their mentality is unbelievable. Guimaraes had been told publicly that he was not at the level required at Brighton , where he had made his only league start and been withdrawn around the hour. His answer was a goal and a promise. I felt amazing and I can't wait to score more goals now , he said. We know how tight the Premier League is, so we're very happy with the win. For a little over twenty-four hours, Arsenal were level on points with Manchester City at the top. Then City went to Anfield on Sunday and won 3-0 after Ryan Gravenberch was sent off for a second booking on 62 minutes, with Erling Haaland , Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki scoring. City have won six from six. Arsenal are three points back. Tuesday: seven minutes of football The week ended under a cloud and in a blaze. On Tuesday the club announced the death of its life president, Ken Friar , at 92. That evening the Emirates stood to applaud him before kick-off against Lille , and then watched one of the best spells of football Arsenal have produced this season. Arteta made five changes from Saturday. Guimaraes got his first Emirates start, Eberechi Eze and Gyokeres started, and Bukayo Saka , Martin Odegaard and Havertz began on the bench. For an hour it was patient and not particularly sharp. Guimaraes fired wide from close range and had a deflected shot palmed away by Berke Ozer . Mikel Merino headed at the goalkeeper. Eze , arriving on the penalty spot, shot straight at him. Lille had a goal from Ayase Ueda ruled out for offside. Then it opened up. On 64 minutes Madueke slipped in Timber , and the Dutchman dinked a finish over Ozer . Timber said afterwards that his teammate had been screaming, ‘Shoot, shoot, shoot’ as he went through. A minute later Arteta made another triple substitution: Saka for Madueke , Odegaard for Merino , Havertz for Gyokeres . On 67 minutes Guimaraes found Saka , whose low cross was turned in by Eze with a slight deflection. On 71, Odegaard slid Havertz through, Havertz cut it back and Saka curled it into the far corner. Three goals in seven minutes, from three different scorers. Sky Sports' match page recorded that Lille did not manage a shot on target all night. It was a joy to watch, the three goals were unbelievable, the connections, the timings. Mikel Arteta , after Lille Arteta was candid about the first half. He said his side's technical quality wasn't good enough to deliver moments of real threat before a positional change at half-time lifted it. The more telling line was about the season as a whole: When other aspects aren't working, we need to make sure we have a variety of ways to win football matches. It is hard not to read that as a reference to set-pieces, which have not yet produced a single corner goal this season. Lille coach Davide Ancelotti , son of the Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti , told UEFA.com: I don't think the players deserve this scoreline. His side have no points after two games, having lost to Real Betis on matchday one. Arsenal have six, and share top spot in the league phase with Barcelona and Sporting CP . Not everything about the week was clean. The team that beat Leeds lost two players in a session after the final whistle, and the attack, for all the brilliance of Tuesday, is still not converting enough of what it creates. But Arsenal entered the week with questions about their nerve after Brighton . They leave it with a manager tied down, two wins, five goals across the two games and a bench that changed both matches. Key Facts: the week in two results Saturday 10 October Arsenal 2-1 Leeds United , Premier League, Emirates Stadium. Justin 55, Calafiori 62, Guimaraes 70. Tuesday 13 October Arsenal 3-0 Lille , Champions League league phase, matchday two, Emirates Stadium. Timber 64, Eze 67, Saka 71. League Second on 15 points from six, three behind Manchester City , who have won all six. Europe Six points from six, level at the top with Barcelona and Sporting CP . Tuesday stats Possession 58 per cent to 42. Shots 16 to 4. On target 8 to 0. Sources: PA Media and AP reports of Saturday's match , Al Jazeera on Tuesday , and Arseblog News for the match statistics. The bench that won the week Two triple substitutions, and two matches turned by the players who came off the bench. On Saturday Arteta sent on three players at 63 minutes, and one of them, Guimaraes , scored the winner seven minutes later. On Tuesday the three he sent on at 65 minutes were involved in both goals that followed inside six minutes, Saka with a goal and an assist and Havertz with an assist. Arteta called the timing of Tuesday's change instinctive. I felt it was the right moment to make the triple substitution with the way the game was panning out , he said, and he spread the credit: that's credit to the starters, and as well the ones who come in to create those moments. It is a striking contrast with the start of the season, and with Arsenal Women, whose problem this autumn has been exactly the opposite: games drifting away the moment the changes are made. For the men, at least this week, the bench was the weapon. Transfer News After the manager, the midfielder: Rice closes in on a new deal Within hours of Arteta 's extension, the BBC reported that Declan Rice was close to committing his long-term future too. The window is shut, so the business this week was about keeping people rather than buying them. On the evening of 7 October, BBC Sport reported that Rice was close to agreeing a new long-term contract. Talks, first reported by the BBC in March, were said to be at an advanced stage. Rice is 27 and joined from West Ham United in July 2023 for an initial one hundred million pounds, with five million more in add-ons. He has made 165 appearances for Arsenal . His current deal runs to 2028 with a club option for a further year. The BBC said he is reported to earn around two hundred and forty thousand pounds a week, and that the new contract would substantially raise that, bringing him level with Bukayo Saka , believed to earn about three hundred and fifty thousand. The following day Fabrizio Romano added his stamp. Arsenal are closing in on new deal for Declan Rice after Mikel Arteta, plan 100% confirmed , he posted, adding that Rice has already decided to stay and sign soon with final details of new deal now being discussed . No length or salary figure has been officially confirmed, and nothing had been signed by the end of the week. There was a footnote on fitness, too. Rice was left out of England's most recent camp, which Arteta described as load management . We have to manage him because he's had a few issues since he came back from the World Cup , the manager said on Friday. Rice then started both games this week and laid on Arsenal 's winner against Leeds . Arseblog News also noted that Martin Odegaard is reportedly in talks over new terms. That one remains a single line in the reporting rather than a story with detail. Nusa, again, and a door that stays shut The January left-winger search has a familiar name and a familiar obstacle. Last week's edition reported the claim that Antonio Nusa of RB Leipzig is Arsenal 's top January target. On 7 October FourFourTwo , citing the German outlet Fussball News, reported that Arsenal are working on formalising an offer for the Norway winger. That is the German-side corroboration this digest said it was waiting for. It came with a large caveat. The same report said Leipzig have no interest in letting one of their best players leave in the middle of the season. No fee has been reported. Transfermarkt values him at forty-five million euros. Stage: concrete interest, no bid. The logic has not changed. Arsenal sold Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard in the summer, Tzolis is injured again and Madueke was the left-sided starter against Leeds by default. He then set up the opener against Lille , which complicates last week's narrative about him drifting out of the picture. Contract Watch SIGNED Mikel Arteta , head coach, to 2030. Announced 7 October. His previous deal was due to expire in June. He has also extended in 2022 and 2024. CLOSE Declan Rice , midfielder. BBC Sport and Fabrizio Romano report a long-term deal is close. Current terms run to 2028 plus a club option. TALKS Martin Odegaard , captain. Reportedly in talks over new terms. No detail. PENDING Nicolas Jover , set-piece coach. Talks led by Andrea Berta , as reported last week. Nothing new this week. Compiled from BBC Sport, Arsenal.com and Arseblog News. Contract lengths are as reported unless announced by the club. The Rumour Mill A quiet week for January talk, which is how international breaks usually end. Antonio Nusa , RB Leipzig . As above. Stage: concrete interest, with the selling club publicly reluctant. And the sale question. Last week this digest said a Madueke sale funding a left-winger was the version of January that fitted the club's finances. A week later Madueke has started two games and assisted once. If he keeps doing that, the sale half of that equation gets harder, and the January budget gets tighter. The Squad Two ankles, one warm-down and a scene nobody had seen in seven years Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi were hurt in a small-sided game after the Leeds win. Hincapie 's looks the more serious. The injuries that cost Arsenal two players this week did not happen in a match. After Saturday's early kick-off, Arteta sent the substitutes and unused players back out for a session of small-sided games, a routine for players who had not had enough minutes. Hincapie , who had come on for Calafiori in the 82nd minute, and Zubimendi , an unused substitute, both hurt their ankles. Supporters filmed Hincapie in obvious distress. PA Media reported that he was carried off by the third-choice goalkeeper, Illan Meslier . Arteta confirmed both injuries on Monday. In two very unfortunate actions we lost two players. Not great , he said. Both ankles. They're both going to miss tomorrow's match for sure. Of Hincapie , he added: Piero's one looks a little bit more serious, but we have to wait and see. He also said: It has never happened in seven years that I have been here. The small-sided games, he explained, had been planned for the following day anyway. When you play these kinds of small-sided games, there is contact, and these things happen. After the Lille match he put a rough frame on the Hincapie absence: It will be a matter of weeks for him, we don't know exactly how many. For Hincapie it is another interruption. Sports Mole counted sixteen club and country matches missed since he arrived from Bayer Leverkusen , through two groin problems and two muscular ones. For Zubimendi it is a rarity: before Saturday he had not been injured in an Arsenal shirt. The returns: Havertz, Konsa and Rice all started The good news was that the break's walking wounded were fit. Kai Havertz , who had come off with what Arteta called a muscular injury on Germany duty, started against Leeds and assisted the third goal against Lille . Ezri Konsa , released by England with a quad problem, played every minute of both games. Arteta said on Friday that communication with the England camp had been good, and listed Hincapie , Cristhian Mosquera and Max Dowman as back from their own problems. Tzolis , injured with Greece, was the one who would miss a few weeks . Asked if his was the worst of the three, Arteta said: Yeah, he's not available. Saliba: back on the grass, still weeks away William Saliba trained individually on the grass at London Colney on Monday, the first public sighting of him outdoors since the back injury that he carried through the World Cup and aggravated in France's semi-final against Spain . In the next few weeks we can start to introduce him with the team , Arteta said. Asked whether that meant before or after the November international break, he answered: We're still talking about weeks. Set-pieces: none from a corner yet The most revealing number of the week came from the manager himself. Arsenal , whose corner routines set a Premier League record last season, have not scored from a corner in this one. Arteta said on Friday that his side had created better corner situations than last year and should have scored several. On the league's tighter refereeing of contact in the box, he said the team must adapt to what is now allowed, and that the change opens another window for different ways to score. On Monday he widened the point. He called the attacking output before the break better than any other year , but said: We need to be more clinical now to finish more actions. And on mentality, with Brighton in mind: We have to be emotionally dominant regardless of what the context is. Availability: end of the week OUT Piero Hincapie , ankle, a matter of weeks . Martin Zubimendi , ankle, scanned on Monday. Christos Tzolis , hamstring, a few weeks. William Saliba , back, individual work on grass. BACK Kai Havertz started against Leeds and came off the bench against Lille . Ezri Konsa played 180 minutes. Declan Rice started both. Cristhian Mosquera was on the bench against Lille . WATCH Max Dowman , fit again after his England under-19 knock, made a cameo from the 85th minute against Lille . Compiled from Arseblog News , Sports Mole and PA Media. Hale End A Champions League cameo, a Messi endorsement and still no under-21 win Max Dowman got five minutes in Europe. The under-21s twice came from behind. The under-18s kept winning. Max Dowman 's week ended on the Emirates pitch. Fit again after the knock that cut short his England under-19 camp, the sixteen-year-old replaced Eze on 85 minutes against Lille and had two late shots blocked. Two other academy players, Ceadach O'Neill and Marli Salmon , were among the substitutes. Dowman also turned up in an advert. Lionel Messi named him as a future star in an Adidas campaign, and Arteta was asked about it on Monday. He said Dowman has something special and praised his movement and touch, while noting that Messi 's judgement of talent is rather good. Myles Lewis-Skelly , nominated for the Golden Boy award last week for the second time, started both senior games, alongside Rice in midfield against Leeds and again against Lille . Under-21s: still waiting for a win David Horseman 's under-21s are still waiting for their first Premier League 2 win. On Saturday at Meadow Park Sunderland 's Trey Samuel-Ogunsuyi scored twice. James Scanlon , who scored for Gibraltar during the break, got one for Arsenal , and Andre Harriman-Annous , who made his England under-20 debut in the same window, rescued a point with a late equaliser set up by substitute Teshaun Murisa . Sunderland finished with ten men after Ajibola Alese was shown a second yellow card. Arseblog News reported that Salmon captained the side for almost an hour on his return from injury. Academy results via Arseblog News. Fixture dates via FotMob. Arsenal Women No match, three more injuries, and Russo and Stanway shine for England The WSL took a week off. Renee Slegers 's squad did not get any healthier during it. There was no club football for Arsenal Women this week, which after a 4-2 defeat at Manchester City and a collapsed 2-0 lead in Paris might have been welcome. It was not restful. The break produced three fresh fitness problems and left Slegers without her most creative player for the next block of games. Mariona Caldentey pulled out of Spain's friendly double-header against the United States with a hamstring injury picked up at the Etihad. Arseblog News reported she was due to see a specialist and looked likely to miss the whole run of matches before the late-November international break. Selina Cerci withdrew from Germany's squad for friendlies against Japan and Australia. The German federation's website said simply that she was unavailable due to knee problems . She has played forty minutes for Arsenal this season. In Sweden, Smilla Holmberg sprained her foot in training. Sweden's head of performance, Niklas Egnell , said: She sprained her foot during yesterday's training session. That leaves Slegers , already short of a forward who can stretch a low block, without the player she has been using wide to create. The WSL resumes on Saturday 17 October against newly promoted Birmingham City at the Emirates. The Lionesses: 8-1 and through to the decider The Arsenal players who did go away came back in form. In the first leg of England's World Cup play-off on Friday, at the Pankritio Stadium in Crete, Georgia Stanway opened the scoring before half-time and Alessia Russo added the third after Maya Le Tissier 's goal, in a 3-1 win. Sarina Wiegman told ITV: We started well, they started very aggressively too, but we stayed calm. She added, of the late Greek goal: I'm not happy with the goal we conceded. The second leg at the King Power Stadium on Tuesday night was a rout. Russo scored early, from a Lauren James pass, and again on 75 minutes. Stanway headed in on 34 minutes. James scored twice. England won 5-0, 8-1 on aggregate , and now play Ukraine in the final round of the play-offs for a place at the 2027 World Cup. For Russo , who scored in the defeat at the Etihad nine days earlier, that is three goals in two games for her country. For Stanway , signed from Bayern Munich in the summer, it was a goal in each leg. If Slegers is looking for something to build on, the in-form centre-forward and the midfielder arriving in the box is not a bad place to start. Where they stand League Tenth in the WSL, five points from five matches, one win, two draws, two defeats. No league win since the opening day. Goals Four scored, six conceded. Manchester City lead with fifteen points from five. Europe Unbeaten in the Champions League league phase after a 1-0 win over HB Koge and the 2-2 in Paris. Benfica visit on 28 October. Injuries Mariona Caldentey (hamstring), Selina Cerci (knee), Smilla Holmberg (foot sprain, on international duty). Standings as of the start of the international break, via Soccer News . No WSL matches were played between 7 and 13 October. Off the Pitch Ken Friar, 1934 to 2026: the boy who chased a ball and stayed eighty years The club's life president died aged 92. He saw the men's team win twenty-five major honours under seven managers, the last of them in May. On Tuesday 13 October Arsenal announced the death of Ken Friar OBE. It is with profound sadness that we announce the death of Life President Ken Friar OBE , the club's statement began. It went on to say that no one has had an influence on the club quite like Mr Friar . His story is the kind that clubs no longer produce. He was born in Islington on 13 August 1934. In 1946, aged twelve, he was retrieving a ball outside Highbury when the manager, George Allison , noticed him. He was given a job running messages from the box office for half a crown a week, and joined the permanent staff in 1950. He became club secretary in 1973, succeeding Bob Wall , and managing director in 1983, appointed by Peter Hill-Wood . As managing director he handled player and manager contracts. With director Danny Fiszman , he was central to the move from Highbury to the Emirates, which opened in 2006. He received an OBE for services to football in 2000 and the freedom of Islington in 2004. He stepped down from the board in 2020, after seventy-four years of service, and became life president. The bridge that links the stadium with the surrounding streets is named after him, and a statue at its entrance shows him as a boy playing football outside Highbury. This week, scarves and flowers were laid there. It's a really sad day for everybody that loves Arsenal Football Club or anybody that has come across him. Mikel Arteta , after Lille The Emirates held a moment of reflection before the Lille game and stood to applaud. Afterwards Arteta said : I had the privilege, the honour to meet him, to spend time with him, to learn from him. Former players followed. Tony Adams called him the epitomisation of all that Arsenal stands for . David Seaman said: Ken Friar is an Arsenal icon and his achievements will never be forgotten. Charlie George , speaking to Arsenal.com, said: He knew everything and every person in the building. Supporters' groups joined in. The Lead The clock started at 7pm on Thursday Manchester City have appealed. The verdict stands until a new panel says otherwise, the punishment has not been set, and the timetable for both is now the most important document in English football. T he deadline was Friday. Manchester City did not wait for it. The club confirmed on Thursday 1 October that it had lodged its appeal at 7pm that evening, against the independent commission that found it guilty of serious breaches of Premier League financial rules across nine seasons, from 2009/10 to 2017/18. The appeal went to the Chair of the Premier League’s Judicial Panel, ITV News reported . The league says the Appeal Board hearing will stay private and confidential until its outcome can be published. City ’s statement repeated the line it has held since the verdict. The commission’s opinion, it said, contains “clear material errors of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.” It added, without qualification: “The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League.” “This disciplinary case, and this decision, are the most significant in Premier League history.” Richard Masters , Premier League chief executive What the appeal is actually about The commission found that sponsorship income booked by the club was, in large part, not paid by the sponsors at all. NBC Sports’ summary of the findings puts it at around 87 per cent of the reported commercial income over the period, supplied instead through the owners, the Abu Dhabi United Group. City ’s central argument, as ITV describes it, is that government funding through the Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Court helped sponsors meet their obligations. The commission rejected that account as a narrative built after the fact. That is the ground the appeal will be fought on: not whether money moved, but whose money it was. The timetable, and why it matters The Premier League handbook says an appeal hearing must finish within twelve weeks of being lodged. Counted from 1 October, that lands on Christmas Eve. The appeal panel then has 30 days to rule, which points to a decision in January. There are two catches. Sports Mole noted that it is unclear whether these fast-track rules apply to a case that began before they were introduced. And City ’s chief executive Ferran Soriano has warned that the process could take considerably longer. Route and key facts The Premier League v Manchester City The charges Serious breaches of financial rules over nine seasons, 2009/10 to 2017/18, plus charges of failing to co-operate with the investigation. The verdict Guilty of all the serious-breach charges and most of the co-operation charges. Communicated on 24 September, redacted decision published on 29 September. The appeal Lodged at 7pm on Thursday 1 October, a day inside the deadline. Heard in private by a fresh panel. The clock Hearing to finish within twelve weeks, around 24 December. Ruling within 30 days of the hearing, so likely January 2027. The sanction A separate hearing, with no date set. City can appeal any sanction too. Waiting in the wings Arsenal , Liverpool , Manchester United and Tottenham , who reserved the right to claim compensation in 2024. The Football Association is reviewing the findings. The punishment nobody has priced yet The sanction is a separate process, and nobody has said when it will be heard. Several Premier League clubs want it settled before the end of this season, according to The Sun as relayed by Sports Mole, and believe the new fast-track rules should apply. The precedents are small next to the scale of this case. Everton lost eight points across two profitability cases in 2023/24. Nottingham Forest lost four. Those were single-season accounting breaches; this is nine seasons and a finding of deliberate concealment. The Football Association has added another layer. It said it is reviewing the commission’s findings, that the decision has “significant implications for the integrity of the game”, and that it may act where appropriate. It will say nothing more while proceedings continue. The second front: money Four clubs preserved the right to sue back in 2024: Arsenal , Manchester United , Liverpool and Tottenham . The Independent has reported they are planning to act, with a combined claim of around 200m pounds discussed. The Times put the potential exposure to rival claims at more than 100m pounds. None of that can start yet. Legal action can only begin once the case and its appeals are finished, which is another reason the January date matters so much. And the football carries on Through all of this, City are top. Enzo Maresca ’s side have won all five league games and lead on fifteen points. Their first match back from the break is at Anfield on Sunday, against Liverpool . That is the strange shape of the autumn. The club playing the best football in England is also the club whose place in the league depends on a hearing held in private before Christmas. Every point City win between now and January is a point that may or may not count for anything. The bill for the longest break in memory Club football in Europe’s big leagues has been dark since 20 September. As it ends, the clubs are counting what four internationals in one window cost them. FIFA’s new calendar folded two international windows into one this autumn. National teams played up to four matches between 24 September and 6 October, and the big European leagues paused for three weekends. It returns this Friday. Niko Kovac spoke for a lot of coaches on Wednesday. “Those four games were definitely too many for me. The break was too long,” the Borussia Dortmund coach said, in comments carried by dpa . His point was not only about injuries. “We also had two and a half weeks with no rhythm at all,” he said. That matters for a side that won its first four league games and leads the Bundesliga. “When you have to play four games, there’s a lot of travel, and the squads are relatively small.” Niko Kovac , Borussia Dortmund coach Dortmund ’s own list shows why. Konstantinos Karetsas and Daniel Svensson came back with colds. Nico Schlotterbeck hurt an ankle in Germany training and is doubtful for Friday. Julian Ryerson is nursing a knock from a collision. In Barcelona the worry is Raphinha . He left the Brazil squad early with muscular swelling in his right thigh after the win over Australia . Early signs were not serious, but Marca reported that Hansi Flick will not rush him back. The reason is last season. Raphinha hurt the same thigh on Brazil duty in September 2025, his return was accelerated, and he broke down again. He then missed 58 days and 13 matches, Sports Mole recalled . Napoli had problems before the break and have more after it. Tuttomercatoweb reported on Wednesday that Antonio Vergara has a strain of the right soleus and will miss at least four or five matches. Mati Olivera came back from Uruguay with a groin problem. Costantino Favasuli , hurt with Italy ’s under-21s, is probably out until after the November break. They join a list that already included Alex Meret , Alessandro Buongiorno , Scott McTominay and Frank Anguissa . That leaves Massimiliano Allegri with nine matches between 10 October and 4 November, and a squad that is thinner than it has been all season. Elsewhere the damage had been done earlier in the window. Real Madrid diagnosed Kylian Mbappe with a hyperextension of the back of his left knee, picked up while scoring for France against Turkiye , and said he would be out for two weeks or more. Carvajal picks Getafe , if La Liga allows it A six-time European champion with Real Madrid has said yes to a club on the southern edge of the city. The last word belongs to the league’s accountants. Dani Carvajal is 34 and has been a free agent since his Real Madrid contract ended on 30 June. He has not played an official match since. This week he chose his next club, and it is Getafe . This week, Getafe president Angel Torres confirmed that Carvajal had passed a medical and that the agreement with the player was closed. Fabrizio Romano reported a verbal agreement too, citing ABC. Where it stands Agreed with the player, medical passed. Getafe still need La Liga to approve the registration under the club’s squad-cost limit, and Torres said it cannot be called final until then. The obstacle is the spending cap. Getafe operate with far less room than the clubs Carvajal spent his career with, and Bordalas admitted as much in September. Even a free transfer has to fit under the limit, and that is now a conversation between the club and the league. Bournemouth put up the closed sign for Scott Chelsea are expected to come back for Alex Scott . Bournemouth have already given their answer. A week earlier, the journalist Dean Jones had reported the same stance for Flashscore and put Bournemouth ’s valuation at around 110m euros. Treat that number as an estimate, not an asking price. Where it stands Concrete interest, no sale sanctioned. Two separate reports agree on Bournemouth ’s position.
