k: Arsenal return from a three week international break second in the table with eight goals in five games and the sharpest question of their season still unanswered.
x: The Weekly Arsenal Digest Everything Arsenal, every Tuesday No. 8 · Season 2026-27 Tuesday 6 October 2026 In this edition The Lead · Transfer News · The Squad · Hale End · Arsenal Women · Off the Pitch · Gunners Abroad · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch Collapse all sections The Lead Twenty-one days to fix the thing nobody has fixed Arsenal come back from the longest break of their season second in the table and short of goals. Leeds United arrive at the Emirates on Saturday unbeaten, and the champions still cannot say where the next one is coming from. T he last competitive football Arsenal played was on 19 September, and it was awful. Brighton and Hove Albion pressed them man for man, watched them panic and won 3-0. Pascal Gross curled in from distance after half an hour. Charalampos Kostoulas struck fifteen seconds after Bukayo Saka had been denied at the other end. Chema Andres headed in a Gross corner nine minutes after the break. Mikel Arteta said his side did not respect the game and were extremely poor technically . Then the international calendar swallowed three weeks whole. The table says the damage was contained. Arsenal are second on twelve points from five, three behind Manchester City , who have won all five. Four goals conceded is championship-grade. The problem is at the other end. Eight scored is the lowest in the top seven and exactly half of Brighton 's sixteen. It is not hard to see why. Gabriel Martinelli went to Al Hilal for a club-record sixty million pounds in August, Leandro Trossard to Besiktas , Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona . Christos Tzolis , bought from Club Brugge for thirty-four million as Trossard 's replacement, is out with a hamstring strain. Kai Havertz pulled a hamstring for Germany and is a doubt. Noni Madueke has drifted so far out of the picture that Atletico Madrid and Juventus are watching. And Viktor Gyokeres , the centre-forward, has five Arsenal appearances and no goals. We have to make sure we learn the lesson because this can’t happen again. Mikel Arteta , after Brighton What Arsenal do have is the thing that won them the league. Nicolas Jover 's routines produced a Premier League record from corners last season, and the league responded over the summer with fresh instruction to referees to clamp down on holding and wrestling in the box at set-pieces. Five games in, the champions' first-choice route to goal is being refereed differently and their open-play alternative has been sold. That is why January already feels load-bearing. Saturday is harder than the names suggest. Leeds United are fifth and unbeaten, two wins and three draws, with three goals conceded in five matches. Only Brighton have a better defensive record. They are the opposite of the fixture Arsenal need: a low block with a tidy structure, against a side with no left winger and a striker without a goal. Arteta 's questions are not about shape. They are about who plays in front of Gyokeres , and whether Eberechi Eze or Dowman is trusted to unpick an organised defence. Behind that, the defence is a jigsaw. William Saliba has not played since July, when he came off in the first half of France's World Cup semi-final against Spain with a back problem he had carried for weeks. L'Equipe report he is targeting November. Ezri Konsa , the fifty-one million pound answer to that absence, was released by England with a quad complaint after ninety minutes against both Spain and Croatia . Gabriel Magalhaes and Piero Hincapie can cover, but a 12:30 kick-off on the first weekend back is exactly when a patched back four gets found out. Arsenal 's league season: 3-0 Coventry City , 1-0 at Aston Villa , 2-1 Chelsea , 2-0 Sunderland , 0-3 at Brighton . They also beat Manchester City 3-0 in the Community Shield, won 1-0 at Napoli and knocked out Ipswich Town 4-2 in the Carabao Cup. The record-breaker who cannot score for Arsenal Viktor Gyokeres spent the break rewriting the Nations League record book. He returns to a club where he has not scored all season. Earlier this week in Bucharest he scored the only goal of a 1-0 win over Romania , pouncing on the rebound after Sebastian Nanasi 's shot came off the post. It was his seventh consecutive Nations League match with a goal, a competition record , past Aleksandar Mitrovic and Benjamin Sesko , and his twenty-fifth for Sweden, moving him ahead of Marcus Berg . He had scored against Bosnia and Herzegovina on 3 October too. Two columns tell the story: for Sweden four appearances and four goals, for Arsenal five appearances and none. Sofascore rated him 6.5 against Manchester City , 6.4 against Chelsea , 6.6 at Napoli , 6.2 at Ipswich Town , 6.5 at Brighton . The uncomfortable reading is that this is a supply problem rather than a finishing one: Arsenal , with Martinelli and Trossard sold and Saka carrying the width almost alone, give him possession and few crosses worth attacking. Transfer News The winger hunt is already on, and Leipzig is where it starts Arsenal did not sign a left-sided attacker in the summer. Five games into a title defence, the January search has a name attached to it. David Ornstein set the frame before the season began. Asked in a Q and A for The Athletic whether Arsenal would sign an attacker in January, he said: I could see something happening because they wanted to, I thought they needed to, in the summer and they didn't. He noted the club has money but operates close to UEFA's financial limits. Summer pursuits of Vinicius Junior , Julian Alvarez and Morgan Rogers all came to nothing. On Tuesday a name arrived. CaughtOffside's Ahad Shaukat reported , citing sources close to the agents industry, that Antonio Nusa of RB Leipzig is now Arsenal 's top January target, with Andrea Berta preparing a fresh approach after the club looked at him in the summer and moved on. Nusa is twenty-one, a Norway international, and exactly the profile Arsenal no longer have: a left-sided dribbler who can beat a man. Ole Werner , his coach at Leipzig , has said of him: He is a player who will be world class in the near future. Mind the certainty tier: a single-sourced report of concrete interest, not advanced talks, with no fee attached and no Leipzig -side corroboration in the German media yet, which is usually where a deal like this surfaces first. What makes it worth reporting is that it fits Arsenal 's stated need. The alternative on the same list, Kenan Yildiz of Juventus at around eighty-five million pounds, is a January fantasy rather than a January plan. Madueke is drifting, and Europe has noticed One goal, a shrinking role and two Champions League clubs watching. Noni Madueke is in the Arsenal Champions League squad and barely in the team. He has one goal and a role that has contracted as Arteta has leaned on Saka and Eze , and Sports Mole reported this week that Atletico Madrid and Juventus are both monitoring him ahead of January, with Arsenal braced for bids. Twelve clubs, one sixteen-year-old, and a decision Arteta keeps deferring Max Dowman scored twice at Ipswich Town , was called up by England and sent off by England under-19s inside three weeks. Dowman scored twice in the 4-2 Carabao Cup win at Ipswich Town, is the highest-rated player in the under-21 side and already has two senior goals, more than Gyokeres . Reporting in late September put loan enquiries into double figures, more than twelve approaches, with Arteta publicly open-minded about letting him go for regular minutes. He assisted and was then sent off for England under-19s against the United States on Friday, then withdrew with an impact injury, having been named in Thomas Tuchel 's senior England group before being released alongside Konsa . A sale funding a purchase is the only version of January that fits all three. If Madueke 's situation hardens into a bid, expect the Nusa story to accelerate. The Squad A back four held together, and a manager committing to five more years The break cost Arsenal two forwards and returned four fit players. Meanwhile Arteta and his entire coaching staff are being tied to 2030. Arsenal lost Christos Tzolis to a hamstring strain inside twenty minutes of Greece's 2-2 draw with the Netherlands , reported at two to three weeks, which takes out Saturday, Lille and probably Nottingham Forest . They lost Kai Havertz to a hamstring problem in the 1-1 draw between the Netherlands and Germany, Jurgen Klopp 's first game in charge of the Germans, with the German federation calling it a muscle strain and Klopp hoping he would be relatively quickly available again . They also nearly lost the centre-back they bought to fix a centre-back problem. Ezri Konsa played ninety minutes against Spain and ninety against Croatia carrying a quad complaint and was sent home before Tuesday's game with Czechia . Thomas Tuchel put it plainly: He played versus Spain, which made it worse. He tried everything for Croatia and gave the green light. He got another hit on the quad, and it caused some light trauma. Against that, four returns: Ben White (groin), Piero Hincapie (muscular), Cristhian Mosquera (hamstring, out since late August) and Declan Rice , held out of the England squad and rested in Dubai. Selection: the shape of a thin attack If Havertz does not make it, the options for a 12:30 kick-off against the division's second-best defence are Gyokeres through the middle, Saka right, Eberechi Eze and Martin Odegaard in the creative positions, and a choice on the left between Noni Madueke , out of the picture, and Max Dowman , sixteen and coming off a red card and a knock. Mikel Merino is the hybrid who gives height in the box. Set-pieces, and the contracts that follow Arsenal 's dead-ball operation was the biggest competitive advantage in English football last season, producing a Premier League record from corners. Over the summer the league instructed officials to take a stricter line on holding and wrestling in the penalty area at set-pieces. Which makes the contract news interesting. Nicolas Jover is in talks over a new deal, and Daily Cannon reported on Tuesday that Andrea Berta is leading the negotiation personally. Arsenal's staff and players remain very much aligned on the value of set-pieces, and the club are willing to recognise that with a good contract , the report said. Above him, Mikel Arteta has agreed a four-year contract expected to run to June 2030, first reported by Sami Mokbel for the BBC in late September and corroborated by ESPN and the Irish Times, with Fabrizio Romano adding it carries a rise on his existing salary of around ten million pounds a year plus bonuses. The agreement remains verbal and formally unannounced. The Athletic reported the whole coaching staff will sign for the same four years: Albert Stuivenberg , Jover , Inaki Cana , Miguel Molina and, on enhanced terms, Gabriel Heinze . Arsenal Women Tenth, four goals in five, and a manager insisting she still has the board Arsenal have surrendered leads in three of their last four matches. The expected-goals numbers say the problem starts the moment Renee Slegers makes a substitution. This is the second-worst start to a Women's Super League season in Arsenal 's history. They are not being outplayed. They are being out-finished and out-lasted. One win in five, two draws, two defeats, five points, four goals scored and six conceded, tenth in a fourteen-team league. Manchester City lead on fifteen. Sunday at the Etihad was the clearest version yet. Lisa Baum put Arsenal ahead on forty-three. Lauren Hemp equalised in first-half stoppage time. Alessia Russo curled Arsenal back in front five minutes after the break. Then Kika Casparaji levelled on sixty-three, Hemp scored again on seventy-two and Georgia Shaw added a fourth on eighty-four. Manchester City 4-2 Arsenal , from a position of control, for the second time in a week. The first time was in Paris. Arsenal led Paris FC 2-0 in the Champions League on 30 September and drew 2-2, with Leah Williamson conceding a penalty . Slegers did not attend the post-match press conference, later explaining that it was important to spend time with the players after the game . They get immediate effect when they make their changes. We haven’t had the same effect as last season. Renee Slegers , after Manchester City Tim Stillman 's analysis for Arseblog put numbers on it. Against Paris FC , Arsenal were 2-0 up having generated 1.3 expected goals; over the following forty minutes of substitutions that rose only to 1.7, and they conceded twice in the final eighteen minutes. Against HB Koge the xG line totally flatlined between the 65th and 85th minutes . The full piece is worth reading . Stillman 's diagnosis is a squad-profile problem. Geraldine Reuteler , signed from Eintracht Frankfurt after a year of pursuit, has barely been used. Selina Cerci has four appearances totalling fifty-nine minutes. Mariona Caldentey is played wide, which fields four midfielders and leaves Arsenal with nobody to stretch a low block. Some of this is the cost of the most aggressive overhaul in the club's modern history. Seven players arrived and thirteen left . In came Georgia Stanway from Bayern Munich , Ona Batlle from Barcelona , Misa Rodriguez from Real Madrid , Lisa Baum from RB Leipzig , Isabella Damm from Brondby , plus Reuteler and Cerci . Out went Beth Mead to Manchester City after nine years, Katie McCabe to Chelsea , Victoria Pelova to Tottenham Hotspur , Laia Codina to West Ham United and Manuela Zinsberger to Borussia Dortmund . That is a rebuild, not a refresh. Slegers was unambiguous about her position on Sunday. She told reporters there is a strong togetherness and I've really felt [the board's] support , naming Clare Wheatley , Richard Garlick , James King and Jodie Taylor , and added: I believe in the potential that we possess. She is the manager who won the Champions League in 2025 after taking over as interim. She has earned time. Europe is salvageable. A 1-0 win over HB Koge and the 2-2 in Paris leaves Arsenal unbeaten in the league phase, with Benfica at home on 28 October, Barcelona away on 11 November, OL Lyonnes at home on 19 November and Inter away in December. Off the Pitch Arsenal will not be building a bigger stadium After months of speculation about 80,000 seats and a temporary move to Wembley, the club has chosen renovation over reconstruction. Arteta was one of the voices against. Arsenal have ruled out a major expansion of Emirates Stadium. The decision was communicated at an Arsenal Advisory Board meeting, where co-chair Josh Kroenke and chief executive Richard Garlick said the club had shared a commitment to continued evolution of Emirates Stadium, rather than a huge scale masterplan . Arseblog News reported the detail and the decision was confirmed elsewhere the same week. The option on the table was a rebuild taking capacity to around eighty thousand, which would have required Arsenal to play home matches at Wembley during construction. Mikel Arteta opposed that, concerned about severing the connection between team and supporters at the moment the club had rebuilt it. Capacity stays at 60,704. Instead come smaller things: expanded hospitality and retail, a catering identity called 1886 by Arsenal with Legends Global, 5G and stadium-wide connectivity, seat refurbishment and concourse work. Safe standing is already operational in the Clock End, with the North Bank to follow in 2027-28. The commercial logic is not subtle. Arsenal 's matchday income passed one hundred and fifty-four million pounds in 2024-25, and premium hospitality yields several times general admission per seat. It is also, for anyone who has spent a decade on a season-ticket waiting list, the end of a hope. The verdict that landed while Arsenal were away Manchester City were found guilty of more than a hundred financial breaches on 29 September. Arsenal are one of four clubs reported to be preparing a claim. On 29 September an independent commission found Manchester City guilty of all the serious charges brought by the Premier League, covering 2009-10 to 2017-18. The commission concluded the club had arranged what it described as sham contracts and used schemes to inflate revenues artificially, with figures above nine hundred million pounds cited in reporting of the findings. Manchester City say they are disappointed and surprised, maintain the opinion contains clear material errors, and have appealed. No sanction has been imposed. Guilt and punishment are separate stages. Sky Sports reported that rival clubs do not expect Manchester City to be in the top flight next season if the appeal fails, and that a single-season points deduction is widely regarded as insufficient. The appeal is expected before Christmas. The Arsenal angle is twofold. First, money. Arsenal joined Manchester United , Liverpool and Tottenham Hotspur in reserving the right to seek compensation in November 2024, because the Limitation Act allows six years for breach-of-contract claims. The Independent has since reported the four clubs are now planning to launch an action, with combined claims potentially exceeding two hundred million pounds. Arsenal finished fifth in 2016-17 and were runners-up to Manchester City in 2022-23 and 2023-24. Second, the table. Manchester City are top with a perfect record and Arsenal are three points behind. Any sanction applied this season would reshape a title race Arsenal are currently losing by the margin of one game. k: An independent commission found Manchester City guilty of serious financial breaches across nine seasons, and the sanction is still to come.
x: The Weekly Soccer Digest World football, told properly Wednesday Edition · 30 September 2026 · Arsenal covered separately In this edition The Lead · Transfer News · Around the Leagues · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead Guilty: the verdict that rewrites nine seasons of English football An independent commission has found Manchester City guilty of serious financial wrongdoing across nine seasons, ruling that the club inflated its revenues and cut its costs by more than £900 million through contracts it called commercial and the panel called sham. The sanction is still to come. Everything about the Premier League now bends around it. The document that landed on Tuesday afternoon runs to a redacted core decision and a conclusion that leaves almost no room to stand. An independent commission, appointed under Premier League rules, found Manchester City guilty of every charge relating to serious breaches of the league's financial regulations across nine seasons, from 2009/10 to 2017/18. It also upheld three of the four charges alleging that the club failed to co-operate with the investigation that produced them. In the panel's words, by its conduct the club clearly intended to circumvent the rules, and it made concerted efforts to stop and frustrate the league's inquiry. The mechanism, as the commission describes it, was not a rounding error or an accounting disagreement. Commercial partners were required to pay only part of the sponsorship fees that appeared in the club's books, with the remainder funded by Abu Dhabi United Group Investment and Development, the ownership vehicle. Other arrangements allowed costs to be recorded at artificially low levels. Between them, the panel found, these structures inflated revenue and suppressed expenditure by more than £900 million, roughly $1.2 billion, across the period in question. Accounts were misstated. Auditors and regulators were kept from the real picture. Both Premier League and UEFA spending limits were breached, substantially. Premier League chief executive Richard Masters put the finding in a single sentence: the core decision, he said, details how the club systematically broke Premier League rules for nearly a decade. That is the sort of language a regulator uses when it believes it has won. “By its conduct the club clearly intended to circumvent the PL Rules.” The independent commission, in the redacted core decision How the public came to know is its own story, and not a flattering one for the league. The commission's decision was communicated on Thursday 24 September. Club executives were briefed at a shareholders' meeting the same day and asked to sign non-disclosure agreements. Within about a day the substance was in The Guardian, The Athletic, the BBC, The Times and on Sky Sports. The Premier League then published its redacted core decision on Tuesday 29 September, five days after the parties who stand to claim compensation had already been told the outcome. Several outlets have characterised the ruling as 114 of 115 charges proven; the league's own statement simply says all charges of serious breach, plus three of four on co-operation. City's response was defiant and carefully lawyered. The club said it was disappointed and surprised, insisted a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence supports its positions, and declared that it would be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums. The opinion, it argued, contains clear material errors of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe. It noted pointedly that it had respected due process for eight years on the understanding that the Premier League board would behave as an impartial regulator free from partisan influence. Chief executive Ferran Soriano took no questions. The Case: Route to the Verdict Origin Football Leaks documents obtained by Rui Pinto and published from 2018 triggered scrutiny of the club's sponsorship structures. UEFA A two-year European ban imposed in February 2020 was overturned at the Court of Arbitration for Sport, which left a €10 million fine in place. Charged February 2023, after a four-year Premier League investigation, with more than 100 alleged breaches. Hearing A closed hearing before an independent commission, held over a period of months. Verdict Communicated Thursday 24 September 2026. Reported publicly by Friday 25 September. Redacted core decision published Tuesday 29 September. Appeal window City have until Friday 2 October to appeal to a fresh three-person commission under Section W of the rules. There is no route to CAS, though a High Court challenge alleging procedural unfairness remains open. Sanction A separate hearing, still to be listed. The Times reports it is expected within weeks rather than months. Sources: Premier League statement, 29 September 2026; Sky Sports; The Times; Al Jazeera. Which brings us to the only question anyone in England is actually asking. What does it cost? The Premier League deliberately publishes no tariff, on the reasonable theory that a fixed price for cheating is simply a budget line. The commission has discretion to fine, to deduct points, to impose other sporting sanctions, and in theory to expel. Expulsion is the exotic option and worth understanding properly: it would not relegate City to the Championship. A club outside the league is outside the pyramid, and would have to apply to the Football Association to rejoin, entering the English Football League at League Two subject to a majority vote of EFL clubs. The Premier League would be left with nineteen teams and, most likely, two relegation places that season. The realistic range is a points deduction, and the precedent ledger is where the argument will be fought. Everton lost eight points in total in 2023/24 across two profitability cases, six of them after a successful appeal against an initial ten. Nottingham Forest lost four in the same season. Further down the pyramid, Derby County were docked 21 points in 2021/22 and Luton Town 30 in 2008/09. The football finance academic Kieran Maguire has suggested that a proportionate penalty here would sit between 40 and 60 points, which would have placed City eighteenth last season. Figures inside other clubs, according to The Times, want a deduction heavy enough to amount in practice to relegation. Precedent: points deductions in English football Luton Town, 2008/09 (agent payments and improper administration exit) 30 pts Derby County, 2021/22 (administration and financial irregularities) 21 pts Everton, 2023/24 (two profitability cases, combined) 8 pts Nottingham Forest, 2023/24 (profitability) 4 pts Chart built from published sanctions. No penalty has yet been set in the Manchester City case, and the commission is not bound by any of these figures. Then there is the second front, which may ultimately cost more than any deduction. Several Premier League clubs have already taken legal advice on compensation claims, the BBC reports, arguing that City's conduct affected their own league positions, European qualification or, in the worst case, their relegation. The template exists. In June, Burnley won a £35 million settlement from Everton on exactly that reasoning, a decision Everton are appealing. Multiply that logic across nine seasons and a dozen aggrieved clubs and the exposure becomes genuinely existential, whatever happens to the points column. The cruellest detail is the football. Manchester City go into October top of the Premier League with a perfect record: five wins from five, fifteen points, seven consecutive victories in all competitions under Enzo Maresca , who replaced Pep Guardiola in the summer and has lost only the Community Shield. Erling Haaland leads the division's scoring charts. Reports in Spain say there is no relegation release clause in Haaland's contract, which runs to 2034, though nobody at the Etihad pretends a severe sanction would leave the squad intact. Sponsors, the Mirror reports, are already examining their agreements against the possibility of a season without European football. Guardiola himself broke cover on Wednesday, posting that he wanted every City supporter to know he was there, more than ever, behind his club, his owner, his chairman, Ferran Soriano , the players, the staff, Maresca and the fans, and adding that they would get through it together. Maresca had been more oblique on Sunday, posting a line of Socrates on Instagram: the only thing I know is that I know nothing. Time to breathe, he added. Time to analyse. Time to learn. There is one more layer of irony, and it is not small. This is the first season of the Premier League's new financial architecture. Profitability and Sustainability Rules expired with 2025/26. In their place sits the Squad Cost Ratio, which caps on-pitch spending at 85 per cent of football revenue adjusted for player trading, with a multi-year allowance to exceed that by 30 percentage points at a financial cost, alongside a Sustainability and Systemic Resilience test of working capital, liquidity and positive equity. The league built a new rulebook and, in the same autumn, found that the old one had been dismantled from the inside for the better part of a decade. Whatever the sanction, that is the finding that will follow English football around. Secondary Feature The window that ate October: inside FIFA's first XL break Club football stopped on 20 September and does not restart until 10 October. In the gap, an experiment: four internationals instead of two, three weeks instead of one, and a Nations League that has already produced the result of the year. FIFA's answer to a crowded calendar was to consolidate rather than trim. The September window ran from 24 September to 6 October, national teams were handed up to four fixtures rather than the customary two, and the October break was abolished altogether. Add the buffer either side and the big five European leagues are dark from 20 September to 10 October. The stated logic is player welfare and travel: with the World Cup final falling on 19 July, the season started late and FIFA wanted two international windows a season rather than three. The remaining breaks are 9 to 17 November, 22 to 30 March and 7 to 15 June. UEFA slotted the Champions League league phase around it, with matchday one on 8 to 10 September and matchday two not until 13 and 14 October. The effect on the ground is strange and, for a European league fan, slightly disorienting. Three weekends without domestic football is not a pause, it is a mid-season break. Lower divisions in England kept playing. MLS took a fortnight off its own run-in. And the international game, handed the entire stage, has filled it. Start with the only story that can compete with Manchester for column inches. Greece have beaten Germany for the first time. Dimitris Kourbelis scored the goal, deflected, on 75 minutes in Augsburg on Sunday, and Jürgen Klopp lost his first match as Germany head coach on his home debut. Klopp took the blame without flinching: the line-up and the many changes, he said, were 100 per cent on him. He also insisted he would rather have a bad start than a bad ending. Captain Joshua Kimmich was blunter, describing a side that struggled against a deep block and was too static and not creative enough. Germany have one point from two; Greece have six and lead the group. Elsewhere the new managers are mostly thriving. Zinédine Zidane has won both with France , 1-0 in Türkiye through Kylian Mbappé and 1-0 in Belgium through a slaloming solo goal from Michael Olise two minutes from time. Jorge Jesus has won both with Portugal , with João Félix scoring in each. Xavi Hernández began at Netherlands with a 1-1 draw against Germany rescued by a Cody Gakpo volley in added time, then won 2-1 in Serbia through two goals from debutant Mexx Meerdink . Roberto Mancini 's Italy lost 2-0 at home to Belgium and then went to Türkiye and won 4-1, Pio Esposito and Michael Kayode among the scorers. And the world champions keep winning. Spain came to Wembley on Saturday and beat England 3-2, a result that will feel familiar to anyone who watched the last two finals these sides have contested. Lamine Yamal scored inside two minutes, Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane turned it around before half time, Kane struck the bar from the penalty spot on 54 minutes, and then Álex Baena equalised on 60 and Mikel Oyarzabal won it on 74. Three days later Spain hammered Croatia 4-1 in Seville with Yamal scoring twice. Thomas Tuchel 's England recovered by winning 2-0 in Czechia against ten men, Gordon and Kane again. Nations League A: after two matchdays Group A1 France 6 pts, Belgium 3, Italy 3, Türkiye 0. Group A2 Greece 6 pts, Netherlands 4, Germany 1, Serbia 0. Group A3 Spain 6 pts, England 3, Croatia 3, Czechia 0. Group A4 Portugal 6 pts, Denmark 3, Norway 3, Wales 0. Two teams qualify from each group for the quarter-finals. Matchday three runs 1 to 3 October, matchday four 4 to 6 October, with matchdays five and six on 12 to 17 November. England edge Croatia and Denmark edge Norway on goal difference. The bill for all this arrives at the training grounds. Mbappé suffered a hyperextension of the posterior capsule of his left knee in Türkiye and is expected to miss around two to three weeks, which for Real Madrid compounds a defensive injury list that already included Ibrahima Konaté and Fede Valverde . Jamal Musiala tore a muscle fibre in his right thigh. Gakpo went off with an ankle problem seventeen minutes into the Serbia game; Alexander Isak returned to Liverpool with a thigh complaint. Sunderland lost Brian Brobbey to a hamstring, Manchester United fear the same for Patrick Dorgu , and Barcelona had a scare with Eric García 's left knee before tests found nothing wrong. Four matches instead of two was always going to read like this. Also This Week The fight for FIFA reaches a Florida courtroom The other governance war escalated sharply. On Wednesday the Swiss Football Association withdrew its support for Gianni Infantino 's re-election as FIFA president, a remarkable rebuke from his home federation, which had pledged backing as recently as June. The Swiss cited two things: the secretive FIFA Forward Enterprise plan to sell stakes in World Cup commercial operations, revealed on 28 July and abandoned within days, and pressure from United States president Donald Trump not to impose a mandatory one-match ban on the USA forward Folarin Balogun after a red card against Belgium at the World Cup. Credibility, transparency, accountability and effective statutory bodies, the federation said, are essential to trust in the governance of the game. A day earlier, FIFA had filed a 21-page response through the law firm Linklaters in the Southern District of Florida, opposing UEFA's application to obtain documents and testimony for a planned criminal complaint in Switzerland. UEFA alleges the FFE proposal was developed with a small circle of advisers outside normal governance, that investors would have paid $4.2 billion for a stake in a business valued near $20 billion with no open auction or independent valuation, and that a $30 million commissioner role was earmarked for Infantino. FIFA calls the application bad faith and harassment, accuses UEFA of a misinformation campaign timed to influence the election, and argues it would have been a dereliction of duty not to evaluate such a project at all. Club football has taken a side. On 25 September the Premier League , LaLiga , Lega Serie A and the Bundesliga issued a rare joint statement calling for structural reform, arguing that the FIFA presidency should not combine unchecked regulatory, commercial and political power, and describing what had happened as one of the biggest abuses of power in FIFA's history. UEFA, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation had already written that leadership of the game should never be treated as personal property. Nominations close on 18 November and the vote is in Rabat on 18 March 2027. UEFA meets its 55 member federations in Berlin next week, still without a candidate. That is the thing to watch: not the filings, but whether a challenger emerges before the deadline. Transfer News The European windows are shut. That has never stopped the business, and with three weekends of empty fixtures the agents have had the floor to themselves. One story dominates, and it belongs to a boy who cannot legally sign a professional contract for another week. The boy who turns sixteen on 6 October Manchester United have a generational forward in their academy who has asked to leave, an Irish passport that lets him, and a birthday next Tuesday that makes it possible. Joseph Junior Andreou Gabriel , known to everyone in English football as JJ, was born in Enfield on 6 October 2010. He passed through the academies at Chelsea , Arsenal and West Ham before joining Manchester United in 2022. In April 2025, aged fourteen, he became the youngest player ever to appear for United's under-18s and scored twice on debut against Leeds United . In May 2026 he was named the under-18 Premier League player of the season. He has nine England youth caps across the under-15, under-16 and under-17 age groups. He wears the number 95 at Carrington. He has never played a senior minute, and he is already the most consequential transfer story in Europe. The reason is a passport. Gabriel holds Irish citizenship, which makes him eligible under FIFA's rules to move to a club inside the European Union from the age of sixteen rather than waiting until eighteen, as an English-only player moving abroad would have to. He turns sixteen next Tuesday. In mid-September he formally asked United to terminate his registration with immediate effect, stopped training, missed a Premier League 2 fixture against Brentford , and travelled to Barcelona. United refused to release him. Barcelona are the club most heavily linked, having first hosted him on a tour of the facilities in August 2024, when he met Lamine Yamal . Real Madrid are described by ESPN as monitoring the situation closely, with Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain also watching. One outlet, 101greatgoals, has gone further and reported that Gabriel will join Real Madrid on a free transfer on his sixteenth birthday; that claim is single-sourced and should be treated as such. Fabrizio Romano has pushed back on part of the narrative, stating that Gabriel did not hold direct talks with Barcelona in person and that it is his representatives who are speaking to several clubs. Romano's reading of United's position is that they are not giving up and still hope to keep him. United's head coach, Michael Carrick , has tried to lower the temperature, saying only that JJ is a young boy, that it is important nothing is played out in public, and that making sure he is all right is what matters. The hard-edged reality is simpler. If United retain his registration he cannot join an English club this season, which leaves a move to continental Europe as the only live route, and leaves United to argue about training compensation rather than a fee. For a player of this billing, that is the difference between a windfall and a rounding error. Certainty check: JJ Gabriel Where it sits Advanced interest and representative-level talks. No agreement reported with any club. Hard facts Turns 16 on 6 October. Has requested termination. Irish passport permits an EU move at 16. Best sourced ESPN (Barcelona and Real Madrid monitoring); Fabrizio Romano (no direct player-to-club talks; United still hopeful). Treat with care Reports of a done deal with Real Madrid on his birthday. Single-sourced. Bayern begin planning for life after Kane A contract running out in 2027, a Barcelona hovering, and a 6ft 6in Plan B currently playing in Turin. Harry Kane 's Bayern Munich contract expires in 2027, which means it is now inside its final nine months, which is precisely the point at which a striker with 152 goals in 154 appearances for the club becomes the most interesting man in Europe. He reached 100 Bundesliga goals faster than anyone in history, in 49 matches. Barcelona have been monitoring the situation for weeks. Kane himself addressed it on 25 September, telling Goal that talks are going well, that he is hoping something gets done, and that over the next month or so there should be some sort of decision. A separate strand of reporting claims he wants a release clause permitting a Premier League return. Bayern have announced nothing, so the correct reading is this: an extension is expected, it is not signed, and Barcelona are close enough to hear it if the talks stall. Behind that, Bayern are doing the sensible thing and building a list. Nick Woltemade is on it. The Germany forward moved to Newcastle United for a club record fee of around £69 million in 2025 and was loaned to Juventus on 1 September 2026 for a fee reported at about €4 million, with the Italian club covering his wages. Tuttosport, cited by Sport Witness, reported on 29 September that Bayern have held preliminary conversations with his representatives and that Newcastle would want in the region of €60 million to sell next summer. Nothing is imminent. Juventus, who are paying to watch him every week and would like to make the move permanent, are the immediate competition. Woltemade's own stated priority is more prosaic: get fully fit, play, score. Barcelona keep building the spine Rodri arrived for a package worth €76.5m. Since then the club has spent its energy locking down what it already has. The headline summer move in Spain was Rodri leaving Manchester City after seven years for Barcelona , with City accepting a package reported by Sky Sports and others at €76.5 million. The knock-on has been a burst of retention. Raphinha , who leads La Liga's scoring charts with nine goals, has extended to 2030 on improved terms. Xavi Espart has also signed to 2030, and the midfielder Marc Bernal has extended from 2029 to 2031. On top of that Barcelona have completed the signing of Dany Freire , a sixteen-year-old Portuguese attacking midfielder, on a three-year deal to 2029 after a successful trial. Romano calls that one done, and frames it as Barcelona moving early to head off rival interest, which is a familiar pattern and, given the JJ Gabriel saga, a pointed one. Chelsea sketch a January midfield Sell two senior midfielders in the summer, lose your remaining one to injury, and January arrives early. Chelsea sold Enzo Fernández to Manchester City and Andrey Santos to Manchester United over the summer, then watched Moises Caicedo manage fourteen minutes of football before injury intervened, which has forced Xabi Alonso to field right-backs in central midfield. The club's reporter Nizaar Kinsella , writing for BBC Sport, says Chelsea are open to signing a midfielder in January, while cautioning that they may prefer to wait until the summer for genuine quality rather than take a short-term option, depending on Caicedo's recovery and how the academy players develop. The primary target is Alex Scott of Bournemouth , who has so far been reluctant to sign an extension while the club tries to tie him down, possibly with a release clause attached. The alternatives named are Lamine Camara at Monaco , whose summer move collapsed, Manu Koné at Roma , Adam Wharton at Crystal Palace and Sander Berge at Fulham . Status: concrete interest, no negotiation. Juventus sign a goalkeeper out of season With Kamil Grabara injured and the window closed, Juventus went to the free-agent market and re-signed Neto , announced officially on 28 September on a deal running to June 2027. The Brazilian returns to Turin for a second spell as cover. It is a small piece of business with an unusual amount of romance attached to it, and a reminder that the closed window is not a sealed one: any club with a genuine emergency can still recruit an unattached player. Reported first by Nicolò Schira and confirmed by the club. The Rumour Mill Everything still simmering, with the certainty labelled. Treat anything below “fee agreed” as a story that can die overnight. Endrick, Real Madrid . Status: no move. Liverpool , Aston Villa , Roma and Milan all tested Madrid's resolve in the summer and were told no. The Brazilian is recovering from injury. Romano describes the situation as calm and says Madrid remain absolutely confident in him. Rodrygo, Real Madrid . Status: watch the medical room, not the market. Originally not expected back until February 2027 after a serious injury, he could now return in December or January. Any decision about his future is a summer 2027 conversation. Nick Woltemade, Newcastle (on loan at Juventus ). Status: preliminary contact. Bayern have spoken to representatives; Newcastle want around €60m next summer; Juventus want to buy. Tuttosport, 29 September. Harry Kane, Bayern . Status: advanced talks, nothing signed. Kane said on 25 September that talks were going well and a decision should come within a month. Barcelona are monitoring; a Premier League get-out clause is reported to be part of the discussion. Alex Scott, Bournemouth to Chelsea . Status: concrete interest. Player has not extended; Chelsea's first-choice January midfield target per BBC Sport. Dani Olmo, Barcelona . Status: speculation. A cluster of Premier League clubs have been credited with interest in the Spain midfielder. No club has been reported making contact. Low confidence until an origin source attaches a name to it. Jordan Pickford, Everton to Bayern . Status: link. Reports that Vincent Kompany has pushed for the England goalkeeper as part of Bayern's succession planning for Manuel Neuer . Treat as a link, not a negotiation. Erling Haaland, Manchester City . Status: report. The Spanish outlet Sport says there is no relegation release clause in a contract that runs to 2034. That is a denial of a mechanism, not a denial of interest, and Barcelona's long-term admiration is not a secret. Luis de la Fuente, Spain . Status: done. The Euro and World Cup winning head coach is signing a new contract through July 2030, covering the Nations League, the Euros and the 2030 World Cup. Romano . Calendar note. Italy's winter window opens on 2 January 2027 and closes at 20:00 on 1 February, per Nicolò Schira , with the FIGC having approved an earlier opening on 28 December. England's January window runs to the usual deadline. Media note. Fabrizio Romano has spent several weeks hinting publicly that he may step back from transfer reporting. Nothing has been confirmed. If it happens it is a genuine structural change in how this beat works, and it is worth flagging before it becomes news. Around the Leagues Nobody in Europe's big five has kicked a competitive ball since 20 September, so this is a standings-and-consequences round rather than a results round. It is also, for once, a useful vantage point: five weeks of football is exactly enough to tell you which of the summer's many new managers have landed. ▾ Premier League Take the verdict out of the room for a moment and the sporting story is Enzo Maresca . Replacing Pep Guardiola after a decade should be one of the least survivable jobs in football. Instead Manchester City have won all five league games, sit top on fifteen points, and have taken seven straight victories in all competitions since losing the Community Shield. The manner is not Guardiola's. City beat Sunderland 5-3 on 20 September in a game that had Antoine Semenyo scoring twice, Enzo Fernández and Rayan Cherki adding to it, Erling Haaland leading the division's scoring charts, and Brian Brobbey becoming the first player since 2007 to score a Premier League hat-trick in a defeat. Maresca was unimpressed with the theatre of it. He said he would rather win 1-0 than 5-3, which is the most Marescan sentence available. At the other end the crisis is in north London and it is not subtle. Tottenham are twentieth with two points and two goals from five matches, already out of the EFL Cup at the hands of Liverpool , and beaten 3-2 at home by Aston Villa on 19 September in a game Roberto De Zerbi described with real anger. He said he was very disappointed, very sad and very frustrated, called the second goal conceded unbelievable, and told his squad that leaders need to be leaders, because football is like life and either you are stronger or you lose. He had warned them before kick-off that Villa were playing far more direct football this season. They were caught by exactly that. Romano reports that Spurs are not preparing to sack him, on the basis that they backed his ideas in the summer and understood this would be a process. Whether the stand holds through a fixture list that resumes with Manchester United away is a different question. Fulham , nineteenth on two points, would quite like the attention elsewhere. In between, the picture is genuinely strange. Xabi Alonso 's Chelsea have a minus goal difference and a set-piece problem that Brentford exposed in a 3-0 win on 18 September. Andoni Iraola 's Liverpool are unbeaten but have scored seven in five, with Alexander Isak responsible for most of the decisive moments, including both goals at Ipswich and the only goal at Bournemouth . Brighton have sixteen goals in five, more than anyone, including a 5-0 win at Coventry . And the promoted clubs are not drowning: Hull City are eighth, Ipswich Town have six points, and Coventry, for all their minus-nine goal difference, won at Nottingham Forest . Leeds United are fifth and put four past Newcastle . Manchester United , twelfth on five points, are the anomaly that keeps being an anomaly. Premier League: top and bottom after five Club GD Pts 1 Man City +8 15 2 Arsenal +4 12 3 Brighton +11 10 4 Brentford +6 9 5 Leeds +4 9 … 18 Coventry −9 3 19 Fulham −3 2 20 Tottenham −6 2 Every club has played five. Liverpool and Everton are also on nine points. Play resumes with matchweek six on Saturday 10 October. ▾ La Liga Barcelona have won all seven, scored thirty-one goals and conceded seven. That is not a start, it is a statement, and Hansi Flick was named La Liga coach of the month on Wednesday for good reason. Raphinha , freshly extended to 2030, leads the scoring charts with nine. There have been 7-2 and 5-0 and 4-2 scorelines, and a 3-1 win at Sevilla on 19 September that felt like the moment the rest of the league did its arithmetic. Which leaves José Mourinho six points back in fourth with a problem that is partly his own and largely medical. Real Madrid have fifteen points from seven, having lost 1-0 at Real Betis on the opening weekend and 2-1 in the derby at Atlético Madrid on 20 September. Kylian Mbappé is now out for two to three weeks with a knee injury picked up on international duty. Ibrahima Konaté and Fede Valverde were already out, and Raúl Asencio needs surgery on a fractured tibia that may cost him the rest of the calendar year. October then delivers five matches in sixteen days: Villarreal at home on the 10th, Roma away in the Champions League on the 14th, Sevilla on the 18th, RB Leipzig on the 21st and the Clásico at Barcelona on the 25th. Mourinho has spent September publicly dismissing the pressure. It arrives anyway. Below that, Atlético and Betis are level on sixteen and both capable of holding a top-four place. The horror show is at Valencia , where the club's worst start on record produced a double sacking on 15 September: head coach Carlos Corberán , whose contract had been extended two months earlier, was dismissed on a video call while owner Peter Lim sat 10,000 kilometres away in Singapore, and chief executive Ron Gourlay went with him, ten days after publicly defending the club's stability. Braulio Vázquez has arrived from Osasuna to run the search, with Ernesto Valverde and Jagoba Arrasate reported among the candidates, and B-team coach Óscar Sánchez in temporary charge. Promoted Deportivo A Coruña are seventh, which is the happier end of the same story. ▾ Bundesliga Four games, four wins, nine scored and two conceded: Niko Kovaç 's Borussia Dortmund are top of the Bundesliga, and they got there the unglamorous way, with a 1-0 win at Stuttgart on 19 September. Bayern Munich are second on ten with a far better goal difference, having put seven past Union Berlin on 18 September, but they also drew 0-0 at promoted Schalke on the opening weekend and have now lost Jamal Musiala to a torn muscle fibre in his right thigh. Freiburg , quietly, are also on ten. The first managerial casualty of the German season came at Borussia Mönchengladbach , and it was not close. The club endured the worst three-match start in its history, capped by a 5-0 defeat at Freiburg on 12 September, and Eugen Polanski departed with zero points. Sporting director Rouven Schröder framed it as being about points rather than individuals. Polanski, to his credit, conceded he had never seen individual defensive mistakes at such a number and frequency. In the space where the football should have been, their manager agreed to stay until 2030, their great rivals were found guilty, and the injury list kept growing. T he extended international break meant Arsenal 's men went from the 3-0 defeat at Brighton and Hove Albion on 19 September to a blank calendar. Their next game is Leeds United at the Emirates on 10 October. That left the week to the people in suits, and they were busy. The big one had broken on the Tuesday before this week began. Sami Mokbel reported for the BBC that Mikel Arteta had agreed an improved contract, ending months of talks . His existing deal runs out at the end of this season. In May, co-chair Josh Kroenke had called securing the manager's future the club's priority. On Thursday the shape of the deal arrived. Fabrizio Romano reported that the agreement is valid for the next four years , which would presumably take Arteta to June 2030, and said the verbal agreement is done . Mokbel described a sharp pay increase on a current salary of around ten million pounds a year plus bonuses. No new figure has been published. It is not only the manager. David Ornstein of The Athletic reported that Arteta 's backroom staff are in the process of renewing their deals, and Romano said they will sign for the same four years. Ornstein did not name names. Arseblog News thought it reasonable to assume the group includes Albert Stuivenberg , set-piece coach Nicolas Jover , goalkeeping coach Inaki Cana and tactical assistant Miguel Molina , with Gabriel Heinze also in line for improved terms. There is one thing missing: an announcement. As of Tuesday night the club had confirmed nothing. Arseblog News reported the announcement was unlikely to come quickly because the club had yet to film the content that goes with it. For a manager who ended the long wait for a league title last season, after three straight second-place finishes, the paperwork feels like a formality. It is still paperwork. The verbal agreement is done. Fabrizio Romano , on Arteta ’s new deal The timing matters. Arsenal won their first four league games of the title defence and then were taken apart at Brighton . A contract signed in that light is a statement that the club sees one bad afternoon for what it was. It also gives Arteta security going into a stretch that, after the break, runs straight into Leeds United , Lille in the Champions League and a run of games every three or four days. The other contract news of the week was about Declan Rice . Romano reported on Thursday that a new deal is really, really close , with final details being sorted and paperwork going to lawyers before an announcement. His current contract runs to 2028, so the extension would land before it enters its final year. That good news came with a worry attached. Rice had withdrawn from the England squad on 21 September, with football.london reporting his workload was being managed. Then Thomas Tuchel confirmed on Saturday that he was carrying a problem. The England manager said he saw straight away on TV that something was off while watching Rice at Brighton , and that the player just confirmed that impression . After fifty-five games for Arsenal last season and seven of England's eight World Cup matches, the rest looks sensible rather than alarming. Key Facts: the week at a glance Played Nothing. x: World Football, Weekly The Weekly Soccer Digest Reporting, analysis and the transfer paper trail Wednesday, September 23, 2026 · No. 1 · Arsenal covered separately In This Edition The Lead · Transfer News · Around the Leagues · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead Football's Cold War Reaches the Ballot Box Two months after Gianni Infantino tried to sell a fifth of the World Cup's commercial future to private capital, the withdrawal has not settled anything. A conciliatory letter landed on Monday. By Tuesday the German federation had called it a campaign stunt, and on Wednesday UEFA's president was talking about broken trust. The 2027 election has effectively begun. Governance · Analysis T he letter went out on Monday to all 211 of FIFA's member associations, and it was written in the register of a man who knows he has a problem. Gianni Infantino told the federations he was willing to put his own house under outside inspection. "First, I will ask the Council whether it wishes to commission an independent external review of FIFA's current governance framework for major strategic initiatives and recommend potential improvements," he wrote, in a passage reported by Reuters . Of the scheme that triggered the crisis, he was blunt: "It remained a proposal, not a decision, and was always subject to the necessary approvals of the Council and the Member Associations. It has now been withdrawn and will not proceed." The scheme was FIFA Forward Enterprise. Announced on 28 July, it would have moved World Cup and Club World Cup broadcasting, sponsorship, ticketing and licensing rights into a commercial subsidiary valued at roughly $20bn, with Joshua Kushner 's Thrive Capital taking about 20 per cent for $4.2bn. The sweetener was aimed at the small federations who hold the votes: annual development funding would have climbed from $8m to $20m for the 2027 to 2030 cycle. For the confederations that generate the revenue, it was the sale of an asset FIFA holds in trust rather than owns. The revolt was faster than anyone at FIFA appears to have modelled. On 30 July all 55 UEFA associations voted unanimously to boycott future World Cups and FIFA competitions. CONCACAF and its 41 members rejected the plan. The Asian Confederation's Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa called it "totally unacceptable." Infantino withdrew it on 31 July, three days after announcing it. That is not a retreat. That is a rout. Gianni Infantino is definitely not the right person to lead a reform process. He has squandered all credibility. Bernd Neuendorf , president of the German Football Association, 22 September Withdrawal did not buy peace. On 27 August UEFA launched legal action against Infantino personally, alleging he had "fraudulently" offered the stake without proper FIFA authorisation at an "absurdly low enterprise value of only approximately $20bn," and describing the vehicle as a way for "Infantino and that small circle to acquire a permanent stake in and otherwise profit from FIFA's most valuable assets." The boycott was suspended only once FIFA confirmed in writing that the plan was "irrevocably and permanently withdrawn" and would "not re-appear in any other shape, construction, name or form." UEFA added that the underlying crisis had not been resolved. Reporting differs on where the action was filed, so we are not naming a venue. ( Yahoo Sports ) Which brings us to this week, and to the reason Monday's letter did not land the way it was meant to. Within twenty-four hours Bernd Neuendorf , president of the German Football Association , went on the record with Reuters : "I regard Gianni Infantino's letter as a transparent ploy to secure his re-election next year." He added that Infantino "is definitely not the right person to lead a reform process" and "has squandered all credibility." Germany is not a peripheral federation lodging a protest. It is a four-time world champion, the host of the last European Championship, and one of the four or five associations whose position other federations read before settling their own. On Wednesday it escalated again. The Associated Press reported UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin speaking directly to the damage, framing the task ahead as repairing trust broken by Infantino's World Cup plan ( AP, 23 September ). The choice of word is deliberate. A governing body that has to litigate against its own president to establish what he is authorised to sell has a problem no external review can write away. The arithmetic, though, still favours the incumbent, and that is the uncomfortable part for the reformers. Reuters reports that Infantino stands for re-election in March 2027 and that sources believe he retains the votes to win, with opponents concentrating on limiting his powers rather than fielding a rival. FIFA's electorate is one association, one vote, which means Germany and Gibraltar count the same. The federations that were offered a tripling of their development grant in July are the same federations who will fill in the ballot in March, and Infantino's letter took care to promise that a federation's position on governance "would not affect their treatment by FIFA." It is a sentence that only needs writing if people were worried about the opposite. So the shape of the next six months is clear. Europe and CONCACAF have the money, the clubs and the lawyers. Infantino has the ballot box. Every reform proposal from here will be read by both camps as a vote count, and the confederations will keep the litigation running because discovery is the only mechanism capable of establishing what was actually promised in July and to whom. None of it is incidental to the football. The question underneath is who decides what the World Cup is for, and it will be settled by a show of hands in a conference hall. Spain Has Its Own Civil War, and It Is Not About Football Real Madrid lost a derby, the referees' committee conceded one of the three big calls, and within forty-eight hours the club had formally demanded the resignation of the league's president. Meanwhile Barcelona quietly went seven from seven. The match itself was tight and bad-tempered. Atletico Madrid beat Real Madrid 2-1 at the Metropolitano on Sunday. Dean Huijsen was dismissed after a VAR review, Alejandro Grimaldo converted the resulting penalty on fifty minutes, Jonathan David made it two on 59 and Antonio Rudiger headed a consolation on 89. Real Madrid's own match report, published on the club's website, carried the headline "Un pesimo arbitraje decide el derbi" : a dreadful refereeing performance decides the derby. Clubs do not usually put that on their own front page. On Monday and Tuesday the Spanish referees' technical committee published its review, and the outcome was genuinely split. The committee ruled that Lee Kang-in 's 44th-minute challenge on Fede Valverde was a clear and obvious error: it should have been a red card and VAR should have intervened. It also ruled that the earlier incident involving Cristian Romero and Jude Bellingham was correctly handled, and that Huijsen's red card and the penalty were correct ( via El Nacional ). Two right, one wrong. Madrid had a legitimate grievance and, in the committee's judgement, not the one they were shouting loudest about. Jose Mourinho , in his first Madrid derby since returning to the Bernabeu bench in June, did not wait for the review. "Son dos tarjetas rojas claras," he said, two clear red cards, before turning on the video official: "this gentleman has a very complete history as a VAR referee in Real Madrid matches" ( La Opinion ). It is the oldest script Mourinho owns, and at the Bernabeu it plays. Then the institutions took over. On Tuesday Real Madrid issued a formal statement calling it "intolerable that the LaLiga president uses his institutional position to continue discrediting and attacking Real Madrid," and said the competition required "a leader capable of administering it with the essential duty of neutrality" ( EFE ). The trigger was Javier Tebas 's social-media reply to the refereeing row, in which he said that arguing referees are directed against Real Madrid is living in another galaxy. Tebas answered the statement the same day and aimed straight at Florentino Perez : "The president of LaLiga is not the owner of the competition. Neither is the president of Real Madrid." And: "I am not the owner of LaLiga and I will not run it as though it belonged to a single club. Respect for everyone. Subordination to no one." ( beIN Sports ) Two things are worth holding onto. Tebas is also among the loudest voices calling for Gianni Infantino to resign, which made this a week in which Spanish football's most combative administrator fought on two fronts at once. And then there is the table. While all this went on, Barcelona won 3-1 at Sevilla to move to seven wins from seven. Real Madrid are fourth, six points back, and go into the break without Fede Valverde , whose club medical report described a severe trauma to the left ankle ( Real Madrid ). Transfer News A Four-Time European Champion, a Rome Clinic and a Club 15th in Serie A The summer window shut three weeks ago, which is exactly why the free-agent market is suddenly the most interesting room in football. David Alaba has picked the least predictable door in it. The best transfer story of the week did not involve a fee. But that second number is the explanation: Kosta Runjaic has an injury-thinned back line and a defender with 400 elite matches behind him is available for nothing. The risk is his fitness record. The upside is the most decorated centre-back in the division, at no cost. He is not the only serious name changing address outside a window.
