The First of January Is Closer Than It Looks Anyone whose contract expires in June 2027 can open talks with a foreign club on New Year's Day. That clock is now ticking on Harry Kane, Christian Pulisic and a surprising number of others. The single biggest expiry in world football belongs to Harry Kane , who is in the final year of the deal he signed with Bayern Munich in 2023 and who on 18 September became the fastest player ever to 100 Bundesliga goals, reaching the mark in his 98th appearance. Bayern are not hiding. Chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen has said the club are "having productive discussions" and expects matters to wrap up after the international break; president Herbert Hainer has gone further: "We want to extend his contract further, and I also think that's what will happen" ( bundesliga.com ). Kane himself, on the night of the record: "All I can say is that I enjoy every minute of it. I'm extremely happy here. The talks are ongoing" ( beIN Sports ). Bild has reported a target of 2029, a broadly flat salary near €25m a year and an exit clause under discussion. Status: advanced, not signed. The renewal nobody is covering properly is Christian Pulisic 's. Marco Conterio of Tuttomercatoweb reported on Wednesday that the American's AC Milan deal runs to 2027 with a club option, that he currently earns around €4.5m net, that his camp opened at €8m and would settle at €7m, and that this sits above Milan's wage ceiling. The detail that matters is procedural rather than financial: talks were serious in the autumn and then stalled, and Pulisic's side expected a formal written proposal of the kind other players received and never got one. A club that values a player's commercial weight in North America while declining to put a number on paper is a club that may find itself negotiating with Barcelona's lawyers in January instead. Elsewhere on the expiry board: Jude Bellingham 's Real Madrid deal runs to 2029 and Matteo Moretto has reported an extension to 2030 or 2031 is close, though we could only reach that reporting second-hand and are labelling it accordingly. Kevin De Bruyne 's Napoli situation produced the week's cleanest contradiction: Nicolo Schira reported on Wednesday that renewal talks on his 2027-expiring contract are stalled and the parties look close to parting at season's end, while the player told reporters from the Belgium camp a day earlier that he "never considered the idea of leaving Napoli" and is very happy there ( Fantacalcio ). Both can be true. Only one will be true in June. And then there is the renewal that is not happening. Alexis Mac Allister is contracted to Liverpool until 2028 but said earlier this month that he felt a little sad watching Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai sign long-term deals while his agent was told the club was "not in a position to renew." On 22 September, on Argentina duty, he softened it: "it was more about my emotions than judging the club," and if it is two more years, "that's absolutely fine" ( Sports Illustrated ). Read the club's behaviour rather than the player's manners. Liverpool are comfortable letting a 2028 contract run down, and that is usually the first visible step toward a summer sale. In Barcelona the news was better. Sporting director Deco told the club's general assembly on 19 September that renewals for Raphinha (to 2030), Marc Bernal (to 2031) and Xavi Espart (to 2030) had been all but completed, with formalisation expected within a week (Football Espana). None had been signed as of Wednesday, which is a distinction worth preserving. Given what Raphinha has done in the first seven matchdays, it is also the cheapest business the club will do this season. Barcelona Close the Alvarez File, and Laporta Lights It on Fire The summer's most expensive non-transfer got its epilogue this week, and it doubled as a warning about what Barcelona can and cannot do in January. Barcelona bid €100m for Julian Alvarez in late May and Atletico Madrid refused to sell to them specifically. On 21 September Joan Laporta finally said out loud what the club had been briefing privately: "They acted offended; they had no way to justify their attitude. We were constantly hearing that they would sell him to every club except Barca. Then they dropped the pretense and said it openly." He added that he had suspicions about why, but no proof, so he would keep them to himself ( Sports Illustrated ). It is not the language of a president who intends to try again in eight weeks. The finances say the same thing more plainly. Barcelona's vice-president for economics, Ferran Olive , told Cadena SER this week that the club will have positive financial fair play headroom in January but would still need to sell before buying, and that the move to Montjuic during the Camp Nou roof works is expected to push them back outside the one-to-one rule in the summer of 2027 ( El Desmarque ). Earlier modelling by Cronica Global put Barcelona's registration room at roughly €43m against an Alvarez package costing €50m to €55m a year. The gap is real, the political route is closed, and in the meantime Raphinha has scored twelve league goals in seven games playing centrally. Status: dormant, and we would treat any January revival as a rumour until Atletico say otherwise. The Rumour Mill Everything still simmering, with a certainty label on each. This is where the not-yet-official stories live, and where the reader should keep a hand on their wallet. Endrick to AC Milan. The best-triangulated January link on the board. Daniele Longo of Calciomercato reported on 22 September that Ruben Amorim wants a left-footed number ten and that Endrick is the first name on the list, with feasibility resting entirely on whether Florentino Perez will do business. Separately, Joaquin Maroto has reported the player is increasingly frustrated with his role at Real Madrid . Two outlets, two countries, same direction. Complicating it: Romano quoted Madrid in mid-September saying they remain "absolutely confident in Endrick." Concrete interest. Rayan Ait-Nouri to Juventus. Gazzetta dello Sport, relayed by Tuttomercatoweb on 23 September, reports that Juventus re-established contact with the left-back's entourage during this international break after first talks in late August, and are weighing a loan with an option to buy so the permanent negotiation can wait until summer. The premise is that he is behind the queue at Manchester City under Enzo Maresca . Concrete interest, contact made. Federico Chiesa and Wataru Endo out at Liverpool. Both were left out of Liverpool 's Champions League squad. Endo has played no minutes at all this season; Chiesa has five goals in 50 appearances since arriving from Juventus in 2024 and is now behind Bradley Barcola , Rio Ngumoha , Cody Gakpo and reportedly the 21-year-old Lewis Koumas . Italian outlets have him linked with a Serie A return ( via SportBible ). Strongly signposted exit, no destination agreed. Bernardo Silva is being forgotten at the Bernabeu. This one is ours to flag rather than anyone's to confirm. Silva joined Real Madrid on a free from Manchester City this summer on a two-year deal. Under Jose Mourinho he has 282 minutes in six league games with no goals and one assist, including eight minutes across the last two fixtures (Fichajes, a low-tier outlet, though the minutes are checkable). Barcelona pursued him in the summer before talks collapsed over money and playing time. A 32-year-old who is ninth choice by late September, with a domestic rival who wanted him six weeks ago, is a January story forming in plain sight. Speculative. No contact reported. Alejandro Garnacho's loan is failing, and the clause may be why. Three appearances for Aston Villa and benched for the last two. Unai Emery earlier this month: "We continue working with him, but for now there are others performing better." The loan from Chelsea reportedly carries an appearance-triggered obligation to buy, which is precisely the mechanism that gives a club a reason not to play someone. The Daily Mail reports Spanish clubs want him in January (via the Daily Mail). Concrete interest, no talks reported. And briefly. Manu Kone to Chelsea : Corriere dello Sport says Roma now want around €100m, roughly double the summer figure. Rumour. · JJ Gabriel , the 15-year-old at Manchester United who turns 16 on 6 October: Romano called Real Madrid favourites with Barcelona in contact, and Christian Falk added Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain on 23 September (CaughtOffside). Rumour, but serious reporters on it. · Thiago Pitarch , 19, has played no minutes for Real Madrid and was sent to Castilla for the break after the club blocked a summer move to Fulham . Interest expected to revive. The Fee That Keeps Talking: €145m Liverpool paid a reported €145m to Paris Saint-Germain for Bradley Barcola , the biggest fee of the summer. Five matches in, he has 248 minutes, no goals and no assists. Andoni Iraola on the fit: "He has very good passing quality. In counter-attack situations, we didn't find him twice, so we need to learn these movements" ( Foot Mercato ). Set beside Florian Wirtz at a reported €125m, who also started slowly and is now the subject of exit stories, Liverpool have roughly €270m tied up in two attackers who are not yet firing. The league table is less forgiving than the performances: Liverpool are sixth on nine points, six behind Manchester City, having drawn three of their first five. Around the Leagues Premier League Manchester City are five from five and Enzo Maresca 's first autumn in charge is already producing the sort of numbers that make a season feel decided in September. Sunday's 5-3 win over Sunderland was the most entertaining match of the round and statistically one of the strangest of the Premier League era. City took the lead three separate times before half-time, which Opta records as only the seventh instance in league history. Brian Brobbey scored a hat-trick and lost, the sixth time that has happened in the Premier League and the first since Roque Santa Cruz managed it for Blackburn in December 2007. Erling Haaland scored the fifth and in doing so completed the set: he has now scored against all 25 Premier League clubs he has faced. Regis Le Bris took charge of his 100th Sunderland match, the first manager to reach that mark at the club since Roy Keane . The result that will echo longest, though, was on Friday night. Brentford beat Chelsea 3-0, and the underlying numbers are alarming for Xabi Alonso . Chelsea have now conceded 23 set-piece goals since the start of last season, joint-worst in the division, and have gone 22 consecutive league matches without a clean sheet at a rate of 2.2 non-penalty goals conceded per game. This was their eleventh defeat of the calendar year, more than in the whole of 2025 ( Sky Sports ). Alonso was direct: "We concede the first goal, you're still in the game but then we lose the shape. We were out of control." Levi Colwill went further: "At times we have been bullied." Brentford are unbeaten through five for the first time in their history. All of this arrived four days after Todd Boehly and Mark Walter agreed to sell their combined 25 per cent stake to majority owner Clearlake Capital, taking Clearlake to 86.5 per cent in a deal valuing the club at £5bn ( Sky Sports ). At the other end, two very large clubs are in genuine trouble. Manchester United have five points from five, equalling their joint-worst Premier League start, and Michael Carrick spent the week absorbing it: "I'm totally happy taking responsibility, absolutely no problem with that, it doesn't bother me" ( Irish News ). The 1-1 at Fulham prompted Gary Neville to call a passage of United's play the worst fifteen minutes he had ever seen from them in possession, and Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa to complain that officials do not like Manchester United to lose. Tottenham are bottom of the table on two points with no wins, and the reporting on Roberto De Zerbi is contested. Fabrizio Romano was the clearest: "the message from Tottenham, as of today, remains a message of confidence in Roberto De Zerbi," and "I don't have any indication of Tottenham exploring different ways" ( via Football365 ). Other outlets have run harder lines. Weigh accordingly. Around them: Coventry City won at Nottingham Forest through Jay Dasilva for their first top-flight victory since 2001, having failed to score in their opening four matches. Oliver Glasner said he had felt the heaviness of Forest's past for the first time; they have not won a home league game since December (Sky Sports). Everton are unbeaten in seven, matching David Moyes 's own 2006-07 side, and spent Wednesday morning mocking The Athletic on social media for leaving every Everton player out of its in-season top fifty. Off the pitch, Profit and Sustainability Rules are gone: this is the first season of the Squad Cost Ratio, capping wages, transfers and agent fees at 85 per cent of football revenue plus net player-sale profit, with a six-point deduction for breaching the red threshold ( Premier League ). And Daniel Levy received a £27m exit payment from Tottenham, taking his total earnings there to £88m, reported by The Athletic as the second-largest payout to a departing Premier League executive ( via Yahoo Sports ). La Liga Barcelona have won all seven. The engine is Raphinha , who has twelve league goals in those seven games, three of them penalties, a total bettered at this stage of a season this century only by Cristiano Ronaldo 's thirteen in 2014-15. He scored hat-tricks in consecutive matches: seven days after putting three past Racing Santander in a 7-2 win he produced a perfect one at Sevilla , header, curled finish and chip, in a 3-1 away victory in which Barcelona's expected goals read 3.26 to 0.45 ( beIN Sports ). Around him, Lamine Yamal is now a club captain at 19, the youngest in Barcelona's history to wear the armband on a Champions League debut, and leads the team for chances created. Hansi Flick 's one worry going into the break is Andreas Christensen , who went off at the Pizjuan with a thigh problem. Behind them the table is unusual. Atletico Madrid are second after the derby, level on sixteen with Manuel Pellegrini 's Real Betis . Real Madrid are fourth. Alaves are sixth on eleven, their best start in La Liga history, and promoted Deportivo La Coruna are seventh with Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang , 37, on five goals. At the bottom, Valencia confirmed Javier Aguirre as head coach on Wednesday, his seventh La Liga club, ten days after sacking Carlos Corberan and football chief executive Ron Gourlay (Fichajes.net). He starts at Racing Santander on 11 October. One fixture went unplayed: Levante against Athletic Club was postponed under an official weather alert after flooding in Valencia and is rescheduled for 21 October (El Desmarque). Bundesliga Two things happened in Germany this week and both were emphatic. Borussia Dortmund won 1-0 at VfB Stuttgart through a 70th-minute Maxi Beier finish, assisted by Jobe Bellingham , and went into the break top of the table with four wins from four, their best start in eleven years. It was, remarkably, Dortmund's first shot on target of the match from ten attempts ( BVB ). Niko Kovac is doing it without Emre Can and Giannis Konstantelias , both with cruciate ligament injuries. Meanwhile Bayern Munich beat Union Berlin 7-0. Michael Olise scored a hat-trick and took 88 per cent of the man-of-the-match vote; Harry Kane scored twice and became the fastest player to 100 Bundesliga goals, reaching the mark in his 98th appearance and demolishing Dieter Muller 's 129-game benchmark (bundesliga.com). The league is scoring at a rate not seen in forty years: 137 goals in the first 36 matches, 3.8 a game, the third-highest total after four matchdays in Bundesliga history (bundesliga.com). Freiburg are third and set a club record with six straight competitive wins before drawing at Eintracht Frankfurt . Promoted SC Paderborn beat Hoffenheim 3-1 for their first Bundesliga win since 2020. At the bottom, Borussia Monchengladbach have no points from four: Eugen Polanski was dismissed on 13 September and Alexander Blessin confirmed on 22 September on a deal to 2028, arriving from St Pauli ( bundesliga.com ). Union Berlin have one point and seventeen conceded, and Mauro Lustrinelli is next in the queue. Off the pitch, Jurgen Klopp , now Germany head coach, named a first squad of 44 players for the four Nations League fixtures ( DFB ), and the cartel office's August ruling that 50+1 is lawful only if applied consistently has left the exemptions held by Wolfsburg, Leverkusen, Hannover and Leipzig looking exposed. Serie A Three clubs are level at the top on thirteen points and the separation is goal difference: Roma first, Inter second, Lazio third. Gian Piero Gasperini 's Roma have conceded three goals in five matches, the best defence in the division, and drew 2-2 with Inter at the Olimpico in the round's best match: Manu Kone scored twice in the first half, Lautaro Martinez twice in the second ( Corriere dello Sport ). Fourth, and this is not a misprint, are Cagliari on twelve points with two goals conceded in five under Fabio Pisacane . Promoted Frosinone are sixth. Juventus beat Atalanta 2-0 through Francisco Conceicao and Bremer , which leaves Maurizio Sarri with three straight defeats and one goal scored in them, his first such run at Atalanta. AC Milan are fifth and unbeaten domestically after a 3-0 win over Lecce . Napoli are ninth on seven points, their worst start in a decade, and Corriere dello Sport reported a heated dressing-room confrontation at the Franchi in which Massimiliano Allegri made clear he had wanted two more signings, a centre-back and a striker of substance (Corriere dello Sport; press reconstruction, not on the record). Bologna sacked Domenico Tedesco on 16 September after one point from four and installed Raffaele Palladino on a three-year deal the same afternoon (Il Fatto Quotidiano). Away from the table, Italian football buried a monument: Sandro Mazzola died on 19 September aged 83 (Sky Sport Italia), and the disciplinary judge fined Juventus €10,000 after a small section of the Curva Sud turned their backs during his minute's silence. Lazio published accounts showing a €10m loss against a €104.6m wage bill, with no European football and a supporter boycott costing roughly 25,000 season tickets (Corriere dello Sport). The Meazza, meanwhile, turned 100. Ligue 1 France has produced the most disorderly table in Europe. Monaco lead on thirteen points, Lyon are second on eleven with the division's best goal difference after thrashing Rennes 4-0, and Paris FC are third, also on eleven. Sunday's Classique at the Velodrome went to PSG 2-1 in front of 61,499: Ferran Torres , the €50m summer signing from Barcelona, scored seven minutes after coming on for Khvicha Kvaratskhelia , Amine Gomes equalised for Marseille on 72 and Marquinhos won it two minutes later ( Foot Mercato ). Luis Enrique was measured afterwards: his side controlled the first period without creating, started the second brilliantly and missed clear chances. Marseille are the story. The 2026 season was rebuilt around the World Cup, so most clubs still have around eight of 34 matches to play, the Wild Card round begins 18 November and MLS Cup is 18 December. k: Arsenal and Mikel Arteta have agreed a new long-term contract, the BBC reports, three days after Brighton beat the champions 3-0 on the south coast.
x: The Weekly Arsenal Digest All Arsenal, all week, every Tuesday No. 6 · Edition of Tuesday, September 22, 2026 · Premier League Matchweek 5 · International Break · Read this edition on the web In this edition The Lead · Transfer News · The Squad · Hale End · Arsenal Women · Gunners Abroad · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch THE LEAD Arteta Gets His Deal. His Champions Get a Warning. The BBC reported on Tuesday morning that Arsenal and their manager have agreed terms on a new long-term contract. It lands three days after Brighton & Hove Albion pulled the champions apart on the south coast, and the sequence tells you a great deal about how this club now sees itself. T here is a particular kind of week that only happens to a club that has finally won something. Sami Mokbel of the BBC reported on Tuesday morning that Mikel Arteta has agreed a new long-term contract at Arsenal , with a significant rise on the roughly 10 million pounds a year he currently earns. No end date has been made public and no announcement has been issued. The old deal ran only to 2027, and for most of this year the absence of a new one has been the quiet hum underneath everything else at London Colney. That hum has now stopped. What has not stopped is the noise from Saturday evening, when Brighton & Hove Albion beat Arsenal 3-0 at the Amex and made it look less like an upset than an inevitability. Pascal Gross struck from distance on the half hour. Charalampos Kostoulas added a second on the stroke of half time, fifteen seconds after Bukayo Saka had tamely missed a chance to equalise. Chema Andres headed in a corner nine minutes into the second half. It was the first defeat of the season, the end of a seven-match winning run, and the first time since the title was won in May that anyone had been able to say out loud that this Arsenal side looked ordinary. The timing is coincidence rather than cause and effect. But put the two stories side by side and you get the truest picture of Arsenal in September 2026 that anyone is going to draw: a club that has decided the manager is the answer, and is now discovering that the squad still has a question in it. KEY FACTS: THE ARTETA EXTENSION REPORTED BY Sami Mokbel , BBC Sport, Tuesday September 22, 2026 STATUS Terms agreed. No official announcement, and no end date disclosed. CURRENT TERMS About 10m pounds a year plus bonuses, including 5m for Champions League qualification. The existing deal ran to 2027. IN CHARGE SINCE December 20, 2019 HONOURS Premier League 2025-26; FA Cup 2020; Community Shield 2020, 2023 and 2026 LAST SEASON Champions of England. Champions League runners-up. EFL Cup runners-up. Start with the defeat, because it was more instructive than the scoreline. Brighton & Hove Albion pressed Arsenal from the first throw-in, which is close to the phrase Arteta reached for afterwards, and the champions had no coherent way through it. David Raya was imprecise with the ball at his feet and the nervousness travelled up the pitch from him. Gabriel Magalhaes gave Gross the yard he needed. The defending at the corner for the third was, in the view of even sympathetic Arsenal writers, not really defending at all. And when Arsenal did reach a promising area, there was no pace to run beyond anyone and no Plan B to reach for. That last point is the structural one, and it did not appear on Saturday. It has been there since the window shut on September 1. Gabriel Martinelli went to Al Hilal . Gabriel Jesus went to Barcelona . Leandro Trossard went to Besiktas . In came Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge , a fine footballer who has already started to build something with Kai Havertz and Riccardo Calafiori , but who arrived as a replacement for three departures rather than as an addition on top of them. “A very disappointing result and performance. They were another gear from us in the basics of the game.” Mikel Arteta, after the defeat at Brighton David Ornstein of The Athletic has been blunt about what that means. Arsenal wanted a player to raise the level of their attack this summer and did not get one. Vinicius Junior was the headline pursuit. Julian Alvarez was a long-standing admiration. Malick Fofana was looked at as an investment. Bradley Barcola and Morgan Rogers were explored and ruled out. None of them moved at a price Arsenal were willing to pay, so the money stayed in the building. The owners, Ornstein says, showed a willingness to fund a marquee signing. The club simply could not land one. The consequence is visible in a number that should trouble nobody and yet nags at everybody: eight goals in five Premier League matches, from around 6.8 expected goals. Arsenal are not failing to create. They are creating and then wasting, and they are doing it while scoring nothing at all from set pieces, the single most reliable source of goals in last season's title win. A team that took 19 league goals from corners in 2025-26, a competition record, has taken none from any dead ball in eight matches this term. Arteta delivered the Premier League title, ending a 22-year wait and taking the club's tally to 14. He took them to a Champions League final in Budapest in May, where they drew 1-1 with Paris Saint-Germain after extra time and lost 4-3 on penalties. He lost an EFL Cup final to Manchester City in March, then beat the same opponent 3-0 in the Community Shield in August. Tying him down now, with the squad unfinished, says the club believes the ceiling is above the roof they have already touched. And the contract work does not stop with him. TEAMtalk has reported that talks with Declan Rice , Martin Odegaard and Jurrien Timber are all advancing alongside the manager's. The architecture of the next five years is being built during an international break, which is exactly when clubs of this size do their least visible and most consequential work. THE SQUAD The Set-Piece Machine Has Stalled, and It May Not Be an Accident Nineteen corner goals last season, a Premier League record. None from any dead ball in eight matches this one. A rule change is hovering over the explanation. The most striking statistic about Arsenal 's start is not the eight goals or the one defeat. It is the zero. Eight matches into 2026-27, across the Community Shield, the Premier League, the Champions League and the Carabao Cup, Arsenal have not scored from a corner or a free kick. To understand why that is remarkable you have to remember what last season was. Arsenal scored 19 Premier League goals from corners, breaking a record that had stood since 1992-93. Add indirect free kicks, direct free kicks and long throws and the total reaches 25 non-penalty set-piece goals, the most in the division and around 35 per cent of their 71 goals. No champion had previously taken more than 30 per cent of its non-penalty goals from dead balls. At the other end they conceded only eight set-piece goals, a net swing of 17 and the best figure in the league. The architecture belongs to Nicolas Jover , who arrived from Manchester City in July 2021 and built a system around crowding the goalkeeper in the six-yard box and attacking the flick-on at the back post. Gabriel Magalhaes was the primary target, winning first contact on 13 crossed corners. Declan Rice became the principal taker with 95 corners, 87 from the left, producing seven goals and 6.9 expected goals, the best of any taker in the league. Bukayo Saka handled the right. Bars are scaled to the 19-goal record. So what has changed? One candidate is the refereeing guidance introduced for this season, which instructs officials to be stricter about holding, pulling and wrestling in the penalty area at set pieces, with penalties explicitly available as a sanction. The guidance retains a high bar for intervention, and the Premier League has not framed it as being about any one club. k: Europe's great managerial reshuffle faces its first verdicts as Maresca's Manchester City go four from four and Mourinho's Real Madrid chase Barcelona.
x: World football, every Wednesday The Weekly Soccer Digest Edition of Wednesday, September 16, 2026 · Arsenal covered separately In this edition The Lead · Transfer News · Around the Leagues · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead The Great Reshuffle Meets Its First Reckoning Seven of Europe's biggest clubs changed manager inside a single calendar year. Four games into the new season, the early returns are already brutally uneven. There is a version of this season that will be written in a year's time as the most consequential managerial turnover in the modern history of the European game, and the remarkable thing is that we are only four matchdays into finding out whether that is true. Pep Guardiola is gone from Manchester City . Jose Mourinho is back at Real Madrid . Arne Slot was dismissed by Liverpool three weeks before the World Cup final and Ruben Amorim , sacked by Manchester United in January, is now standing in the technical area at AC Milan . Almost every door in the sport swung at once. The scale is easier to grasp in numbers than in names. Between the first day of January and the end of May, the Premier League's traditional big six lost seven managers: six sackings and one voluntary departure, an average of one every twenty-one days. Chelsea alone got through two, dismissing Enzo Maresca on New Year's Day and Liam Rosenior in April before settling on Xabi Alonso , who began work on the first of July. Tottenham Hotspur also burned through two before landing on Roberto De Zerbi . Only Mikel Arteta , in post since December 2019, has watched the whole carousel from a fixed seat. What makes this week the right moment to take stock is that the evidence has finally started arriving. The Champions League league phase opened on September 8 and the domestic leagues have now played four or five rounds. That is a small sample, and anyone claiming certainty from it is selling something. But it is no longer nothing, and the spread between the best and worst of these appointments is already wider than anybody would have predicted in July. The best of it, and the worst of it At the top of that spread sits Enzo Maresca , which is not where most people expected to find him. Handed the hardest inheritance in football, he has taken Manchester City to four wins from four in the Premier League, a 2-0 win at Porto in Europe and a 1-0 victory at Old Trafford, all while presiding over a squad that has been rebuilt around him rather than for him. Rodri , the 2024 Ballon d'Or winner and a World Cup winner with Spain in July, was sold to Barcelona for 65.4 million pounds. Savinho went to Tottenham Hotspur . Tijjani Reijnders went to Al-Qadsiah . Bernardo Silva left for Real Madrid on a free. In their place came Elliot Anderson for 116 million pounds, Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille , and, on the window's final day, Enzo Fernandez for a fee that equalled the British record. It is a total rebuild conducted at full speed, in public, by a manager in his first month. At the other end sits the season's genuine emergency. Tottenham Hotspur have played four Premier League matches and scored zero goals. Not one. They sit seventeenth with two points and a goal record of nought scored and five conceded, which is the sort of line that normally belongs to a side already cut adrift in April, not one four games into September under a coach hired precisely because he is supposed to make teams play. Roberto De Zerbi arrived from Marseille on March 31 on a long-term deal, with sporting director Johan Lange calling him one of the most creative and forward-thinking coaches in world football. The creativity has not yet shown up on a scoresheet. “We worked four years in the same structure and we always felt comfortable. Now, we need time.” Unai Emery , whose Aston Villa won the Europa League in May and have one point from four Neither a triumph nor a disaster, yet Between those poles, the picture is genuinely difficult to read. Andoni Iraola , who left Bournemouth for Liverpool in June, has one win and three draws from four: unbeaten, but blunted, and a goalless home afternoon against Fulham did nothing to quiet the question of whether his high-pressing model survives contact with the expectation at Anfield. He did at least win his European opener, edging Atletico Madrid 2-1. Michael Carrick 's Manchester United are thirteenth in the league but put four past Sabah in Europe. Matthias Jaissle inherited a Newcastle United side that sold its three best players in a single summer. And then there is Madrid. Jose Mourinho returned to the Bernabeu on June 11, signing until 2029, sixteen years after he first walked in and three managers after Xabi Alonso left in January. His Real Madrid have twelve points from five, beat Inter 2-1 on the opening night in Europe through Kylian Mbappe and Federico Valverde , and put four past Rayo Vallecano at the weekend. They are also, already, three points behind a Barcelona side that has won all five of its league games with a goal difference of plus seventeen. The reshuffle gave Madrid a serial winner. It did not give them a head start. The honest summary is that the market for managers behaved this year less like a market and more like a panic. Clubs did not so much choose replacements as grab whoever was nearest when the music stopped, and the reason the table already looks strange is that several of them grabbed well and several grabbed badly. The next three months will sort them. What is not in doubt is that the sport has never asked so many new men to answer so many questions at once. Arsenal lead on goal difference. Also in the lead Europe's Second Tier Opens, and Three English Clubs Step Into the Unknown The Europa League league phase begins tonight and tomorrow. Sunderland , Crystal Palace and Bournemouth have never been here in this form, and AC Milan and Juventus would rather not be. The Europa League returns this evening with the first of its eight league-phase matchdays, and the entry list tells you a great deal about how the last eighteen months have gone for some very large football clubs. AC Milan open at home to Benfica . Juventus host N.E.C. tomorrow. Celtic , Lyon , Marseille , Real Sociedad and Bayer Leverkusen are all here too. This is a deep field by any historical standard. For the three English entrants it is something closer to genuinely new territory. Sunderland begin at home to AZ Alkmaar tonight, seeded thirty-third of thirty-six and playing continental football for the first time in decades. Crystal Palace host Lech Poznan tomorrow, and Bournemouth , seeded eighth and the best placed of the three, travel to Real Sociedad under Marco Rose , who replaced Andoni Iraola in the summer. The format rewards consistency over survival. Each of the thirty-six clubs plays eight different opponents, the top eight go straight to the last sixteen, ninth to twenty-fourth drop into a knockout playoff round, and twenty-fifth or lower means elimination from Europe altogether. There is no group to escape and no easy draw to hide behind, which is why a slow start here is far more expensive than it used to be. The holders are not in the field. Aston Villa won this competition in May, beating SC Freiburg 3-0 in Istanbul through Youri Tielemans , Emiliano Buendia and Morgan Rogers for a first trophy in thirty years, and were promoted into the Champions League for their trouble. Two of those three scorers have since been sold. That is a story for the transfer pages, and it is not a happy one. Transfer News City Pay the British Record to Undo Their Own Midfield Enzo Fernandez cost 125 million pounds and reunites with the manager who sold him. Rodri went the other way. The single largest transaction of the summer was also its strangest. On deadline day, Manchester City paid Chelsea 125 million pounds for Enzo Fernandez , a fee that equals the British record set when Liverpool bought Alexander Isak from Newcastle United in 2025. The Argentine signed a five-year deal. The move was confirmed by Sky Sports , ESPN and Al Jazeera . Status: official. The symmetry is almost too neat. Enzo Fernandez now plays for Enzo Maresca , the manager who coached him at Stamford Bridge and was sacked by Chelsea on New Year's Day. Chelsea, meanwhile, booked an 18 million pound profit on a player they bought for 107 million three and a half years ago, which is a respectable piece of accounting and an awkward piece of squad-building. It was awkward because the replacement did not arrive. Chelsea had a 47 million pound deal in place for Lamine Camara when Monaco withdrew from the sale late, leaving Xabi Alonso a midfielder short on the day he lost his most expensive one. Chelsea honoured the Fernandez sale regardless. Set that against City's other business and a coherent, if severe, logic appears. Rodri was sold to Barcelona for 65.4 million pounds in mid-August after seven years and a World Cup win with Spain . Savinho and Omar Marmoush went to Tottenham Hotspur , the latter initially on loan. Tijjani Reijnders went to Al-Qadsiah for around 52 million pounds and Bernardo Silva left for Real Madrid for nothing at all. In came Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for 116 million pounds, Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille for a reported 81 million, and Iliman Ndiaye . City spent roughly 319 million pounds. They also tore out the spine of the most successful English side of the last decade and replaced it with players whose combined age barely reaches the one they sold. Madrid Build a Spine and Pay For Almost None of It Two of Jose Mourinho 's six signings arrived on free transfers. The one they did pay heavily for cost 140 million euros. Real Madrid 's summer is the clearest demonstration this year of what a club can do when it plans two years ahead of a contract cycle. Ibrahima Konate joined from Liverpool on a free transfer on a four-year deal, a move confirmed by ESPN and Sky Sports . Bernardo Silva arrived from Manchester City , also free, on a two-year deal. Status on both: official. The paid-for business was substantial. Marc Cucurella came from Chelsea in a deal Sky valued at 51.8 million pounds and Madrid's own books at around 60 million euros, announced by the club on June 15. Denzel Dumfries joined from Inter . And Yan Diomande arrived from RB Leipzig for a reported 140 million euros on a deal to 2033, the second-largest fee of the entire window. Endrick returned from a loan at Lyon . Out went an era. Dani Carvajal left at the end of his contract after twenty-three seasons at the club. David Alaba also departed as a free agent, and Dani Ceballos left by mutual agreement. Antonio Rudiger signed a one-year extension to 2027. Newcastle Sold Their Three Best Players, and Say They Would Do It Again Bruno Guimaraes , Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon all left in one window. The sporting director is unapologetic. No club in Europe had a stranger summer than Newcastle United . Sandro Tonali went to Tottenham Hotspur for 92.5 million pounds. Anthony Gordon went to Barcelona for a reported 69.3 million. Bruno Guimaraes , the captain and the emotional centre of the side, went to a Premier League rival for 75 million. The club then spent roughly 295 million pounds rebuilding. Eddie Howe had already gone, replaced by Matthias Jaissle . What is unusual is not the churn but the candour about it. Sporting director Ross Wilson told reporters that if you want to be a successful club in the Premier League you have to trade players, and that if you do not, you get stuck. He went further, naming Lewis Hall and Tino Livramento as players who may themselves leave in time. Chief financial officer Simon Capper was equally blunt about the mechanics, explaining that one incoming deal required Nick Woltemade 's loan to Juventus to clear the wage space first. This is profit and sustainability regulation as a design constraint rather than a threat, and it is worth watching closely, because Newcastle are describing openly what several of their rivals do quietly. The early league evidence is inconclusive: twelfth after four, one win, one defeat at home and a trip to face Hull City on Saturday. Paris Sold an Attack, Bought Another, and Forgot How to Win at Home Bradley Barcola left for Liverpool in a deal worth up to 123 million pounds. Luis Enrique says he could not promise him a starting place. Paris Saint-Germain are the reigning European champions and the five-time reigning champions of France. They are also, this morning, seventh in Ligue 1 with five points from four matches. The gap between those two sentences is the most interesting thing in French football. The squad turnover explains a good deal of it. Bradley Barcola joined Liverpool in a deal reported at up to 123 million pounds including variables. Goncalo Ramos went to AC Milan for around 63.7 million. In came Ferran Torres from Barcelona , among others. Luis Enrique was unusually direct about the Barcola exit, telling reporters that the player's desire was to play a more important role in the side, something the manager could not guarantee him. He called the window exceptional. The results have not agreed. Paris went four matches without a win, drawing twice from two goals down and losing 2-1 at home to Monaco on September 4, before finally beating Brest 1-0 on Sunday through, appropriately enough, Ferran Torres . Ousmane Dembele , the reigning Ballon d'Or holder, Desire Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia had gone four games without a goal between them. Then, on September 9, the same team put six past Slovan Bratislava in the Champions League with a Ferran Torres hat-trick. Whatever is wrong in Paris, it is not the forwards' finishing, and it is probably not permanent. Luis Enrique 's own assessment, offered with characteristic serenity, was an invitation to bet on who would be champion at the end of the season. The Window in One Picture The Six Biggest Fees of the Summer Window Enzo Fernandez Chelsea to Manchester City 125 Morgan Rogers Aston Villa to Chelsea 117 Elliot Anderson Nottingham Forest to Manchester City 116 Yan Diomande RB Leipzig to Real Madrid 107 Bradley Barcola Paris Saint-Germain to Liverpool 106 Sandro Tonali Newcastle United to Tottenham Hotspur 92.5 Reported fees in millions of pounds, on a single consistent basis. Arsenal's business is covered in the companion edition and is not shown. The Rumour Mill The window shut on September 1, so everything below is January business or contract business. Certainty labels are attached to each. Treat the unlabelled as gossip, because that is what it is. Bruno Fernandes and the option year Advanced talks, no agreement David Ornstein reported to Sky Sports after the Manchester derby that Bruno Fernandes remains in discussions with Manchester United over a new contract but that the parties have not found common ground. His deal expires at the end of this season and United hold a one-year extension option. The 32-year-old is the reigning PFA Players' Player of the Season, is nominated for this year's Ballon d'Or and has five goal involvements in five matches. This is the most consequential contract situation in England. JJ Gabriel wants out of Old Trafford Reported, single-sourced on the destination The Sun reports that Manchester United fear teenage forward JJ Gabriel will join Manchester City after asking to leave. The Athletic separately places Real Madrid in the running. Gabriel is fifteen. Both strands are credible on the player's desire to go and thin on where he goes. Endrick to United in January Speculative link AS in Spain suggests Manchester United could move for Endrick in January if the Brazilian becomes available. He has just returned to Real Madrid from a loan at Lyon and is behind Kylian Mbappe in the order. No talks have been reported by either club. Branthwaite, revived Concrete interest The Daily Mail reports that Manchester United have restarted their long pursuit of Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite . This link has been live in some form for three windows and has never yet reached a bid that Everton were willing to discuss. Araujo's option to buy Loan active, purchase undecided Ronald Araujo joined Liverpool from Barcelona in August on loan with an option to buy, confirmed by Liverpool and Sky Sports . Fabrizio Romano reported on September 13 that Liverpool are pleased with how the move has gone. Whether the option is exercised is the question that will define Liverpool's January. Barcelona want a number nine Gossip talkSPORT lists Harry Kane , Erling Haaland , Julian Alvarez and Nick Woltemade as Barcelona striker targets. That is less a shortlist than a list of good strikers, and it should be read accordingly. Separately, Sport reports the club is negotiating a contract extension with Raphinha , who has six league goals already. The Raphinha strand is the one worth following. Henderson set for a Palace payday Reported The Daily Mail reports Dean Henderson is poised to become Crystal Palace 's highest-paid player on a new contract, despite interest from Nottingham Forest . Around the Leagues Premier League Four matchdays in, the table has two perfect records at the top and a genuine curiosity beneath them. Manchester City are unbeaten with twelve points and won the Manchester derby 1-0 at Old Trafford on Sunday, a result that said as much about Michael Carrick 's side as Enzo Maresca 's: Manchester United are thirteenth with four points despite Bruno Fernandes playing some of the best football of his career. Behind the leaders, Leeds United and Hull City are third and fourth on eight points apiece, which nobody forecast in August. Daniel Farke 's Leeds are unbeaten. Sergej Jakirovic 's newly promoted Hull have taken points off Chelsea and Aston Villa already. The bottom of the table is where the season's real stories are. Tottenham Hotspur have not scored a league goal. Four matches, nought goals, two points, seventeenth, and a 0-0 at home to Everton on Saturday that extended the drought. Aston Villa are nineteenth with one point, which is remarkable for a team that lifted the Europa League in May. Their summer explains most of it: Morgan Rogers sold to Chelsea for 117 million pounds, Youri Tielemans and Ezri Konsa both gone, two of the three scorers from the final in Istanbul now playing elsewhere. Unai Emery has asked for patience, saying after a goalless draw with Hull City that his side deserved more and that he feels the team is progressing. Reports that the club is weighing Emery's position trace to a single former club scout speaking to Football Insider, and should be treated as exactly that thin. Villa did at least win 3-2 at Club Brugge in the Champions League through John McGinn , Emiliano Buendia and a first goal for Nicolas Jackson . Below Villa, Coventry City have the worst start of any promoted side in recent memory: four defeats, no points, no goals scored and ten conceded, including a 5-0 home defeat to Brighton on Sunday. Frank Lampard took them up and is discovering how unforgiving the step is. Liverpool sit eighth, unbeaten but drawn three times under Andoni Iraola , the goalless afternoon against Fulham the most telling of them. Brighton have scored thirteen in four, more than anyone. And Fulham are eighteenth with a point under Alvaro Arbeloa , who was managing Real Madrid in January and is now fighting relegation in west London, which may be the single most 2026 sentence in this edition. La Liga Barcelona have won all five, scored seventeen, conceded two and lead by three points. Raphinha is the division's top scorer with six. Lamine Yamal scored twice in Sunday's 4-2 win at Levante , where Karim Adeyemi also found the net. This is a side playing with the confidence of a double champion, which is what they are. Real Madrid are second on twelve, having beaten Rayo Vallecano 4-1 with two from Kylian Mbappe and goals for Alvaro Carreras and Jude Bellingham . Atletico Madrid are quietly excellent, winning 3-0 at Real Sociedad through Alejandro Grimaldo , Jonathan David and Giuliano Simeone . The genuine surprise is Alaves , third on ten points. The promoted clubs have brought real romance. Racing Santander are back after fourteen years and beat Alaves 2-1. Deportivo La Coruna are back after eight and sit sixth. Malaga , also back after eight, drew at Celta Vigo . At the other end, Valencia have one point from five, which for a club of that history is an alarm rather than a slow start. Bundesliga Three matchdays in and Bayern Munich are fourth. Above them, improbably, are SC Freiburg and Borussia Dortmund , both perfect on nine points. Freiburg, beaten Europa League finalists in May, thrashed Borussia Monchengladbach 5-0 on Saturday and have a goal difference of plus nine. Bayern have seven points from three after winning 2-1 at newly promoted SV Elversberg . More striking is who is not on the scorers list: Harry Kane , winner of the Torjagerkanone in each of his three seasons in Germany, is not among the leaders. The top of that chart is shared on three goals by Younes Ebnoutalib of Eintracht Frankfurt , Yuito Suzuki of Freiburg , Phillip Tietz of Mainz , Patrik Schick of Bayer Leverkusen and Michael Gregoritsch of Augsburg . SV Elversberg have become the fifty-ninth club to play in the Bundesliga and sit sixth with six points, having already beaten Monchengladbach 4-3 away. Schalke 04 are back after three years and won 3-1 at Union Berlin on Friday. RB Leipzig beat Hamburg 5-0 under Martin Demichelis , and Bayer Leverkusen have four points from three in Carles Martinez Novell 's first season. Serie A Saturday evening in Rome is the fixture of the European weekend. Roma and Inter are the only unbeaten sides, level on points with Roma ahead on goal difference, and they meet at the Stadio Olimpico at 18:00 local time. Gian Piero Gasperini called it an opportunity to measure up against the best and show his side can do better, which is about as close to a gauntlet as he throws. Roma's form is built on Donyell Malen , who has six goals in four matches, equalling a club record set by Francesco Totti in 2001-02, with Paulo Dybala supplying him. Gasperini has praised how the two complete each other. Inter, the reigning champions, have won all three of theirs but lost 2-1 at Real Madrid in Europe. Elsewhere the champions-elect narrative is getting complicated. Juventus lost 3-2 at Sassuolo on Sunday after leading, with former Juventus player Vasilije Adzic scoring the winner, and Luciano Spalletti is already fielding questions about his future despite public backing. AC Milan drew 2-2 at Lazio in Ruben Amorim 's latest outing, with Christian Pulisic registering his first assist of the season. And Fiorentina , who lost their first three, won 4-2 at Venezia thanks to a hat-trick from Franco Mastantuono , who became the youngest Argentinian to score one in Europe's top five leagues, a record previously held by Lionel Messi . Ligue 1 Three clubs share the lead on ten points: Lille , Monaco and Rennes . Davide Ancelotti 's Lille beat Troyes 2-0 on Sunday through Santos and a stoppage-time goal from Ethan Mbappe . Filipe Luis 's Monaco were held 1-1 at Strasbourg . Rennes beat Marseille 1-0 on Friday through Adrien Thomasson . Paris Saint-Germain finally won, 1-0 at Brest through Ferran Torres , and are seventh on five points. Marseille have now lost two in a row under Bruno Genesio and travel to Besiktas in the Europa League tomorrow. Auxerre claimed a first win of the season, 1-0 over Nice . French football also spent the summer in mourning. Eric Roy , who coached Brest to the Champions League and was still in post last season, died on June 17 at the age of 58 after an illness. Julien Lachuer has succeeded him at Brest. Major League Soccer Nashville SC are eight points clear at the top of the overall standings and closing on a first Supporters' Shield. They drew 2-2 at Inter Miami at the weekend in the fixture of the regular season, Lionel Messi putting Miami ahead before Sam Surridge equalised late. The draw denied Nashville a playoff berth they will clinch shortly anyway. Lionel Messi leads the Golden Boot race with eighteen. Behind the headline act, the league's most interesting attacking story is at Orlando City , where Antoine Griezmann has eight goals and, outside Messi himself, the best non-penalty goal contribution rate per ninety minutes of any player with ten or more starts this season. Orlando beat Toronto 3-0. Rafael Navarro has four goals in two starts for St. Louis City since a reported twelve million dollar trade from Colorado , Philadelphia beat San Diego 5-0 with a brace from Cavan Sullivan , who now has seventeen goal contributions in under 1,400 minutes, and Vancouver Whitecaps lead the Western Conference. The regular season ends on November 7 and MLS Cup is on December 18. Numbers of the Week 125 million pounds The fee Manchester City paid Chelsea for Enzo Fernandez , equalling the British record set by Alexander Isak 's move to Liverpool in 2025. 0 goals Tottenham Hotspur 's Premier League output in four matches under Roberto De Zerbi . They are seventeenth. 59 goals in 59 games Erling Haaland 's Champions League record after his double at Porto on the opening matchday. 6 goals in four games Donyell Malen 's start for Roma , equalling a club record set by Francesco Totti in 2001-02. In Brief The 2026 Ballon d'Or will be presented on Monday October 26 at the London Palladium, the award's seventieth anniversary and its first ceremony in London. Ousmane Dembele is the reigning holder and Paris Saint-Germain lead all clubs with nine nominations. Real Betis won their first Champions League match in twenty-one years, 3-2 at Lille , with two goals from Marc Bartra and one from Troy Parrott . Ethan Mbappe was sent off late for Lille. AEK Athens beat LASK 1-0 through a Razvan Marin free-kick for their first Champions League win in twenty years. LASK were making their debut in the competition. Thibaut Courtois made his hundredth Champions League appearance in Real Madrid 's win over Inter . Como marked their first Champions League campaign by beating RB Leipzig 4-1. The Women's Super League has expanded to fourteen clubs this season, with Charlton Athletic making their debut after an eighteen-year absence from the top flight and Birmingham City and Crystal Palace promoted. Liverpool lead the early table. Manchester United Women appointed Eva Olid in August after Marc Skinner left by mutual agreement. Front-of-shirt gambling sponsorship is banned in the Premier League from this season, and the calendar has been cut from five international breaks to four. What to Watch All times Pacific. k: Arsenal begin the Carabao Cup at Ipswich six months after losing its final, unbeaten in six and missing half a back four.
x: The Weekly Arsenal Digest All Arsenal, all week, since the start No. 5 Tuesday, September 15, 2026 In this edition The Lead Transfer News The Squad Hale End Arsenal Women Gunners Abroad Numbers of the Week In Brief What to Watch Collapse all sections The Lead The one trophy that keeps getting away Six wins from six, top of the league, and a manager days from signing a new contract. Tonight at Portman Road Arsenal restart the competition that humiliated them in March, with a defence held together by improvisation. Six months ago Arsenal walked up the Wembley steps as losers. Manchester City beat them 2-0 in the Carabao Cup final on 22 March, Nico O'Reilly scoring twice, and a season that ended with a first league title in twenty-two years began its run-in with a reminder that one pot has eluded this club since 1993. Tonight, at 12 noon Pacific, the Gunners walk out at Portman Road to start it all again. They do so having won everything they have played. The Community Shield against the same Manchester City , 3-0 . Coventry City at home, 3-0 . Aston Villa away, 1-0 . Chelsea at the Emirates, 2-1 . Napoli away in the Champions League, 1-0 . Sunderland at the Stadium of Light on Saturday, 2-0 . Eight goals scored in the Premier League, one conceded, twelve points from twelve, first on goal difference. What makes the run remarkable is who has not played a minute of it. William Saliba was withdrawn after half an hour of France 's World Cup semi-final defeat to Spain in July with a back problem the club described, in a statement on 23 July , as requiring a managed recovery programme and an absence of an extended period . There has been no surgery and, as of Mikel Arteta 's press conference on 11 September, no new timeline. That single absence reshaped the summer. Arsenal spent GBP 51m plus GBP 4m on Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa on 21 August, a signing the club framed explicitly as cover for a centre-back crisis, and Konsa made his full debut against Chelsea because Cristhian Mosquera had gone off injured at Villa Park. Jurrien Timber only returned to team training in the second week of September after a groin problem dating to March. Ben White limped out of Saturday's win with a groin strain and missed Monday's session. “He will have his chance. He will have his minutes, and he will have to earn them like anybody else.” Mikel Arteta on Max Dowman, 14 September So the team that lines up in Suffolk will be a guess. Kepa Arrizabalaga is the expected goalkeeper. Timber needs minutes and may take one centre-back slot; the other could go to Marli Salmon , the seventeen-year-old who signed his first professional contract on 29 August and has not appeared for the senior side since the FA Cup tie at Mansfield Town in March. Piero Hincapie and Myles Lewis-Skelly are the likelier full-backs. Further forward the interest is in the players who have been watching. Martin Zubimendi has not started a Premier League or Champions League match this season. Viktor Gyokeres has played twenty-seven minutes across the opening four league games and has yet to start one. Noni Madueke , Mikel Merino and Eberechi Eze are all in the same bracket: expensive, capable, and short of rhythm. And then there is Max Dowman , who is sixteen until New Year's Eve, sits outside the twenty-five-man Premier League list because of his age, and has been an unused substitute four times already, including in Naples. He played an hour for the under-21s against Chelsea on Saturday instead of travelling to Sunderland. Arteta would not promise a start, which in the current climate is its own kind of answer. Ipswich Town , back in the division and tenth with six points from four, are not a soft landing. They have scored seven and conceded ten, which is to say they will have a go. Arteta 's line all week has been that there is no second tier to this squad, and that every competition counts. The argument for taking him at his word is sitting in the Wembley record books, unpleasantly recent. Fabrizio Romano reported on 14 September that the extension is in its final stages , with lawyers working through the remaining details, and described Arteta as very, very close to signing. The proposed term is three years. The timeline matters. First contact with his representatives came in March or April, before the title was mathematically won. Josh Kroenke called a new deal an utmost priority in May. But a manager who has won the league, reached a domestic cup final and started the defence with six straight wins is not a difficult negotiation, and the direction of travel is unmistakable. Expect an announcement rather than a saga. Transfer News Zubimendi, Madrid and the January question nobody at the club wants asked A Spanish journalist says it is done. The evidence that matters is the team sheet. On 14 September Javi Roldan of El Confidencial said flatly that Martin Zubimendi is going to be Madrid's signing in the winter window . The figure attached by Spanish outlets is EUR 70m , the same sum Arsenal paid Real Sociedad in the summer of 2025. Treat the claim itself with care. It is one reporter, amplified by aggregators, with no corroboration from David Ornstein , Fabrizio Romano , the BBC or Sky. Nothing in it has reached even the concrete-interest tier. The underlying fact is another matter, and it is not in dispute. Zubimendi has made four substitute appearances in the Premier League and one in the Champions League this season. He has started neither competition. He lost his place late last season and the arrival of Bruno Guimaraes for GBP 75m has not made getting it back any easier. TEAMtalk add, on their own sourcing, that Zubimendi would be willing to push for an exit if he is not playing regularly by January, that Real Madrid have kept contact with his camp, and that Chelsea are watching. That is a plausible shape for a story rather than a story. It is also the kind of thing that becomes true if a player spends autumn on a bench. The window that was: a level-raiser that never arrived David Ornstein 's verdict on Arsenal's summer was blunt, and the numbers behind it are stranger than the headline suggests. Arsenal spent heavily and ended the window without the attacking signing they wanted. Ornstein 's assessment, published on 2 September and relayed by Daily Cannon, was that the club failed to land a level-raiser in attack, having pursued Vinicius Junior as the primary target and then Julian Alvarez , Malick Fofana , Bradley Barcola and Morgan Rogers . Christos Tzolis , at GBP 34m from Club Brugge , was a replacement for Leandro Trossard , not an addition. The Vinicius thread is worth closing properly, because it keeps being resurrected. Ornstein reported that Arsenal were prepared to commit major funds and that the move had been approved at every level of the club. Romano reported on 5 August that Real Madrid had improved their offer materially. On 6 August the player signed a six-year extension to 2032. Anyone still writing that link is recycling. Alvarez failed for a different and more bruising reason. Ornstein , on 29 August : the Argentine spoke to Mikel Arteta and said he doesn't want to come , his heart set on Barcelona . Atletico Madrid would have done a deal. Arsenal were prepared to agree one club to club. The player said no. k: The Champions League league phase opens on a redrawn map of Europe, with Mourinho at Real Madrid, Maresca at City and the holders PSG 14th in France.
x: The Weekly Soccer Digest World Football, Every Wednesday The Weekly Soccer Digest Vol. 1, No. 37 Wednesday, September 9, 2026 In This Edition The Lead · The Benches · Transfer News · The Rumour Mill · Around the Leagues · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead Europe Reopens on a Map Nobody Recognises The Champions League league phase began on Tuesday with the holders in disarray at home, a returning heavyweight in the Real Madrid dugout and a Manchester City side that has spent a decade being one thing learning to be another. Eighteen matches across three nights, and the shape of the season is already arguing with itself. T here is a version of this competition that reads exactly as you would expect. Real Madrid beat Inter . Manchester City won at Porto because Erling Haaland scored twice. Borussia Dortmund came from behind in front of the Yellow Wall. Read the six Tuesday scorelines cold and you would conclude that European football has spent the summer standing still. It has done the opposite. The men in the dugouts have almost all changed. The champions of Europe are 14th in their own league. The best player in the Premier League for a decade is playing in Turkey. And the two clubs who contested last season's final have between them lost a manager, a talisman and, in one case, an entire idea of themselves. Matchday one was not a continuation. It was an audit. Start at the Bernabéu, because that is where the noise is. José Mourinho returned to Real Madrid in June on a three-year deal, installed by a president who had just survived an election fought over a trophyless season, and his first European night back ended 2-1 against Inter . It should have been a coronation. Instead it was a survival exercise. Kylian Mbappé finished neatly on 14 minutes, Fede Valverde punished a calamitous piece of goalkeeping three minutes later, and then Madrid spent an hour missing chances while Thibaut Courtois made save after save. Carlos Augusto scored late. There were whistles at the final whistle of a home win. That anxiety has a cause, and it is not the Champions League. Four days earlier Madrid lost 1-0 at Real Betis , beaten by a Troy Parrott goal and by Álvaro Valles saving a stoppage-time Mbappé penalty. Madrid demanded a retake for encroachment; the referee and VAR said no, correctly under the letter of the law, since Marc Bartra still had a foot planted outside the area. Mourinho's response was pure Mourinho. "If the VAR did not order the penalty retaken because they do not know the rulebook," he said, "they need to go home." Madrid are third in La Liga, three points off Barcelona , with Rodrygo out until 2027 and Ferland Mendy out until April. Four matches without a win, seven points behind Monaco, and Paris Saint-Germain responded by extending the manager who won them back-to-back European Cups until 2030. On the same day they lost. Which brings us to the genuine oddity of this September. Paris Saint-Germain are the double defending champions of Europe. They beat Arsenal on penalties in Budapest in May after a 1-1 draw, then beat Aston Villa 2-1 in the Super Cup in August. They are also, as of Sunday night, 14th in Ligue 1 with two points from three games, beaten at the Parc des Princes by Monaco and beaten before that by Lens in the Trophée des Champions. Luis Enrique is not having it. Asked whether his players were physically short after a summer in which most of them went deep into a World Cup, he answered "No, no, no," pointed at the expected-goals numbers, and called the Monaco defeat "inexplicable". His club backed him on the spot: on Friday, hours before kick-off against Monaco, PSG announced contract extensions for Luis Enrique to 2030 and for João Neves , Willian Pacho , Lucas Beraldo , Senny Mayulu and Fabián Ruiz . The French press has settled on the word "préoccupant". Concerning, not yet a crisis. It is worth remembering they sold Bradley Barcola to Liverpool for a reported £106m and Gonçalo Ramos to Milan , and are integrating Ferran Torres and Maghnes Akliouche in their places. Manchester City , meanwhile, look ominously well. Enzo Maresca took a job nobody has held since 2016 and has won his first three league games and now his first European one, 2-0 at the Estádio do Dragão. Haaland scored on 67 and in stoppage time to reach 59 goals in 59 Champions League appearances, four days after his winner against Coventry City became the 300th goal of his career. City spent something close to £320m rebuilding a midfield they had gutted, selling Rodri to Barcelona and buying Elliot Anderson , Ayyoub Bouaddi and, on deadline day, Enzo Fernández from Chelsea . "The squad is complete," Maresca said. On the evidence of eleven days, he is not wrong. The romance came from further down the pots. AEK Athens won a Champions League match for the first time in 20 years, Răzvan Marin bending in a free kick to beat LASK . Real Betis , in their first Champions League game in 21 years, went to Lille, fell behind twice and won 3-2 with two Marc Bartra headers either side of half-time and a Parrott finish on the hour. Wednesday at the Maradona is a test of the squad, not the eleven. T he plane sat on the tarmac at Luton for most of Tuesday afternoon. A technical failure in the UK's air traffic control flight-processing system grounded departures nationwide, and Arsenal , who should have been walking out for a routine evening press conference inside the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, instead landed in Naples at around half past nine local time. UEFA waved through the cancellation of Mikel Arteta 's media duties. The champions of England arrive in southern Italy having lost a day of preparation and gained a small, useful grievance. It is a fittingly awkward overture. Arsenal come into this competition carrying a wound that has not properly closed: the Champions League final in May, lost to Paris Saint-Germain , the one trophy the Arteta era has reached for and dropped. They also arrive as domestic champions with a perfect start, nine points from nine, six goals scored and one conceded, and a manager whose contract is being rewritten around him. The mood is good. The medical room is not. Key Facts: Napoli v Arsenal Match. Napoli v Arsenal , UEFA Champions League league phase, matchday one. When. Wednesday, September 9. 20:00 BST, which is 12:00 noon Pacific . Where. Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, Naples. TNT Sports in the UK. Referee. Glenn Nyberg ( Sweden ). Form. Arsenal have won all four competitive matches this season and conceded once. Napoli have lost two of three in Serie A. Context. Arsenal 's first European tie since losing the 2026 final to Paris Saint-Germain . William Saliba is the absence that reorganises everything. He aggravated a pre-existing back problem playing for France in their World Cup semi-final defeat to Spain , was substituted, and has not played since. Saliba is the defender who has started more Premier League minutes than any other Arsenal player of the last four years. Arsenal confirmed that extensive assessment concluded surgery was not recommended and that he faces a period of rehabilitation rather than an operation, which is the better of two bad outcomes. Reported target dates have crept towards late November. Nobody at the club will put a number on it. So the centre of Arsenal 's defence on Wednesday is likely to be Ezri Konsa , signed from Aston Villa for a fee reported at around £55m and handed his debut against Chelsea on Sunday, alongside Gabriel Magalhaes . That is not a crisis pairing. It is, however, a pairing with two matches of history, and it will spend Wednesday night in a stadium that specialises in making visiting defenders feel their inexperience. Cristhian Mosquera , who would otherwise be the natural deputy, sat out training on Tuesday with the muscular problem he picked up at Villa Park and is expected to miss out. Arsenal 2-1 Chelsea The Window, Reviewed The forward Arsenal never signed, and the one they will meet on Saturday Vinicius, Rogers, Barcola, Fofana, Alvarez. Five chased, none landed. Then the club sold its two remaining Brazilians. David Ornstein's verdict is blunt, and Saturday at the Stadium of Light provides an uncomfortable illustration. David Ornstein of The Athletic has put it about as plainly as an insider of his standing tends to: Arsenal 's primary summer ambition was to add an elite, prime-age attacker, and they did not do it. The list is long. Vinicius Junior was Arteta 's preferred target and signed a new contract at Real Madrid instead. Morgan Rogers went to Chelsea for a reported British record £117m after Arsenal declined to go that far. Bradley Barcola was valued by Paris Saint-Germain at a figure that made the conversation academic. Yan Diomande joined Real Madrid . Julian Alvarez told Atletico Madrid 's sporting director on September 1 that he was staying. The one that stings is Malick Fofana . Arsenal had agreed personal terms with the 21-year-old Belgium winger, who wanted the move; Lyon wanted €40m and would not restructure. Ornstein and Fabrizio Romano both reported Arsenal 's unwillingness to meet the asking price. Fofana travelled instead to Wearside and signed for Sunderland through 2031. Arsenal play at Sunderland on Saturday evening. Sporting director Andrea Berta would argue, with some justification, that the summer was not a failure. Bruno Guimaraes at £75m is a genuine upgrade in the engine room. Ezri Konsa and Piero Hincapie were bought before Saliba 's injury turned centre-back depth from a luxury into an emergency. Illan Meslier arrived free from Leeds United . And Tzolis , at £34m from Club Brugge after 17 goals and 23 assists in 36 league games in Belgium, was signed explicitly as the Trossard replacement and has started like a man who intends to be more than that. The counter-argument is arithmetic. Arsenal began the summer with Martinelli , Jesus , Trossard and Nwaneri on the books and ended it with none of them, having added one senior forward. Berta 's refusal to be held to ransom is a defensible institutional posture. It is also, at the moment, a squad with Bukayo Saka , Kai Havertz and Odegaard carrying an enormous load through a calendar that could run past 60 matches, all three of them having had surgery in the past two years. January is now the pressure point. All of it is at the interest-and-conversation stage. None of it is close. Transfer News Martinelli gone to Al-Hilal for £60m, three days after the deadline The most expensive sale in Arsenal's history, completed through the loophole that lets European clubs sell after they can no longer buy. Gabriel Martinelli is an Al-Hilal player . The 25-year-old Brazil winger completed a four-year deal in Saudi Arabia late on Thursday, September 4, for a guaranteed fee widely reported in the British press at £60m, which makes him the most expensive departure Arsenal have ever sanctioned. The timing looked strange and was not. The English window shut on September 1; UEFA's rules restrict European clubs from buying after their domestic deadline, not from selling. The Saudi Pro League window remained open. Arsenal therefore had three extra days in which a bid they were willing to accept could arrive, and it did. That Arteta had left Martinelli out of the matchday squad for the opening two league fixtures was read at the time as a signal, and it was. He leaves after seven years, having made 53 appearances and scored 11 goals in the title-winning season. His unveiling video carried the line "proud to be blue, proud to be Al-Hilal," which will read oddly in N5 for a while. He joins Ollie Watkins at the club. The knock-on is a left flank thinned to the bone. Trossard to Besiktas , Martinelli to Al-Hilal , Nwaneri to Dortmund . Tzolis and Eberechi Eze are the senior options, with Noni Madueke able to switch and Max Dowman pressing from Hale End. Jesus joins Barcelona, and Arteta defends the decision to let both Brazilians go A reported £8.6m for a striker who arrived in 2022 as the signing that changed the mood at the club. Gabriel Jesus signed for Barcelona on September 1 for a fee reported at around £8.6m, closing a four-year spell that began with one of the most consequential transfers of the Arteta rebuild and ended with a serious knee injury and a place in the pecking order behind Viktor Gyokeres and Havertz . Arteta addressed both Brazilian departures on September 5, praising what Jesus and Martinelli gave the club and defending the summer's calls. His argument, in essence: Arsenal are not in the business of keeping players who will not play, and the money released is money available later. It is worth recording what Jesus was. He arrived in July 2022 for £45m from Manchester City and within a month had persuaded a fanbase that Arsenal were serious again. The trophies came after his best football. The single most important piece of Arsenal business this autumn will not involve a transfer fee. Mikel Arteta 's contract expires at the end of this season. Graeme Bailey of TEAMtalk reports that talks, which began in January and accelerated over the summer, have gone well, and that there is a growing expectation an agreement will be in place by the September international break in the last week of the month. The question is whether the bodies last. The most striking thing about Arsenal 's 2-1 win over Chelsea was not the comeback. It was the shape, or rather the refusal to hold one. Havertz , Odegaard and Saka rotated positions continuously through the first hour, and Chelsea never located a reference point. Arteta called it an incredible game to watch and to coach, and singled out the dynamics and the fluidity. And the longer game: Fabrizio Romano reported on August 29 that Arsenal have agreed terms to sign Andria Bartishvili , a Georgian attacking midfielder, when he turns 18 on March 30, 2027. He is on loan at Iberia 1999 from Kolkheti , with two goals and three assists in 20 appearances. Deals struck this far in advance are the clearest tell of a recruitment department working ahead of the market. Arsenal Women A rebuilt Arsenal win at the first attempt, and Lisa Baum announces herself Nine out, eight in, four debutants in the XI, and a nineteen-year-old settled it inside the first half at Broadfield. Renee Slegers did not so much refresh her squad as replace large parts of it. Out went Manuela Zinsberger , Laia Codina , Victoria Pelova , Rosa Kafaji , Laila Harbert , Jenna Nighswonger and Naomi Williams , plus two departures that will sting on matchdays: Beth Mead to Manchester City and Katie McCabe to Chelsea . In came eight. Georgia Stanway from Bayern Munich , Ona Batlle from Barcelona , Misa Rodriguez from Real Madrid , Geraldine Reuteler from Eintracht Frankfurt , Selina Cerci from Hoffenheim , Isabella Damm from Brondby , Lisa Baum from RB Leipzig , and on deadline day the France defender Elisa De Almeida from Paris Saint-Germain for a reported £550,000. Four of them started the WSL opener at Brighton on Sunday, and one of them won it. Baum , 19, collected the ball in the Brighton half , drove directly at the defence and finished into the roof of the net. Arsenal won 1-0 at Broadfield Stadium. Alessia Russo had two chances to make it comfortable and took neither; Fran Kirby threatened for the hosts before half-time; Rodriguez made a strong early save when Kiko Seike broke clear, and a couple more after the interval. Caitlin Foord and Chloe Kelly came on late. The statistical curio of the weekend belongs to Stanway , who became the first midfielder on record to complete more than 100 passes on a WSL debut for a club. Batlle pushed high from the left and combined repeatedly with Baum . Slegers was pleased and pointedly unsatisfied, saying afterwards the side need greater control in future matches. Second last season is the reference point they are trying to move past. De Almeida 's arrival addresses a specific hole. She is a 28-year-old centre-back who can play right-back, and she is Arsenal 's first specialist centre-back signing since Codina in 2023, brought in with Katie Reid still working back from an ACL injury. BBC Sport's Emma Sanders reported the deal first. Europe will be brutal.
