k: A record 3.46 billion pound Premier League window closed with Enzo Fernandez joining Manchester City for 125m and two agreed deals collapsing after the buzzer.
x: The Weekly Soccer Digest World football, reported and explained Wednesday, September 2, 2026 · The Deadline Week Edition In this edition The Lead · Messi Steps Away · The Boardroom War · Transfer News · The Rumour Mill · Around the Leagues · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead The night the window broke its own record, then broke its word English clubs spent 3.46 billion pounds and sent a British record fee across Manchester. Then, in the two hours after the 11pm buzzer, two agreed deals fell apart and left Chelsea, Everton and Monaco staring at each other across the wreckage. T he 2026 summer window did not so much close as buckle. By the time the Premier League's 11pm deadline passed on Tuesday night, English clubs had committed a record 3.46 billion pounds in gross spending, comfortably beating the previous high of 3.14bn, with 475m of it transacted on the final day alone. The figures come from FootballTransfers founder Paul Macdonald , supplied to BBC Sport. They describe a market with no ceiling, only a clock. The headline act was a 200-mile move that felt like a defection. Enzo Fernandez left Chelsea for Manchester City for 125 million pounds , equalling the British record set twelve months earlier when Liverpool paid the same for Alexander Isak. Sky Sports and ESPN both reported a five-year contract. The Argentine had told Chelsea he wanted to go more than three months ago; the club set a bid deadline a fortnight out and held to it. Chelsea banked an 18m profit on the 107m they gave Benfica three and a half years ago, a modest return on a player of that stature and a sign of how completely the Stamford Bridge trading model now governs football decisions. There is a symmetry to where he landed. Enzo Maresca , Fernandez's head coach at Chelsea for a year and a half until December 2025, is now in the City dugout, appointed on 29 June to replace Pep Guardiola after a decade and costing around 17m in compensation. He inherits the two domestic cups, the most expensive midfield reconstruction in the sport's history, and two wins from two. Key Facts Manchester City rebuilt a midfield from scratch Out this summer: Rodri to Barcelona, Bernardo Silva to Real Madrid on a free, Tijjani Reijnders In: Enzo Fernandez 125m, Elliot Anderson 116m, Ayyoub Bouaddi 86m Combined outlay on those three: 327m pounds Club-record gross spend for the window: 458m pounds , net 154m Sources: Sky Sports, ESPN, FootballTransfers via BBC Sport And then the deadline passed, and the evening turned strange. Chelsea had spent the day executing a plan: sell Fernandez, replace him with Lamine Camara of Monaco for 47m. Sky's Kaveh Solhekol , who drove the coverage, reported that the agreement was written, signed and subject only to a medical, with a six-year contract waiting and the player booked to fly into London. Monaco had been willing to sell a first-team midfielder because they believed they were about to receive 40m from Everton for Folarin Balogun . That Balogun deal wobbled. The striker travelled to Merseyside and something in the medical gave Everton's doctors pause. Reporting from RMC Sport and Get French Football News described a failed medical; Monaco and the player's camp insisted he was fit, having played through the World Cup with a minor problem. Everton went back and renegotiated the terms. Monaco, suddenly comfortable again that the money was coming, informed Chelsea in writing that they were withdrawing from the Camara agreement . That notification arrived after 11pm. “Everything was done, written, agreed, signed. He was flying into London.” Kaveh Solhekol, Sky Sports, on Chelsea's collapsed move for Lamine Camara Then came the last turn of the screw. Shortly after midnight, with the deal sheets still running and Everton believing they had their striker, Balogun changed his mind and pulled out. Everton were described in Sky's reporting as stunned. So Monaco kept both players, Chelsea got neither, and Everton, having already sold Beto to Fiorentina for 15.4m, went to bed with Thierno Barry as their only recognised centre-forward. The detail that matters most is what Chelsea did next, which was nothing. They held a contractual option to cancel the Fernandez sale if the replacement fell through. They chose not to use it. Sky reported the club described Monaco's conduct as extraordinary and deeply unprofessional, and honoured their side anyway. It will be relitigated every time Chelsea's midfield looks light between now and January, and it has left a live grudge between two clubs who must talk again in four months. Zoom out and the window's shape is clear enough. The money moved toward two poles: Manchester City rebuilding for a new manager, and Liverpool spending 123m on Bradley Barcola to replace a departed Mohamed Salah . Four of the five largest transfers in Premier League history were completed in this single window. Tottenham spent 302m and have started the season with two defeats, no goals and bottom place. Ipswich Town , promoted in May, spent 171m. This is the first window run under the league's new Squad Cost Ratio regime, which replaced PSR in November on a 14 to 6 vote and caps squad spending at 85 per cent of revenue with a six-point deduction waiting at the red threshold. The first assessment checkpoint arrives in October. Somebody is going to fail it. What the numbers cannot capture is the sense that the deadline has stopped functioning as a deadline. Deal sheets extended completions by two hours. A signed agreement was torn up after the buzzer with no consequence. A player who had passed a medical walked away at half past midnight. The transfer window is supposed to be the one moment in football where the paperwork binds. On Tuesday night it was a suggestion. Continental fees use each outlet's conversion, so read them as close approximations. Messi closes the international book, and then scores four Six weeks after losing a World Cup final, Argentina's most capped player and record scorer said goodbye to the shirt. Two days earlier he had produced the best individual night of his MLS career. On Monday, Lionel Messi announced on Instagram that he had played his last match for Argentina . He is 39. The statement was drafted on 21 July, two days after the World Cup final, and he said the death of his father Jorge on 8 August made him more certain of it. He leaves with 207 caps and 125 goals, both national records, alongside the 2022 World Cup, the 2021 and 2024 Copa America titles and Olympic gold from 2008. He also holds the World Cup records for appearances, 34, and assists, 12, and is the oldest outfield player ever to start a final. The timing is worth sitting with. Argentina lost the final in New Jersey to Spain , 1-0 after extra time, to a goal from Ferran Torres . Messi finished as the tournament's second-highest scorer and made the Best XI. There was no decline to point at and no injury to blame. He decided a sixth World Cup was the end of the road and closed it himself rather than waiting to be closed out. A 2028 Copa America appearance has not been formally ruled out, but nothing in the statement invited that reading. Club football, meanwhile, is going rather well. On Saturday night Inter Miami beat CF Montreal 7-1, a club record for goals in a match, and Messi scored four of them and assisted a fifth . Two were direct free kicks. It took him to 927 career goals, to 74 free-kick goals, third all-time, and to 98 for Inter Miami. He is the 19th player in MLS history to score four in a game, and reached 20 multi-goal MLS matches in 72 appearances, faster than anyone before him. The win also ended a five-game winless run, which was the actual point of the evening. He now leads the Golden Boot race on 18 goals and 10 assists, and is chasing a third straight MVP. UEFA moves to prosecute the FIFA president A plan to sell a fifth of the World Cup's commercial arm to private investors has been withdrawn. The war it started has not been. The most consequential football story of the week involves no players. FIFA proposed creating a private commercial vehicle, FIFA Forward Enterprise, to run World Cup commercial operations, and selling a 21 per cent minority stake at a 20 billion dollar valuation to raise roughly 4.2bn. The lead investor was to be Thrive Capital, run by Joshua Kushner , with JP Morgan involved. Member associations were offered 40m dollars each over four years to approve it, on a 53-day deadline. All 55 UEFA members rejected it unanimously and threatened to withdraw European teams from every FIFA competition, which put the Women's Under-20 World Cup in September, the Under-17 tournament in October and the 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil directly at risk. Concacaf's 41 nations also refused, citing the artificially short deadline and the absence of any review. FIFA folded. On 27 August, UEFA published a statement from its national association representatives confirming that FIFA had committed in writing to withdrawing the scheme irrevocably and permanently, and that the boycott threat was suspended. The same statement called the affair a profound failure of judgement and an abuse of presidential power, said the trust required to hold the FIFA presidency has been broken and cannot be restored, and committed the signatories to backing alternative candidates should Gianni Infantino seek re-election. Sky Sports reported the same day that UEFA is preparing criminal proceedings against Infantino in Switzerland for criminal mismanagement under Article 158, and has filed in the Southern District of New York to subpoena FIFA and its banks. Kushner, speaking publicly on Monday, said Thrive had failed to appreciate the political dynamics of global football. Aleksander Ceferin has called the proposal a shady, opaque backroom deal. The tournaments are safe. The presidency is not. Transfer News Liverpool spend 123m to fill a hole Salah left Andoni Iraola's first window emptied the dressing room of its landmarks and replaced them with one very expensive winger. Liverpool completed the signing of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain on Monday, one day before the deadline, for a total Sky Sports put at 123m pounds : 106m guaranteed plus add-ons, on a five-year contract. It is the second most expensive signing in the club's history behind Isak. French coverage frames the same deal at around 140m euros rising to 145m, and reports it as the largest sale in PSG's history, beating the 90m Neymar fee, and the biggest fee ever paid for a player leaving Ligue 1. Lyon , his first club, collect around 4.9m in solidarity payments. Reporters Mark McAdam and Lyall Thomas had the 120m agreement in principle on 29 August; PSG had been asking 145m. The scale of the churn at Anfield is what makes the fee legible. Mohamed Salah left on a free for Trabzonspor in August, ending his contract a year early by mutual consent after a season in which Arne Slot dropped him, and departing as the club's third-highest scorer with 257 goals in 442 games. Ibrahima Konate and Andy Robertson also left on frees, Konate to Real Madrid . Curtis Jones went to Inter for 30m on 21 August after 16 years, and Harvey Elliott joined Valencia on loan on deadline day. In came Barcola, Jeremy Jacquet from Rennes for 72m in July, and Lucca Brughmans from Genk for 30m, immediately loaned back. Jamie Carragher, on Sky, put the obvious question about fit: he called Barcola a great player but a left winger, which is a polite way of noting that Liverpool already have Cody Gakpo there. Which brings us to the loose end. ESPN reported that Liverpool rejected an 80m bid from Manchester City for Gakpo, who was understood to be open to the move, and that City then pivoted to Ndiaye. He is still a Liverpool player. He will not be a quiet one in January. Spain closes: Madrid stand still, Barcelona register at the buzzer Jose Mourinho wanted a midfielder and a left-footed centre-back. He got neither, and said so through intermediaries rather than in a press conference. Real Madrid did no deadline-day business at all. Journalist Jose Felix Diaz reported that the club had closed the window, with Mourinho's requested midfielder unavailable because Barcelona had already taken Rodri , and Inter refusing to sell Alessandro Bastoni . Eduardo Camavinga attracted Premier League interest and Raul Asencio was made available; both declined to leave. It caps a window in which Madrid still spent around 225m euros, their heaviest since 2019: Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig for a club record reported between 125m and 140m, Marc Cucurella at 55m, Denzel Dumfries at 20m and free transfers for Konate and Bernardo Silva . One Madrid player did move, and it is a homecoming. Dani Ceballos signed for Real Betis on a free in the early hours of Wednesday, a three-year deal to June 2029, at the club that developed him between 2014 and 2017 before Madrid paid 16.5m for him. Fabrizio Romano confirmed it with the phrase he reserves for done deals. Betis had to clear salary-cap room to register him. Barcelona finished theirs on Wednesday morning by registering Gabriel Jesus , signed for around 10m euros plus variables on a deal to 2029, and goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic , bought from Fenerbahce for 2m plus 500,000 in variables. Both cleared La Liga registration with room to spare, which is not a sentence Barcelona have been able to write in recent summers, though club reporting notes the limits were less severe rather than absent. Livakovic had been close to a loan back to Dinamo Zagreb had it failed. Elsewhere, Atletico Madrid took Jonathan David on loan from Juventus with a 25m euro purchase option spread over four financial years, giving Diego Simeone a third senior centre-forward behind Julian Alvarez and Alexander Sorloth. And Sevilla closed 27 operations across the window, 16 of them exits, and did three on the final day: Felix Correia from Lille, Lucas Stassin from Saint-Etienne and Youssouf Fofana from Milan, registered five minutes past midnight. Serie A bought the whole squad on credit Loans with options, loans with obligations, loans with buy-backs. Italy's window closed at eight o'clock on Tuesday evening and almost nothing about it was permanent. The single biggest Italian deal of deadline day was Jonathan Rowe from Bologna to Atalanta , reported by Gianluca Di Marzio as a 40m euro package built from a 5m loan fee, a 30m obligation to buy and 5m in bonuses, and by Sky Italia as 35m plus 5m. Juventus took Nick Woltemade on a season-long loan from Newcastle and Pape Matar Sarr from Tottenham on a 2.5m loan with a 27.5m right to purchase, while sending Jonathan David to Madrid. Lazio brought in Albert Gudmundsson from Fiorentina on loan with a 12m to 13m option, having already borrowed Davide Frattesi from Inter, who has now scored in both his league appearances for them. Fiorentina ran the busiest desk in the country and moved both ways at once: in came Pedro Goncalves from Sporting on a 2.5m loan with a 22.5m option and Willy Gnonto from Leeds, out went Moise Kean to Como on loan. Como also signed Robert Sanchez from Chelsea on a season loan filed, per Italian reporting, 40 seconds before the deadline. The loudest Italian story, though, is about a deal that did not happen. Roma chased a wide forward all summer for Gian Piero Gasperini , first Jamie Leweling of Stuttgart , then Luiz Henrique of Zenit at a proposed 5m loan and 30m option. Alfredo Pedulla reported an acceleration on the second and Corriere dello Sport reported a preliminary 35m agreement on the first, which then died because, in the paper's words, the bureaucratic machinery of medicals, contracts and signatures could not complete registration in time. Neither arrived. Roma also walked away from Gittens and successfully resisted bids for Manu Kone . Gasperini leads the table having scored eight and conceded none, and still does not have the player he has asked for across two seasons. Eurosport's window verdicts had Inter and Roma joint top on eight out of ten and Napoli bottom of the big clubs on 4.5. Leverkusen spend 60m in the closing week, Dortmund react to a knee Germany's window shut cleanly on 1 September, and the two most interesting moves were made by clubs solving very different problems. Bayer Leverkusen were the biggest spenders of the final week. Guela Doue arrived from Strasbourg on a five-year deal to 2031, for a fee reported at 30m euros fixed rising to around 36m, though one German outlet puts the ceiling at 37.5m. The Ivory Coast right-back, brother of PSG's Desire, played all four of his country's World Cup matches. Sporting director Simon Rolfes said the club had strengthened excellently at right-back. On the same day Leverkusen brought Moussa Diaby home from Al-Ittihad for a reported 30m, on a contract through 2031, four years after he left a club where he produced 49 goals and 48 assists in 173 games. Diaby said he did not hesitate for a second. Their reward was a 3-2 defeat at newly promoted SV Elversberg . Borussia Dortmund 's deadline-day loan was a direct response to an injury. Giannis Konstantelias , signed from PAOK this summer, scored on the stroke of half-time against Hamburger SV on 29 August and tore the anterior cruciate ligament in his left knee seven minutes into the second half. The club confirmed it the next day. Sporting director Lars Ricken said the news hit them hard. Two days later Dortmund took Ethan Nwaneri , 18, on a season-long loan, with Ricken describing him as a very talented and technically gifted midfielder. Bundesliga's own coverage explicitly linked the two events. Elsewhere: RB Leipzig signed Marc Guiu , 20, from Chelsea on a five-year deal for a reported 15m pounds and borrowed Neil El Aynaoui from Roma. Hamburger SV had the busiest final day, taking Fabio Vieira permanently plus Zakaria El Ouahdi and David Moller Wolfe . Union Berlin sold Ilyas Ansah to Hull City in a reported club-record sale. Per Sky Germany's Florian Plettenberg , Borussia Monchengladbach took Nicolas Kuhn from Como on loan with no option, and SC Freiburg paid Karlsruher SC around 7m plus bonuses for Louey Ben Farhat and loaned him straight back. Lille bank 165m in seven days. Marseille sell and do not buy France closed at 19:59 on Tuesday. Two clubs used the window in almost opposite ways, and both are now interesting for it. In the space of a week, Lille sold Ayyoub Bouaddi to Manchester City for 100m euros and Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Newcastle for a figure reported variously as 60m, 65m and 66m. The Bouaddi deal, struck on 26 August, was reported as the largest sale by a Ligue 1 club to a foreign club, and Sky renders it as 86m pounds: 81.3m fixed plus 4.3m. City called it the most expensive teenage signing in Premier League history, beating the 58.9m Manchester United paid for Leny Yoro. Bouaddi is 18 and Moroccan and said he has watched City for years. Lille, under first-year head coach Davide Ancelotti , reinvested a fraction of it on Ayase Ueda from Feyenoord at 15m and a loan for Dilane Bakwa , who scored against PSG two days after arriving. They sit joint second. Marseille did the reverse and it is close to a crisis of stock. Their only summer arrival was Timothy Weah from Juventus for 14m on 1 July. Out went Quinten Timber to Crystal Palace for 20m, Leonardo Balerdi to Roma on loan, Facundo Medina to Leverkusen for 23m, Mason Greenwood to Fenerbahce for 39m and Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang to Deportivo. Head coach Bruno Genesio , who crossed from Lille in the summer, said before the deadline that three or four players would need to leave before the club could register one or two arrivals. Per L'Equipe, Marseille now plan to sign two free agents outside the window, a goalkeeper and the 33-year-old Karl Toko Ekambi , who has accepted what the paper called a derisory salary. President Stephane Richard went on RMC on Wednesday to say the club is not for sale but is open to new investors alongside Frank McCourt. The best small story of the French window was the tug of war over Malick Fofana . Sunderland had terms agreed at around 35m euros; Crystal Palace hijacked late with a reported 39m; negotiations restarted; Fofana ended up back at Sunderland's original numbers. Lyon's own regulatory filing, published Wednesday, gives the total as up to 35m euros, being 30m plus 5m in bonuses, with a 12.5 per cent sell-on. Sunderland majority shareholder Kyrill Louis-Dreyfus flew to Lyon to finish it before the English 1am cutoff. Lyon then used their post-deadline joker slot to sign Keito Nakamura from Reims for up to 20m. PSG signalled through RMC's Fabrice Hawkins that they were done, and L'Equipe reported Ousmane Dembele has agreed a two-year extension to 2030, still unsigned. MLS shuts its own window today, and Miami changed the coach first The 2026 secondary window ran 13 July to 2 September, the first time in two decades that it has stretched into September. Roster freeze follows on 9 October. The most consequential MLS move of the week was not a player. Inter Miami appointed Cristian "Kily" Gonzalez as head coach, replacing Guillermo Hoyos , who stays on in an interim capacity until work permits clear. Hoyos took over when Javier Mascherano stepped down in April, months after winning MLS Cup, was made permanent after the World Cup break, started with 19 points from a possible 24, then went five without a win. Gonzalez is from Rosario like Messi, won 56 caps for Argentina, played for Valencia, Zaragoza and Inter, and played alongside Messi in Argentina's 2005 qualifiers. Asked whether Messi influenced the appointment, Hoyos said he has the influence players of that stature naturally command. On the player side, Miami added the 19-year-old winger Riquelme Fillipi from Palmeiras through 2029-30 on a U22 Initiative slot, and bought an international roster slot from New England for 200,000 dollars. The Chicago Fire signed Johan Gomez , Anzor Mekvabishvili and Andreas Hanche-Olsen from Braunschweig, Craiova and Mainz. Seattle 's has already paid off: Dejan Joveljic , bought from Sporting Kansas City for 6m dollars cash on 25 August as a Designated Player through June 2030, scored twice on debut in a 2-2 draw with Chicago, only the second player to do so for the Sounders. Atlanta United paid a reported 18m dollars for Breel Embolo , and LA Galaxy added Hirving Lozano , Sergi Roberto and Kyogo Furuhashi while selling Gabriel Pec to Cruzeiro for a club record. The Rumour Mill The window is shut, so everything below is either a free agent who can sign tomorrow or a January story that started this week. Certainty is labelled on every item. Julian Alvarez to Barcelona. Concrete interest, deferred On 1 September the Argentine told Atletico Madrid sporting director Mateu Alemany he was staying, turning down both Barcelona and a serious Arsenal push. Chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin said his personal dream was for Alvarez to remain. The follow-up, reported Wednesday by Santi Ovalle of El Larguero, is that Barcelona will come back in January 2027 or the following June, and that they signed Gabriel Jesus cheaply precisely so that the money earmarked for a marquee number nine stays in the bank. The obstacle is structural rather than financial: Atletico will not negotiate with a domestic rival at all, and Al Jazeera reported their asking price at around 150m euros. Nothing is agreed and nothing can be until the winter window. Cody Gakpo to Manchester City. Bid rejected, on ice ESPN reported an 80m pound City bid turned down by Liverpool, with the player understood to favour the move before City redirected the money to Iliman Ndiaye. The arrival of Barcola on the same flank does not obviously help Liverpool's argument for keeping him. Lamine Camara to Chelsea. Agreement signed, then withdrawn Covered in full in the lead. The relevant forward-looking fact is that Chelsea sold their first-choice holding midfielder and signed nobody to replace him, which makes this the cleanest January storyline in England, and that relations between Chelsea and Monaco are now badly damaged. Mauro Icardi to Lazio. Offer made, paused Icardi is a free agent and can sign at any time. Lazio , through president Claudio Lotito and sporting director Angelo Fabiani , made an offer. His agent Elio Letterio Pino said on Wednesday that Fabiani had been very kind and the possibility was real, but that they had decided to stop and wait a moment. Pino added that Icardi wants a two-to-three year project rather than the biggest cheque, and revealed that Juventus also made an approach about January. Sky Italia reported the Lazio offer was rejected as insufficient. Alfredo Pedulla has been tracking it. Treat the whole thread as live but stalled. Roma's missing winger, second attempt. Both targets dead, January priority Eurosport's post-window audit describes the squad as short for three competitions and the wide forward as the priority in January. Corriere dello Sport also took the trouble to debunk a widely shared story that Roma had chartered a plane to Germany for Leweling. They had not. Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, Marseille to Juventus. Unresolved at the deadline Juventus were still working on a loan with obligation as late as 31 August, per French club reporting. He had already turned down Newcastle. Moving him would unlock room on a wage bill Marseille badly need to reduce. The free agent market, which never closes. Available now Karim Benzema , 38, mutually terminated his Al-Hilal contract on 31 August after eight months and 16 games, squeezed out when the club breached the foreign-player limit. Sports Illustrated reports a European return is effectively blocked because it would void a 23m dollar-a-year Saudi Pro League ambassador deal, leaving Al-Ittihad, Al-Shabab or retirement. Paul Pogba was released by Monaco when his contract expired on 19 August. Renato Sanches had his PSG contract terminated. Also unattached: Dani Carvajal , 34, training with the Spanish federation after 451 Real Madrid appearances, David Alaba , Sergio Ramos , 40, who has still not retired, Riyad Mahrez and Raphael Guerreiro . And the smaller threads. Milan bid 20m euros for Tiago Gabriel of Lecce against a 30m valuation and were rebuffed, per a single Italian source, so treat that lightly. Celta Vigo coach Claudio Giraldez says his side still need a centre-back, which they now cannot sign until January. Hicham Boudaoui of Nice has an 8m euro proposal from Al-Ittihad, whose window is open. And Everton , having watched Balogun walk away at half past midnight, will spend four months linked with every striker in Europe. Around the Leagues Premier League Matchweek 2, 28 to 31 August Nine clubs began the season with a new manager, the most since 1946-47, and two matchweeks in the early evidence is that the reset has been kinder to some than others. Manchester City won 4-1 at Crystal Palace on Friday with two goals each from Erling Haaland and Rayan Cherki , and two assists from Phil Foden ; Palace's consolation was a Gianluigi Donnarumma own goal. Maresca praised Cherki's work off the ball, specifically for containing Adam Wharton . Cherki called his own performance so-so and said he played badly in the first half, which is not the standard reaction to a match-winning brace. Manchester United came from behind to beat Ipswich Town 5-2 at Old Trafford with a Bruno Fernandes hat-trick and a Bryan Mbeumo goal, though the second United goal was a Jacob Greaves own goal that arrived off a Harry Maguire handball and was allowed to stand under the letter of the law. Michael Carrick was determinedly unexcited afterwards: his side have not cracked it, he said, and there is a long way to go. The strangest ninety minutes were at Stamford Bridge, where Chelsea led Brighton 3-0 inside 32 minutes through Romeo Lavia , Pedro Neto and Joao Pedro , and then finished the match with 25.6 per cent possession, the lowest figure Chelsea have recorded. It ended 4-3. Joao Pedro scored and then put through his own net against his former club, Cole Palmer restored the two-goal lead and Pascal Gross scored in the sixth minute of stoppage time. Xabi Alonso said his team started playing with the result rather than continuing to play. Enzo Fernandez did not feature, for reasons that became clear two days later, and Moises Caicedo came on and lasted about eleven minutes before going off injured, with Alonso saying only that the player's feeling was not the best and scans would follow. As of this morning no result has been published. At the other end of the mood spectrum, Tottenham are bottom. Two games, two defeats, no goals scored, and a 2-0 home loss to Newcastle in which Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa both scored again, both having underperformed under Newcastle's previous management. The home crowd booed at full time. Roberto De Zerbi 's assessment was blunt: they are not a team yet. A club that spent 302m pounds this summer is entitled to expect more than that by September. Liverpool are 13th and winless after a 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest at Anfield in which the underlying numbers were alarming: 0.25 expected goals against Forest's 1.29, and no big chances created at all despite 63 per cent of the ball. Alexander Isak and Victor Munoz scored, a Florian Wirtz goal was ruled out for offside in the build-up, and Forest have now gone five without defeat against Liverpool. The season's genuine surprise sits third: Hull City , promoted through the play-offs, have won both games without conceding, the second of them 1-0 at Coventry City through a Liam Millar counter-attack on 82 minutes, on the day Coventry played their first top-flight home game in 25 years. Hull are also carrying ten injured players, the most in the division, which makes the record harder to sustain than to admire. Elsewhere, substitute Wilson Isidor won it 1-0 for Sunderland against Fulham , a stoppage-time James Tarkowski header rescued a point for Everton at Bournemouth , and Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised as Leeds United drew 1-1 with Brentford . La Liga Matchday 3, 28 to 31 August Both giants are perfect and Barcelona lead on goal difference alone. Barcelona beat Rayo Vallecano 5-2 at the Camp Nou with braces from Lamine Yamal and Raphinha , which answered a question Hansi Flick had been asked before kick-off. Yamal had gone 154 minutes without a goal after a hamstring injury ended his last club season and a World Cup that yielded one. Flick's reply was that everyone is worried about him, that he played a World Cup after an injury, and that he has had three weeks of holiday. Real Madrid beat Malaga 4-0 at the Bernabeu through Jude Bellingham , an own goal, Kylian Mbappe and a stoppage-time Arda Guler finish, with Trent Alexander-Arnold impressing from right-back in Jose Mourinho 's reshaped side. Raphinha leads the Pichichi race on five, Mbappe has four. The round's real texture was elsewhere. Racing Santander , up after 14 years, won 3-2 against Elche through a Yassir Zabiri hat-trick, their first top-flight victory since 2011-12 and the end of a 23-match winless run in the division. Deportivo La Coruna beat Valencia 3-1 at Riazor for their first top-flight win in eight years, on an afternoon when supporters' groups ended a 40-day standoff with the board by entering in orange shirts, observing complete silence for eleven minutes and erupting in blue and white at the twelfth. Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang , 37, has scored in each of his first three games since returning. And Real Betis lost 5-2 at Levante , a result that turned the Spanish press on Manuel Pellegrini with unusual force, Marca describing the defence as a complete liability ahead of a Champions League campaign. Betis host Real Madrid on Saturday. The week's best oddity came in stoppage time at Anoeta. Real Sociedad goalkeeper Alex Remiro hurt his shoulder keeping the ball in play and was treated on the pitch, which under a rule introduced at the World Cup requires the treated player to leave for a minute, and where that player is the goalkeeper requires the coach to nominate an outfield replacement or lose the captain by default. La Real did not know the procedure. Referee Orellana Cid ordered captain Igor Zubeldia off, booked him for protesting, then dismissed manager Pellegrino Matarazzo and a member of staff. Matarazzo said afterwards that he was in shock and had said nothing wrong. The federation's Competition Committee gave him a one-match touchline ban on Wednesday, so he will not be in the dugout for the advanced fixture against Celta Vigo on Thursday. Bundesliga Matchday 1, 28 to 30 August Germany started a week later than everyone else and immediately produced the weekend's best story. SV Elversberg , from a Saarland village, played the first Bundesliga match in their history and led Bayer Leverkusen 3-0 before winning 3-2. Lukas Petkov scored the club's first Bundesliga goal and took 40 per cent of the man-of-the-match vote; the assist came from Francis Onyeka , who is on loan at Elversberg from Leverkusen, and the second goal from Cole Campbell , signed from Dortmund this summer. Seven Elversberg players made their Bundesliga debut. Leverkusen's two new 30m signings had not yet arrived. There were two hat-tricks on the opening weekend. Yuito Suzuki scored three in 26 minutes as SC Freiburg beat Werder Bremen 4-1, and has already beaten his four-goal total for the whole of last season; he insisted afterwards that he simply tapped all three in and thanked the players who passed. Younes Ebnoutalib scored all three Eintracht Frankfurt goals in a 3-3 draw at Union Berlin , a striker who managed five league appearances last season after a knee injury. Bayern Munich opened their title defence by beating Stuttgart 5-1 with two Joshua Kimmich assists, and RB Leipzig won 3-0 against Borussia Monchengladbach in Martin Demichelis 's first match in charge. The disciplinary story belongs to Borussia Dortmund . Samuele Inacio came on against Hamburg and was sent off three minutes later for a studs-up challenge, then threw a bottle at the club crest on his way down the tunnel. The DFB sports court banned him for two matches on 31 August, ruling him out against Hoffenheim and Paderborn. Schalke 04 's return to the top flight after three years lasted 63 minutes before Ron Schallenberg was dismissed, and ended 3-0 to Augsburg . Separately, and handled carefully by the German press, Jamal Musiala missed Bayern's opener. He collapsed twice in pre-season and was diagnosed with absence seizures caused by a neurological dysfunction, brought on by a change in medication. He has returned to team training after that medication was adjusted, has said there is no additional health risk, and Vincent Kompany says he is reacting well and will be in a squad again with medical guidance. Serie A Matchday 2, 28 to 31 August Six clubs have six points from six and Roma lead them all on goal difference, having scored eight and conceded none. That is almost entirely one man. Donyell Malen has five goals in his first two Serie A appearances, a hat-trick against Fiorentina in which Paulo Dybala supplied three assists, then two more in a 4-0 win at Lecce on Monday. Gasperini's side have played 120 minutes of football and produced a top-of-the-table position out of them. Two results ran against the grain. Napoli lost 2-1 at home to Como , Massimiliano Allegri 's first defeat since taking the job and a tactical win for Cesc Fabregas , with a Stanislav Lobotka equaliser disallowed in the 95th minute for an offside in the build-up. And Fiorentina lost 3-0 at home to newly promoted Frosinone on the day the club celebrated its centenary, with Baggio, Batistuta and Rui Costa in the stands and the team whistled off. Fiorentina are bottom with no goals scored and seven conceded, and Fabio Grosso 's first weeks have gone about as badly as they could. Two structural stories are worth more than the scorelines. The first is that VAR has effectively disappeared from Italian football: under new designator Orsato there have been zero on-field reviews across the opening two matchdays, against four by the same stage last season, under a directive to whistle fouls rather than contacts and to use silent checks. Il Fatto Quotidiano, which has been most critical, also notes the suspension of the Open VAR transparency programme, and lists three contested non-interventions already. The second is at Inter , where Piero Ausilio left on Wednesday after 28 years, by mutual agreement, with Dario Baccin promoted to chief sport officer. Ausilio had been sporting director since 2014 and oversaw three Scudetti and three European finals; the sticking point, per Sport Mediaset's Orazio Accomando , was contract length rather than money, with Inter offering only one year beyond 2027. Ausilio said that after 28 unforgettable years the most difficult moment had arrived. Napoli, meanwhile, announced on 1 September that Scott McTominay has a mild benign arrhythmia and will undergo a corrective ablation procedure, with a return expected after the late-September international break. Ligue 1 Matchday 2, 28 to 30 August The five-time champions are twelfth. Paris Saint-Germain have two points from two matches and have twice come from two goals down to draw, first at Rennes and then at Lille , where Vitinha scored in the first minute of stoppage time and Marquinhos in the fifth. Olivier Giroud , at 39, assisted both Lille goals. The finish produced a referee row still running this week: Eric Wattelier publicly defended the added time, saying Lille's goalkeeper had stayed down, that he had booked their left-back for time-wasting and had warned both coaches to expect four minutes minimum, and dismissed the backlash as part of the football circus. The only club with two wins is Monaco , who beat Marseille 2-0 at the Stade Louis II through a brace from the young forward Paris Brunner , the individual performance of the round. Paris FC beat Nice 3-0 for Liam Rosenior 's first home league win, and Nice have still not scored a goal this season despite an almost entirely rebuilt attack including Elye Wahi on loan. At Rennes, Djibril Sidibe of promoted Le Mans came on and was sent off roughly thirty seconds later for a late challenge, in a match that lasted 106 minutes and finished 3-2 to the hosts, Esteban Lepaul scoring twice including a stoppage-time penalty. Lepaul has three goals in two games and is being talked about for a first France call-up. That call is now Zinedine Zidane 's to make: the new national coach names his first squad at 18:00 on Friday 18 September. x: One Club · Every Angle · Every Tuesday The Weekly Arsenal Digest No. 3 · Tuesday, September 1, 2026 · Deadline Day Edition · North London In This Edition The Lead · Transfer News · The Squad · Hale End · Arsenal Women · Gunners Abroad · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead Arsenal Sell the Summer and Back What They Already Have Gabriel Jesus is a Barcelona player. Gabriel Martinelli is bound for Riyadh in the biggest sale the club has ever made. Julian Alvarez is still not an Arsenal player. With hours left in the window, the champions look leaner, considerably richer, and unbeaten. T here is a version of this deadline day in which Arsenal look like a club in retreat. Two forwards gone in twenty-four hours. A first-choice target who never wanted to come. A late alternative lost to Sunderland over a few million pounds. Read the outgoing column alone and you would guess the champions were dismantling something. The table says otherwise. Arsenal have played three competitive matches since lifting the title in May. They have won all three, scored seven, and conceded none. They beat Manchester City 3-0 in Cardiff, Coventry City 3-0 at home, and Aston Villa 1-0 at Villa Park on Monday night without ever looking troubled. That is the context for everything Andrea Berta has done this summer. Arsenal did not need to buy from a position of weakness, and they have not. Bruno Guimaraes arrived from Newcastle United for £75m on August 9 . Ezri Konsa followed from Aston Villa for £55m on August 21 . Neither was a panic buy. The selling has been just as deliberate, and rather more brutal. Gabriel Jesus completed his move to Barcelona for £8.6m after four years, 123 appearances and 32 goals. He took a pay cut to go. Gabriel Martinelli is on his way to Al-Hilal for a fee that will comfortably break the club's record for a sale. Key Facts: Deadline Day Window closes: 11pm BST Tuesday, September 1, which is 3pm Pacific. The women's window runs until 11pm BST on Thursday, September 3. Confirmed today: Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona . Fabio Vieira to Hamburg . Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund on a season-long loan. Agreed, awaiting announcement: Gabriel Martinelli to Al-Hilal . Unresolved at press time: Julian Alvarez. Gone elsewhere: Malick Fofana, to Sunderland . Two departures of that size would normally be balanced by a marquee arrival. That is where the summer has stalled. Julian Alvarez has been the target since the spring, and the pursuit has never once looked comfortable. Atletico Madrid will not sell to Barcelona , the club the player actually wants. Arsenal have spent weeks trying to be a destination rather than a fallback. Sky Sports reported on Friday that Atletico had set the player a deadline to commit or engage. Chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin said publicly that Alvarez was "really struggling" and that "there were people who misled him, who left him confused." Not the language of a club expecting a clean resolution. "We have to sell what we want to sell as well, not just to sell. We have to be very careful, because some of the assets, after maybe they grow and we still want them." Mikel Arteta, August 30 Deadline Day Churn The reporting since has pulled hard in both directions, which is what deadline day does to a story. Spanish outlets suggested on Tuesday morning that Arsenal had stepped back and were assessing alternatives . Hours later, TEAMtalk and the Evening Standard were reporting the opposite: a green light at roughly £130m, a willingness to write a future Barcelona release into the contract, and help relocating the player's family. Treat that second version carefully. It is single-sourced, it is not carried by David Ornstein or Fabrizio Romano , and it arrived precisely when deadline-day traffic peaks. What is solid is Romano 's line that Barcelona now consider their incoming business closed after signing Jesus , and will not activate the €100m bid president Joan Laporta confirmed was still live. Which leaves Arteta where he has been all summer: with Kai Havertz fit and scoring, Viktor Gyokeres unused, and a squad that has not yet needed rescuing. He was blunt on Monday night. "We are trying to improve the squad, and until tomorrow night we're going to try to do that." He also warned against selling for the sake of it. The honest reading is that this window has been a success in structure and a frustration in ambition. Arsenal have upgraded midfield and defence, cleared £80m or more of wages and fees from players who were not going to start, and kept their powder dry on a striker they were never going to get cheaply. Whether that reads as discipline or as a missed opportunity depends entirely on what Havertz 's hamstrings do between now and January. Seven Scored, None Conceded, and No Saliba The champions have started their defence with their best defender in rehabilitation and a 22-year-old centre-half nobody expected to be first choice. It has not cost them a goal. William Saliba came back from the World Cup with a back problem picked up in France's semi-final. Surgery was considered and rejected in favour of a managed rehabilitation programme . He is not expected back until winter. Jurrien Timber has not played since the Champions League final and had minor groin surgery over the summer. Arteta says he is progressing well but remains weeks from full training. September or October is the realistic window. So the back line at Villa Park read Ben White , Cristhian Mosquera , Gabriel Magalhaes and Riccardo Calafiori , with David Raya behind them. Villa did not register a single shot on target all night. They are still without a goal after two matches. Mosquera is the story inside the story. Signed as depth, he has started every competitive match and handled Nicolas Jackson and Emiliano Buendia without fuss on Monday. He came off on 79 minutes holding the back of his leg, which is how Konsa got his debut against his old club. Arteta said afterwards: "He is fine. But he was feeling like he was about to have something. He could not continue." Transfer News Martinelli to Al-Hilal: the Biggest Sale in Arsenal's History Seven seasons, 278 appearances, 62 goals, and a fee that pushes past Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain's 2017 departure. Gabriel Martinelli has been left out of Arsenal matchday squads since the season began, which is usually its own kind of announcement. He is 25. He arrived as a teenager from Ituano and leaves as a Premier League champion. The fee has climbed as the week has gone on. Daily Cannon reported a verbally agreed £56.5m on Saturday. By Sunday, David Ornstein was reporting a €70m fixed fee , up from an earlier structure of €58m plus €8m in add-ons. James Benge reported that the two clubs had been working through a sell-on clause. At any of those numbers it is a club record for an outgoing transfer, comfortably clear of the £40m Liverpool paid for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain nine years ago. Fabrizio Romano reported that Arsenal granted authorisation for the player to travel. Announcement is expected before the window shuts. Certainty tier: fee agreed and personal terms done, awaiting official confirmation. Reported by Ornstein and Romano independently, which is about as firm as it gets without a club statement. Gabriel Jesus Joins Barcelona, and Takes a Pay Cut to Do It A four-year Arsenal career that never quite recovered from a knee injury ends for £8.6m and a three-year deal in Catalonia. Gabriel Jesus arrived from Manchester City in 2022 for £45m and changed the mood around the club almost immediately. He leaves having started three Premier League matches last season, his campaign wrecked by the knee injury he suffered in the FA Cup in January 2025. Barcelona paid €10m, around £8.6m, on a contract running to June 2029. Jesus has since confirmed he reduced his salary to make the move happen. He consulted Raphinha , Joao Cancelo , Rodri and Eric Garcia before deciding. "I have the opportunity now to be here at Barca," he said on arrival. "It's a dream for me." He finishes with 123 appearances and 32 goals for Arsenal , plus a title medal he did much of the early work for. There is a strategic footnote. Romano reported that signing Jesus is what closed Barcelona 's incoming market and killed any late move for Alvarez . In selling a squad striker cheaply, Arsenal may have removed their own competition for a better one. Certainty tier: official. Announced by both clubs on September 1. Fofana Slips Away on a Question of Structure Personal terms agreed, structure not. Sunderland moved, Crystal Palace counter-moved, and the Belgian ended up doing his medical in France without knowing who for. Arsenal 's late look at Malick Fofana was first reported on Sunday night by the Evening Standard's Matt Verri . The 21-year-old Lyon winger fits an obvious hole: pace and directness from the left, which the champions have lacked since Martinelli stopped playing. According to Ornstein , Arsenal got as far as agreeing personal terms before refusing to meet Lyon 's €40m valuation. Romano added the detail that mattered: Arsenal only ever wanted a loan or a loan with an obligation, not a permanent purchase at that price. Sunderland had no such reservations and agreed roughly €30m plus add-ons, with a five-year contract to 2031. Crystal Palace then matched the package and tried to win the player on personal terms. What followed was the most deadline-day scene of the day. Two private jets waited at Lyon airport, one bound for the north east and one for London. French journalist Romain Molina reported that Fofana completed his medical in France while still deciding where he was going. He went to Sunderland . Certainty tier: dead for Arsenal . Confirmed independently by Ornstein and Romano . Nwaneri Goes to Dortmund, and the Reason Is Eze A season-long loan with a recall option for the 19-year-old, after a Marseille spell that fell apart through no fault of his own. Ethan Nwaneri flew to Germany on Tuesday morning and completed a season-long loan to Borussia Dortmund . He remains under contract at Arsenal until 2030, and the deal carries a recall option. The reasoning is straightforward and slightly sad. The arrival of Eberechi Eze pushed him down a pecking order that already contained Bukayo Saka , Martin Odegaard and Mikel Merino . Club and player agreed he needed regular football. His January loan to Marseille was undone almost immediately when Roberto De Zerbi was dismissed shortly after he arrived. Dortmund is a better bet: they have an excellent record with young attackers, and they moved after losing Giannis Konstantelias to an ACL injury. A neat detail: Nwaneri scored against Dortmund in Arsenal 's 3-2 pre-season defeat, which is reported to have sharpened their interest. Certainty tier: official. The Summer Ledger Confirmed and agreed fees reported in pounds. Red is money out of the door, navy is money coming back in. The striker has been talked about as a makeweight in an Alvarez deal. He denied any unhappiness in July: "I feel extremely comfortable at Arsenal." Single-sourced rumour. Bartishvili, pre-agreed for 2027 Arsenal have agreed terms to sign Georgian attacking midfielder Andria Bartishvili from Kolkheti 1913 when he turns 18 in March 2027. The player has publicly thanked supporters for the reaction. Agreement reported, not yet a registrable transfer. The bookmakers' list Several outlets ran deadline-day pieces listing Marcus Rashford , Adam Wharton and Eli Junior Kroupi as Arsenal possibilities. Those lists are built from betting odds, not reporting, and none of the three has been linked by a credible Arsenal source. Treat as noise. The Squad Arteta Has Found a Midfield Two, and One Half of It Is a Left-Back Myles Lewis-Skelly started alongside Declan Rice at Villa Park. A £75m midfielder watched from the bench until the 71st minute. The XI at Villa Park was Raya ; White , Mosquera , Gabriel , Calafiori ; Rice , Lewis-Skelly , Odegaard ; Saka , Havertz , Tzolis . A 4-2-3-1 in name, closer to a 4-3-3 in practice. The interesting selection is Lewis-Skelly . He came through as a midfielder, was converted to left-back out of necessity, and is now being converted back. He was excellent on Monday, progressing the ball cleanly and giving Rice licence to push. That has an immediate consequence for Bruno Guimaraes . Signed for £75m three weeks ago, he picked up a thigh problem in the Community Shield, missed the opener, and got 19 minutes at Villa Park. Reviewers liked what they saw: a different passing register, more forward risk. He is being eased in rather than built around. Christos Tzolis is having the harder introduction. Excellent against Coventry , where he was involved in the first two goals, he was withdrawn at half-time at Villa Park after a poor 45 minutes. The Premier League's physicality is the standard first hurdle for a Belgian league arrival. Nobody at the club will be worried yet. Eberechi Eze replaced him and changed the game. He was the link in the winning goal, receiving from Mosquera and finding Calafiori , whose low cross Saka turned in on 59 minutes. That is Calafiori 's second assist in consecutive matches, and he is quietly the most productive left-sided player at the club right now. The Number Nine Question The number nine question has an answer, at least for now. Havertz starts. Gyokeres , who scored 21 goals in 56 appearances last season, has played 15 minutes all campaign and was an unused substitute in both league games. Arteta put it carefully on Tuesday: "Sometimes you have certain issues with players physically that you have to make changes, and I'm sure there are going to be minutes for everybody." Scorers So Far, All Competitions Kai Havertz 2 (Community Shield, Coventry) Bukayo Saka 2 (Coventry, Aston Villa) Martin Odegaard 2 (Community Shield, Coventry) Riccardo Calafiori 1 (Community Shield, after 24 seconds) Odegaard is the other quiet subplot. Arteta was pointed about him last week: "He's fit and available, I think that's the baseline. Last season he had too many incidents where it didn't allow him to have any consistency." Two goals in three games is a start. He was withdrawn on 71 minutes at Villa Park, which reads as management rather than concern. One theme worth watching all season is squad size. Arteta renewed his campaign against the 20-outfield-player matchday limit last week: "That's what I've been begging the Premier League. Every squad needs more than 20 outfield players, ideally, to sustain the level of demands, games, international games that we have." With eight Champions League league-phase fixtures plus two domestic cups, he will make that argument again. Injuries & Availability William Saliba (back). Injured on World Cup duty with France. Surgery declined in favour of rehabilitation. Expected back in winter. Jurrien Timber (groin). Minor summer surgery. Has not played since the Champions League final. Targeting September or October. Cristhian Mosquera (precautionary). Withdrawn on 79 minutes at Villa Park. Arteta expects him available for Chelsea . Bruno Guimaraes (thigh, resolved). Missed the opener, returned as a substitute on Monday. Full round-up here . Hale End A Restocked Academy, a New Interim Coach, and Two Red Cards Six recruits in a fortnight, a debut goal at Brighton, and an under-18 side that has not won a game yet. The academy recruitment department has had the busiest week of anyone at the club. James Scanlon , a 19-year-old winger with 24 caps for Gibraltar , arrived from Manchester United . So did Habeeb Ogunneye , a 20-year-old right-back who spent last season on loan at Newport County , taking squad number 62. They were joined by Axel Donczew , a 16-year-old Welsh winger from Cardiff City who signed scholarship terms and turns professional in February 2027, and Igor Tyjon , an 18-year-old striker from Blackburn Rovers with three senior appearances, wearing 64. Both new arrivals went straight in at Brighton on Monday and both looked the part. Scanlon scored on debut after 24 minutes, set up by Ife Ibrahim . Ogunneye started at right-back. Marli Salmon , who signed his first professional contract on turning 17 last week, captained the side. Brighton led 2-1 through Younes Ibrahim and Bailey Palmer before Evan Mooney equalised in the 88th minute. That is two points from two Premier League 2 games, after a 1-1 draw with Crystal Palace . The EFL Trophy has been less kind: a 5-1 defeat at Barnet on August 18. The Under-18s The under-18s are struggling more seriously. They lost 2-1 at Brighton on August 29 with nine men. Emerson Nwaneri , younger brother of Ethan, was sent off for a second bookable offence in the first half. Goalkeeper Jack Talbot followed late on. Abraham Owusu-Gyasi had put the ten men ahead on 61 minutes before Daniel Rudin equalised three minutes later and Raffaele Oppong won it on 84. That leaves the under-18s with one point from three league games and no win in four in all competitions. Josh Smith has been promoted from assistant to interim head coach. Out on Loan On the loan front, Ismeal Kabia has settled fast at St Mirren , debuting the day after his August 17 move and playing 59 minutes in a 5-1 defeat to Rangers . Four academy players trained with the first team before the Villa game: Josh Ogunnaike , Ceadach O'Neill , Archie Stevens and Theo Julienne . Arsenal Women Slegers Rebuilds Around Stanway, and Finally Buys a Centre-Half Seven in, ten out, a new build-up structure, and Elisa de Almeida arriving from PSG days before the champions open at Brighton. This has been the most aggressive summer Arsenal 's women's team has had in years, and it needed to be. Renee Slegers won the WSL last season with 51 points from 22 games, lost one match all campaign, and won the inaugural FIFA Women's Champions Cup by beating Corinthians 3-2 in February. Then she lost half her spine. The Turnover Beth Mead left for Manchester City after nine years. Katie McCabe went to Chelsea , Victoria Pelova to Tottenham , Laia Codina to West Ham , Manuela Zinsberger to Borussia Dortmund . Jenna Nighswonger , Rosa Kafaji , Laila Harbert and Vivienne Lia also went. In came Georgia Stanway from Bayern Munich , Ona Batlle from Barcelona , Misa Rodriguez from Real Madrid , Geraldine Reuteler from Eintracht Frankfurt , Selina Cerci from Hoffenheim , Lisa Baum from RB Leipzig and Isabella Damm from Brondby . Kim Little , Steph Catley , Leah Williamson and Caitlin Foord all extended. The Signing One hole stayed open all summer, and it is being filled this week. BBC Sport's Emma Sanders reported on Tuesday that Arsenal have agreed a deal for Elisa de Almeida , the 28-year-old France defender, from Paris Saint-Germain for around £550,000 . Arseblog News sources say it is in the final stages. She would be the first centre-half Arsenal have signed since Codina in 2023, and she is needed. Katie Reid is recovering from an ACL injury, and in the Charlton friendly Slegers was reduced to playing midfielder Smilla Holmberg at centre-back. The women's window stays open until 11pm BST on Thursday. Pre-season Form Pre-season suggested the rebuild is coming together. Arsenal beat Paris FC 1-0 on August 23 through an Olivia Smith goal in the 91st minute, then beat Charlton Athletic 5-1 on August 26. Stanway scored her first Arsenal goal, with Mariona Caldentey from the penalty spot, Kyra Cooney-Cross , Smith and Frida Maanum adding the rest. Cooney-Cross ' goal was the one that mattered. The Australian returned to competitive football after five months away on compassionate leave following her mother's terminal cancer diagnosis, and marked it with a long-range strike. Slegers called her "amazing" since coming back. How They Will Play Tactically, the interesting change is Stanway 's role. She is dropping between the centre-backs in build-up with Kim Little ahead of her as a shield, a 3-1-6 shape that takes progression duties off Little and Mariona and adds a genuine long diagonal passer. Arsenal are also shooting from range far more often, a direct response to their trouble breaking low blocks. "We had more shots and more end product," Slegers said. "That is something we spoke about." The other pattern to watch is the rotation between Holmberg and Baum , both 19, on the right: one holds the touchline while the other inverts as a right-sided ten. Individual honours arrived last week too. Alessia Russo , Emily Fox and Mariona Caldentey were all named in the PFA WSL Team of the Year, and Olivia Smith won the PFA Women's Young Player of the Year award for a second consecutive season. Russo scored 24 goals in all competitions last term. Gunners Abroad A Rare Week With Nobody Away, and a Diaspora That Keeps Growing The post-World Cup calendar pushed the first international window to late September. In the meantime, the list of Arsenal players plying their trade elsewhere has grown by five in a fortnight. There is no international football this week and none next. Because the World Cup ran into July, UEFA pushed the opening Nations League league-phase window into the second half of September. The headline fixture of that window is England against Spain at Wembley on September 26, a game likely to feature Arsenal players on both sides. So this section belongs to the departed and the loaned. Ethan Nwaneri is now a Borussia Dortmund player for the season, and will be in Germany when Arsenal host his loan club in the Champions League on November 24. He remains recallable. Ismeal Kabia is the only other current Arsenal player out on loan in the men's game. He has played once for St Mirren , 59 minutes in a heavy defeat at Rangers , which is exactly the sort of chastening Scottish Premiership afternoon a loan is for. Among the recently departed, Jakub Kiwior is at Porto , Leandro Trossard at Besiktas , Karl Hein at Werder Bremen , Fabio Vieira now at Hamburg , Gabriel Jesus at Barcelona and Gabriel Martinelli heading to Al-Hilal . That is a lot of recent Arsenal football scattered across Europe and the Gulf. On the women's side, Sophie Harwood is at Sheffield United and Jessie Gale at Newcastle United for the season, with Cecily Wellesley-Smith at FC Rosengard in Sweden until December. Chief executive Richard Garlick tied it to the title win. Fabio Vieira joins Hamburg. The Portuguese midfielder completed a permanent move for a reported €9m to €10m on deadline day, four years after arriving from Porto . Reiss Nelson's 19 years end. The 26-year-old winger had his contract terminated by mutual consent on August 27, closing an association with the club that began in the academy. Coventry could not lay a glove on them. In Arsenal 's 3-0 opening-day win, Frank Lampard 's side did not make a single tackle in the first half and registered their first on 69 minutes, a rarity in Opta's records since 2007. Konsa's homecoming. The £55m defender made his Arsenal debut at Villa Park against the club he left ten days earlier, coming on for the injured Mosquera on 79 minutes. A penalty given, then taken away. VAR overturned a second-half penalty at Villa Park after determining Ian Maatsen 's contact on Saka occurred outside the area. Arsenal scored three minutes later anyway. The Champions League draw is done. Made on August 27, it gave Arsenal Real Madrid , Borussia Dortmund , Lille and Sabah at home, and Bayern Munich , Napoli , Real Betis and Slavia Praha away. k: Six days from the September 1 deadline, a World Cup summer has pushed Europe's most expensive week into the middle of the season.
x: The Weekly Soccer Digest World football, reported and weighed Edition No. 1 · Wednesday, August 26, 2026 Deadline week In this edition The Lead · Transfer News · The Rumour Mill · Around the Leagues · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead Six days left, and the money has not stopped moving The summer window shuts on Tuesday. A World Cup pushed every European calendar back, so for the first time in years the most expensive week of the football year is being played out with the league tables already on the wall. T he transfer window closes on Tuesday, September 1, at 23:00 in England and just before midnight on the continent. Major League Soccer follows a day later, on September 2. That is the ordinary rhythm of a European summer. What is not ordinary is where the season sits when the whistle goes on it. The World Cup finished on July 19 at MetLife Stadium, where Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time through Ferran Torres in the 106th minute, with Enzo Fernandez and Leandro Paredes both sent off. Every domestic calendar in Europe slid back to accommodate it. The Premier League did not start until August 22. The Bundesliga has not started at all: matchday one is Friday. So clubs are now conducting the single most consequential week of their financial year with points already on the board and, in several cases, with a crisis already in the building. The Deadline Board Ten deals that could still land before Tuesday, and how far each has actually travelled. Omar Marmoush Man City to Tottenham Medical Liam Delap Chelsea to Nottingham Forest Medical El Hadji Malick Diouf West Ham to Brentford Medical Bradley Barcola PSG to Liverpool Advanced talks Nicolas Jackson Chelsea to Aston Villa Advanced talks Moise Kean Fiorentina to Como Terms agreed, fee open Ollie Watkins Aston Villa to Al-Hilal Four bids rejected Rafael Leao Milan to Aston Villa Talks, no fee agreed Enzo Fernandez Chelsea to Man City No formal bid yet Julian Alvarez Atletico Madrid, exit sought Club refusing to sell Status as reported on the morning of August 26. Sourcing for each item appears in the write-ups below. One morning, one teenager Consider Wednesday morning as a single data point. Manchester City confirmed the signing of Ayyoub Bouaddi , 18, from Lille . Sky Sports reported the structure as £81.3m guaranteed with £4.3m in add-ons, a total of roughly £86m; Lille announced it in euros at £100m equivalent, or a shade under. Whichever currency you prefer, it is the most expensive teenager in Premier League history, comfortably past the £58.9m Manchester United paid for Leny Yoro in 2024. Lille, for their part, called it the largest sale a Ligue 1 club has ever made to a foreign buyer, beating the €80m Nicolas Pepe fetched in 2018. Bouaddi is worth pausing on. He made his European debut at 16 years and three days, a competition record, and became the youngest player of the century in Ligue 1 at 16 years and 20 days. He had 96 senior appearances for Lille before his 19th birthday and started five of Morocco's six matches at the World Cup. In his farewell message he wrote that Lille is “where I grew up, where I learned, and where I experienced my first emotions at the highest level.” City are buying a succession plan, not a squad player. They need one. This is the first City summer without Pep Guardiola , who was replaced on June 29 by Enzo Maresca on a three-year deal. Since then City have sold Rodri to Barcelona for €76.5m, Tijjani Reijnders to Al-Qadsiah , Savio to Tottenham for £85m and let Bernardo Silva and John Stones go for nothing. Marmoush is at a medical at Spurs, Nico Gonzalez is expected at Newcastle , and Jack Grealish is still unresolved. Money in the other direction has gone on youth: £116m to Nottingham Forest for Elliot Anderson , now £86m to Lille for a teenager. Maresca was asked on Sunday whether more was coming. “We will see, it's eight days to go,” he said. “For sure something is going to happen.” “I would give that an 85 to 90 per cent chance. I think that's gonna happen. I don't think Liverpool would've come this far to walk away from it.” David Ornstein on Bradley Barcola, The Athletic FC Podcast, August 25 Selling as a strategy The second thing this window has confirmed is that selling well is now a strategy rather than an admission of defeat. Chelsea are the purest expression of it. On Tuesday they agreed to send Liam Delap to Nottingham Forest for £45m rising to £50m, a Forest club record, with the medical set for Wednesday. Delap scored three goals in 47 Chelsea appearances. Chelsea paid Ipswich Town £30m for him a year ago. That is a profit of roughly £20m on a player who did not work out, and it is not an accident. In the same seven days Chelsea loaned Benoit Badiashile to Napoli with a purchase option, sold Omari Kellyman to Strasbourg for around €6m, and moved close to selling Nicolas Jackson to Aston Villa . Santi Aouna of Foot Mercato reported on Wednesday that the clubs are near an agreement but that Jackson has not yet approved it. Meanwhile Chelsea are the ones saying no: Manchester City want Enzo Fernandez , valued at roughly £120m, and as of Tuesday had not submitted a formal offer. Xabi Alonso , four days into his Chelsea tenure, was careful about it. “My wish is that we know what will happen for the future,” he said, “but we will see this week.” Newcastle have run the same play at a larger scale, banking more than £240m in sales including Sandro Tonali to Tottenham and Anthony Gordon to Barcelona for £69.3m, then spending it across five signings. Tottenham have gone past £300m under Roberto De Zerbi . And on the opening Saturday Tottenham lost 3-0 at Brentford , their joint-heaviest opening-day defeat in Premier League history, conceding 5.63 expected goals. De Zerbi did not hide behind the scoreline. “Our physical condition was not at the right level for all players,” he said, “because many came later after the World Cup.” Spending is not the same as a team, and this summer has left almost nobody time to build one. There is a counterweight, and it is Italy. Juventus lost Dusan Vlahovic for nothing this month when his contract expired and he signed for Besiktas . Asked about the market after his side's opening win at Frosinone , Luciano Spalletti shrugged: “potremmo anche rimanere cosi,” we could even stay as we are. He also conceded that without Champions League football, everyone is available. Calcio e Finanza marked the season's start with a blunt accounting: Serie A's domestic television deal is worth about €900m a season against a €1.2bn target, and of the dozen or so clubs on earth who can spend €100m on a single player, not one of them is Italian. The players stop waiting Which brings us to the third and least comfortable feature of the week: the players have stopped waiting politely. Moise Kean arrived late at Fiorentina's training ground on Wednesday, refused to train with the squad and was fined. Julian Alvarez did not turn up to Atletico Madrid training at all, the club citing indisposition, three days after being whistled by his own supporters. Rafael Leao is training away from the Milan group despite being fit. Ousmane Dembele has been given a week off by PSG that RMC's Daniel Riolo flatly called a punishment. Ollie Watkins has turned down a new Villa contract and made clear he would take the Saudi offer. Five clubs, five different countries, one common cause: a window this short, arriving this late, hands leverage to whoever is willing to make a scene. Six days remain. The tell to watch is not the biggest name but the first domino: if Chelsea blink on Enzo Fernandez, City will have spent north of £200m in a fortnight and Chelsea will have another nine-figure sum to reinvest in January. If they hold, this becomes a window remembered for teenagers rather than superstars. Either way, Tuesday night will be busy. Signed and Sealed The five biggest fees officially confirmed between August 19 and August 26, in millions of pounds. Ayyoub Bouaddi Lille to Man City 86 Savio Man City to Tottenham 85 Carlos Baleba Brighton to Man Utd 70 Liam Delap Chelsea to Nottingham Forest 50 Curtis Jones Liverpool to Inter 30 Guaranteed fees as reported, rounded, add-ons excluded except where a maximum has been agreed. Delap is £45m rising to £50m. Bouaddi's total includes £4.3m of add-ons on an £81.3m base. Secondary Feature Nine new managers, and a record that had stood for eighty years Almost half the Premier League changed its head coach this summer. Opta had to go back to 1946 to find anything comparable. Nine of the twenty Premier League clubs began the season with a manager taking charge of his first league game for them. Opta's line, carried by Sky Sports, is that this is the most in an English top-flight season since 1946-47. Serie A very nearly matched it: nine of that league's twenty benches also changed hands, four of them going to men who had never managed in Italy before. The English list reads like a reshuffle of the entire coaching class. Enzo Maresca left Chelsea for Manchester City to replace Pep Guardiola . Xabi Alonso took the Chelsea job Maresca vacated. Andoni Iraola left Bournemouth for Liverpool in succession to Arne Slot , and Marco Rose took the Bournemouth job. Matthias Jaissle replaced Eddie Howe at Newcastle on August 5, the latest appointment of the nine. Oliver Glasner moved from Crystal Palace to Nottingham Forest , with Pierre Sage taking over at Selhurst Park. Alvaro Arbeloa has Fulham after Marco Silva 's departure on June 2, and Gary O'Neil has promoted Ipswich Town . Opening weekend split them neatly. Off the pitch Off the pitch, two structural stories. First, Profit and Sustainability Rules are gone. From this season clubs are governed by a Squad Cost Ratio capping on-pitch spending, wages, head-coach salary, agent fees and transfer amortisation, at 85 per cent of football revenue, with a Red Threshold at 115 per cent. Breaches between the two trigger financial levies; above the Red Threshold the penalty is a six-point deduction rising by a point for every £6.5m of overspend. A separate Sustainability and Systemic Resilience regime adds working capital, liquidity and positive equity tests. Second, Liverpool 's owners FSG sold a minority stake in mid-August to a consortium led by Amit Bhatia and including Jeff Bezos , reported at around 38 per cent on a valuation near $7bn with an option to take control at roughly $8bn within twelve months. FSG's statement was categorical: it “continues to retain majority ownership and operational control.” Sky reported the investment brings no separate transfer budget. Also of note: the Women's Super League expands from 12 clubs to 14 this season, starting September 4, with Sky showing 163 matches live. x: The Weekly Arsenal Digest North London · Est. 1886 · Free of Social Media The Weekly Arsenal Digest Everything Arsenal, Every Tuesday No. 2 · Edition of Tuesday, August 25, 2026 · Champions of England In This Edition The Lead Transfer News The Squad Hale End Arsenal Women Gunners Abroad Numbers of the Week In Brief What to Watch The Lead Six Days to Remake a Forward Line Arsenal have won their first two matches of the title defence by an aggregate of 6-0 and have not conceded a goal. Underneath that placid surface, the champions are dismantling and rebuilding their attack with less than a week of the window left, and the outcome rests on two men who have not yet decided anything. T here is a particular kind of quiet that settles over a club that has just won the league. Arsenal have spent this month enjoying it. They beat Manchester City 3-0 in the Community Shield at the Principality Stadium on August 16, a match settled inside 24 seconds by Riccardo Calafiori and finished off by Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard . Five days later they opened the Premier League season at the Emirates by beating newly promoted Coventry City 3-0 on a Friday night, and the visitors did not register a single tackle in the first half. Two matches, six goals, none conceded, and a manager who described the evening as having "a lot to like" about it. And yet the most consequential Arsenal story of the past seven days did not happen on a pitch. It happened on the phone lines between north London, Riyadh and Madrid, and it concerns the shape of the attack that Mikel Arteta will take into a Champions League campaign that begins in a fortnight. The Premier League window closes at 11pm UK time on Tuesday, September 1, which is 3pm Pacific. That leaves six days for a set of decisions that will define the season more than any of the five signings already made. The Two Undecided Men The first is Gabriel Martinelli . David Ornstein of The Athletic reported on August 23 that Arsenal have placed a valuation of around 70 million euros, roughly 60 million pounds, on the Brazilian, and that the player is open to a move to the Middle East. Al Hilal have been circling for a fortnight. Sky Sports reported on Monday that the two clubs are closing on an agreement, with a sell-on clause understood to be part of the structure, and that the decision now belongs to the player himself. Martinelli turned down an approach from Galatasaray last week. He has been left out of both matchday squads so far this season. Whichever figure the deal eventually lands on, it will comfortably break Arsenal's record for a player sale. The second is the man Arsenal would like to sign with the proceeds, and here the picture is genuinely unresolved. Fabrizio Romano said on Tuesday that Arsenal remain attentive to Julian Alvarez , that the club has an internal feeling it could reach agreement with Atletico Madrid on the financial terms, and that Arsenal will not lodge a formal bid until the striker signals he actually wants to come. That last clause is the whole story. Alvarez has made no secret of preferring Barcelona , a move Spanish reporting describes as financially close to fiction, and the Argentine press is split on whether Atletico are desperate to sell or determined to keep him and rehabilitate him in front of a crowd that whistled him. Arsenal are not, on the current evidence, prepared to spend anything close to 150 million on a player who regards them as a fallback. This is a more disciplined position than Arsenal have historically taken in the last week of a window, and it is worth pausing on. Andrea Berta , in his second summer as sporting director, has run a window of unusual decisiveness. Piero Hincapie made permanent from Bayer Leverkusen for a reported 34.5 million in June, Illan Meslier taken on a free from Leeds United in July, Christos Tzolis bought from Club Brugge for a reported 34 million as the designated replacement for Leandro Trossard , Bruno Guimaraes prised out of Newcastle United for a reported 75 million, and then Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa on the eve of the season for 51 million plus 4 million in add-ons. That is roughly 198.5 million pounds of gross spending before deadline week has even started. "He's done enough with this squad to be treated with a little bit more respect than he's being treated with at the moment." Ian Wright, on Gabriel Martinelli What the Money Has Not Settled What that spending has not yet bought is a resolution to the question Arsenal have been circling for two years. Havertz started the opener and scored, having also scored in Cardiff, which left Viktor Gyokeres on the bench and unused. The Swede scored 14 Premier League goals and 21 in all competitions in his first season, numbers that would flatter most centre-forwards and which somehow still left the debate open. Arteta's public position is that the two are complementary rather than competing. His team sheets over the past ten days suggest something slightly firmer than that. Meanwhile the club is quietly working the other end of the ledger. Ethan Nwaneri , back from a difficult half-season on loan at Marseille , is the subject of loan interest from Newcastle United and others, with Arsenal understood to prefer a temporary move to a sale. Gabriel Jesus has one year left and has been linked with a Premier League exit. Fabio Vieira , Reiss Nelson and Kepa Arrizabalaga are all names the club would move on if the right offer arrives. There is more traffic to come through the gates at London Colney in the next six days than there has been all summer. The context that makes it urgent is Europe. Arsenal lost the Champions League final in Budapest on May 30, drawing 1-1 with Paris Saint-Germain after Havertz had scored inside six minutes, and going out 4-3 on penalties after Eberechi Eze missed and David Raya saved from Nuno Mendes . Arsenal had four shots that night to PSG's eighteen. That is the reason a club that has just won its first title in 22 years spent the summer buying a 75 million midfielder and a 55 million centre-back rather than resting on it. The league is being defended. Europe is being attacked. Both plans need a front line that is finished, and as of Tuesday lunchtime, it is not.
